title.zh: 卷九 魏書九 諸夏侯曹傳
title.en: Volume 9: Book of Wei 9: Biographies of the Xiahous and Caos
title.raw: 卷九 魏書九 諸夏侯曹傳 Volume 9: Book of Wei 9: Biographies of the Xiahous and Caos

sentences.zh: 夏侯惇

translations.literal: Xiahou Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Dun.

sentences.zh: 夏侯惇字元讓，沛國譙人，夏侯嬰之後也。

translations.literal: Xiahou Dun, courtesy name Yuanrang, was a man of Qiao in the state of Pei, and a descendant of Xiahou Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Dun, styled Yuanrang, came from Qiao in Pei commandery. He traced his line back to Xiahou Ying.

sentences.zh: 年十四，就師學，人有辱其師者，惇殺之，由是以烈氣聞。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he went to a teacher to study; when someone insulted his teacher, Dun killed him, and on this account he became known for fierce spirit.
translations.idiomatic: When he was fourteen he took a tutor; a man who humiliated that tutor was slain by Dun, and word of his fierce temper spread from that moment.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起，惇常爲裨將，從征伐。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor first rose, Dun often served as a deputy general and followed on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the earliest days of Cao Cao’s rise, Dun repeatedly served as a deputy commander and rode with him on every expedition.

sentences.zh: 太祖行奮武將軍，以惇爲司馬，别屯白馬，遷折衝校尉，領東郡太守。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor acted as General Who Inspires Martial Might, he appointed Dun marshal of the army, separately encamped at Baima, promoted him to colonel who smashes the charge, and had him concurrently administer the grand administrator of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao held the acting title General Who Inspires Martial Might, he named Dun his chief of staff, detached him to hold Baima, advanced him to colonel of the shock corps, and added the post of governor of Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖征陶謙，留惇守濮陽。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Tao Qian, he left Dun to guard Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched against Tao Qian, he left Dun behind to defend Puyang.

sentences.zh: 張邈叛，迎吕布，太祖家在鄄城，惇輕車往赴，適與布會，交戰。

translations.literal: Zhang Miao rebelled and welcomed Lü Bu; the Grand Progenitor’s family was at Juancheng, and Dun went in light chariots to hurry there, happened to meet Bu, and they fought.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao turned traitor and ushered in Lü Bu. Cao Cao’s household was still at Juancheng; Dun raced there with a light escort, ran straight into Lü Bu’s host, and joined battle.

sentences.zh: 布退還，遂入濮陽，襲得惇軍輜重。

translations.literal: Bu withdrew and returned, then entered Puyang and by surprise seized the baggage train of Dun’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fell back, then doubled into Puyang and overran Dun’s baggage column before anyone could react.

sentences.zh: 遣將僞降，共執持惇，責以寶貨，惇軍中震恐。

translations.literal: He sent a general feigning surrender; together they seized and held Dun and demanded valuables of him; Dun’s army was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a subordinate under false colors of surrender; the man seized Dun as a hostage and demanded ransom. Panic rippled through Dun’s camp.

sentences.zh: 惇將韓浩乃勒兵屯惇營門，召軍吏諸將，皆案甲當部不得動，諸營乃定。

translations.literal: Dun’s officer Han Hao then deployed troops and encamped at the gate of Dun’s camp, summoned the clerks and generals of the army, all kept armor in place by their units and were not allowed to move, and the various camps then stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hao, one of Dun’s commanders, drew up his men at the camp gate, called in every staff officer and captain, ordered each unit to stand fast in full kit, and so steadied the whole encampment.

sentences.zh: 遂詣惇所，叱持質者曰：「汝等凶逆，乃敢執劫大將軍，復欲望生邪！

translations.literal: He then went to Dun’s place and shouted at those holding the hostage: “You are violent rebels; you dare seize and coerce the grand general, and still hope to live!
translations.idiomatic: He strode to Dun’s position and roared at the kidnappers: “You are traitors who dare bind a commander-in-chief and still expect to walk away alive?

sentences.zh: 且吾受命討賊，寧能以一將軍之故，而縱汝乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover I have received orders to punish rebels; how could I, for the sake of one general, let you go?”
translations.idiomatic: I carry orders to extirpate rebels. Am I to spare you for the life of a single general?”

sentences.zh: 因涕泣謂惇曰：「當奈國法何！」

translations.literal: Thereupon weeping he said to Dun: “What can be done about the laws of the state!”
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he told Dun, “The law of the realm leaves me no choice.”

sentences.zh: 促召兵擊持質者。

translations.literal: He urged calling troops to strike those holding the hostage.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the assault troops forward against the hostage-takers.

sentences.zh: 持質者惶遽叩头，言「我但欲乞資用去耳！」

translations.literal: Those holding the hostage were frightened and kowtowed, saying “We only wished to beg supplies and depart!”
translations.idiomatic: The kidnappers panicked, beat their heads on the ground, and cried, “We only wanted money to get away!”

sentences.zh: 浩數責，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Hao repeatedly rebuked them and all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hao berated them again and again, then had every one of them executed.

sentences.zh: 惇既免，太祖聞之，謂浩曰：「卿此可爲萬世法。」

translations.literal: When Dun had been freed, the Grand Progenitor heard of it and said to Hao: “What you did may serve as a model for ten thousand generations.”
translations.idiomatic: After Dun was freed, Cao Cao heard the story and told Han Hao, “What you did should be the precedent for all time.”

sentences.zh: 乃著令，自今已後有持質者，皆當并擊，勿顧質。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an order: from now on whenever there are those who take hostages, all should be struck down together; do not spare the hostage.
translations.idiomatic: He then promulgated a rule: from that day forward, anyone who seized a hostage was to be cut down together with the victim—no one was to spare the captive for fear of the bandits.

sentences.zh: 由是劫質者遂絕。

translations.literal: On this account those who seized hostages then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After that, hostage-taking in his armies all but disappeared.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：案《光武紀》，建武九年，盜劫陰貴人母弟，吏以不得拘質迫盜，盜遂殺之也。

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng says: According to the Annals of Emperor Guangwu, in the ninth year of Jianwu bandits seized the mother and younger brother of the honored consort Yin; the clerks, because they could not seize the hostage to press the bandits, the bandits then killed them.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sun Sheng remarks: The Guangwu Annals record that in Jianwu 9 robbers kidnapped the mother and younger brother of Honored Lady Yin; officials, forbidden to storm the hostage to corner the outlaws, watched helplessly as the bandits murdered them.

sentences.zh: 然則合擊者，乃古制也。

translations.literal: Then those who strike together are an ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: So the policy of striking hostage-takers without mercy was already an old precedent.

sentences.zh: 自安、順已降，政教陵遲，劫質不避王公，而有司莫能遵奉國憲者，浩始復斬之，故魏武嘉焉。〉

translations.literal: From the An and Shun reigns downward, government and instruction declined; seizing hostages did not avoid even kings and dukes, yet those in charge were unable to uphold the statutes of the state; only when Hao again beheaded them did Wei Wu commend it.〉
translations.idiomatic: After the An and Shun emperors, government grew slack and kidnappers no longer spared even princes of the blood, while magistrates shrank from enforcing the code. Han Hao was the first in ages to cut them down without negotiation, which is why Cao Cao praised him so warmly.〉

sentences.zh: 太祖自徐州還，惇從征吕布，爲流矢所中，傷左目。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor returned from Xu province, Dun followed in campaigning against Lü Bu, was struck by a stray arrow, and wounded in the left eye.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao withdrew from Xu province, Dun joined the campaign against Lü Bu, took a stray arrow in the left eye, and was badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：時夏侯淵與惇俱爲將軍，軍中號惇爲盲夏侯。

translations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei says: At that time Xiahou Yuan and Dun were both generals, and in the army they called Dun Blind Xiahou.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei notes that he and Xiahou Yuan were then both serving as generals, and the troops nicknamed Dun "Blind Xiahou."

sentences.zh: 惇惡之，每照鏡恚怒，輒撲鏡於地。

translations.literal: Dun hated this; each time he looked in the mirror he fumed with anger and would dash the mirror to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Dun loathed the sobriquet; whenever he caught his reflection he flew into a rage and smashed the mirror to the floor.

sentences.zh: 復領陳留、濟陰太守，加建武將軍，封高安鄉侯。

translations.literal: He again headed Chenliu and Jiyin as grand administrator, was promoted to General Who Establishes Martial Might, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed the governorship of Chenliu and Jiyin, was advanced to General Who Establishes Martial Might, and received the village marquisate of Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，蝗蟲起，惇乃斷太壽水作陂，身自負土，率將士勸種稻，民賴其利。

translations.literal: At that time there was great drought and locusts arose; Dun then cut off the Taishou River to make a reservoir, himself shouldered earth, led officers and troops to urge planting rice, and the people relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought and locust plague he dammed the Taishou River into a reservoir, carried earth on his own back, and drove his soldiers to plant rice; the common people profited from the scheme.

sentences.zh: 轉領河南尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to head Henan as intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was then named intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 太祖平河北，爲大將軍後拒。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Hebei, he served as rear guard of the grand general.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao subdued Hebei, Dun guarded the army's rear as grand general.

sentences.zh: 鄴破，遷伏波將軍，領尹如故，使得以便宜從事，不拘科制。

translations.literal: When Ye fell, he was transferred to General Who Calms the Waves, kept the intendant post as before, and was allowed to act at discretion without being bound by regulations.
translations.idiomatic: After Ye was taken he became General Who Calms the Waves, kept Henan as before, and was empowered to act on his own authority outside the usual statutes.

sentences.zh: 建安十二年，錄惇前後功，增封邑千八百户，并前二千五百户。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jian'an, Dun's merits before and after were recorded; his fief was increased by one thousand eight hundred households, making two thousand five hundred households in all with the previous.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 12 his cumulative honors were tallied and his fief enlarged by 1,800 households, bringing the total to 2,500.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，從征孫權還，使惇都督二十六軍，留居巢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, after returning from campaigning against Sun Quan, he had Dun command the twenty-six armies and remain at Juchao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, returning from the campaign against Sun Quan, Cao Cao left Dun in command of twenty-six armies, stationed at Juchao.

sentences.zh: 賜伎樂名倡，令曰：「魏絳以和戎之功，猶受金石之樂，況將軍乎！」

translations.literal: He bestowed song and dance with famous performers, with an order saying: "Wei Jiang, for the merit of harmonizing the barbarians, still received music of metal and stone; how much more so for a general!"
translations.idiomatic: He gave him musicians and celebrated courtesans, declaring: "Wei Jiang won music of bells and drums for pacifying the Rong—surely a general deserves no less!"

sentences.zh: 二十四年，太祖軍於摩陂，召惇常與同載，特見親重，出入臥内，諸將莫得比也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when the Grand Progenitor's army was at Mobei, he summoned Dun and often rode with him in the same carriage, showed him special intimacy and weight, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters; no general could compare.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, while Cao Cao camped at Mobei, Dun was constantly summoned to share his carriage, treated with exceptional trust, and admitted to the inner quarters—privilege none of his peers matched.

sentences.zh: 拜前將軍，《魏書》曰：時諸將皆受魏官號，惇獨漢官，乃上疏自陳不當不臣之禮。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Vanguard. The Book of Wei says: At that time all the generals received Wei office titles; Dun alone held a Han office, so he submitted a memorial stating that he ought not follow the rites of one who is not a subject.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General of the Vanguard. The Book of Wei records that every other commander had already taken Wei titles while Dun still bore Han rank; he memorialized that he could not accept honors implying he was not a subject of the Han.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「吾聞太上師臣，其次友臣。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "I have heard that the loftiest treats ministers as teachers, next as friends.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied: "They say the sage-emperor treats ministers as teachers, and after that as friends.

sentences.zh: 夫臣者，貴德之人也，區區之魏，而臣足以屈君乎？」

translations.literal: As for ministers, they are men who esteem virtue; how could a mere Wei make a minister enough to humble a lord?"
translations.idiomatic: A minister is a man who honors virtue—how could petty Wei make me your subject and bow you down?"

sentences.zh: 惇固請，乃拜爲前將軍。

translations.literal: Dun firmly petitioned, and thereupon he was appointed general of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Dun pressed the point until Cao Cao finally confirmed him as General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 督諸軍還壽春，徙屯召陵。

translations.literal: He supervised the armies returning to Shouchun and moved encampment to Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He led the armies back to Shouchun and then shifted the camp to Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，拜惇大將軍，數月薨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the royal throne, he appointed Dun grand general; after several months he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended as king of Wei he named Dun grand general; Dun died within months.

sentences.zh: 惇雖在軍旅，親迎師受業。

translations.literal: Although Dun was amid the army, he personally welcomed teachers and received instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Even on campaign he sought out tutors and received classical instruction in person.

sentences.zh: 性清儉，有餘財輒以分施，不足資之於官，不治產業。

translations.literal: His nature was clear and frugal; whenever he had surplus wealth he would distribute it, and what was insufficient he supplied from office, not managing estates.
translations.idiomatic: He was austere by nature, gave away every surplus, drew on official funds rather than private wealth when funds ran short, and never built up family property.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhong (the Loyal).
translations.idiomatic: He was canonized as Marquis Zhong (the Loyal).

sentences.zh: 子充嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 帝追思惇功，欲使子孫畢侯，分惇邑千户，賜惇七子二孫爵皆關内侯。

translations.literal: The Emperor recalled Dun's merit, wished to make his sons and grandsons all marquises, divided Dun's fief by a thousand households, and bestowed on Dun's seven sons and two grandsons titles, all interior marquises.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, recalling Dun's service, wished to ennoble the whole line: he carved a thousand households from Dun's fief and made interior marquises of seven sons and two grandsons.

sentences.zh: 惇弟廉及子楙素自封列侯。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Lian and his son Mao had long since enfeoffed themselves as ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's brother Lian and son Mao had already held ranked marquisates in their own right.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以女妻楙，即清河公主也。

translations.literal: At first, the Grand Progenitor gave a daughter in marriage to Mao, namely the Princess of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had earlier married his daughter—the Princess of Qinghe—to Mao.

sentences.zh: 楙歷位侍中尚書、安西鎮東將軍，假節。

translations.literal: Mao successively held the posts of attendant-in-chief and minister of the masters of writing, General Who Pacifies the West and Quiets the East, and was given the credentials of office.
translations.idiomatic: Mao rose through attendant-in-chief, minister of the masters of writing, and General Who Pacifies the West and Quiets the East, and carried the baton of command.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：楙字子林，惇中子也。

translations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei says: Mao, courtesy name Zilin, was Dun's middle son.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei gives his style as Zilin and identifies him as Dun's second son.

sentences.zh: 文帝少與楙親，及即位，以爲安西將軍、持節，承夏侯淵處都督關中。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen in youth was close to Mao; when he took the throne, he made him General Who Pacifies the West, bearing the baton, succeeding Xiahou Yuan's post in commanding Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had been close to Mao since boyhood; on his accession he named Mao General Who Pacifies the West with full insignia, succeeding Xiahou Yuan as commander of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 楙性無武略，而好治生。

translations.literal: Mao's nature lacked martial stratagem, but he loved managing livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Mao had no talent for war but a passion for moneymaking.

sentences.zh: 至太和二年228年，明帝西征，人有白楙者，遂召還爲尚書。

translations.literal: By the second year of Taihe, 228, when Emperor Ming campaigned west, someone reported Mao, and he was summoned back as minister of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 (228), during Emperor Ming's western expedition, an informer denounced Mao and he was recalled to court as minister of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 楙在西時，多畜伎妾，公主由此與楙不和。

translations.literal: When Mao was in the west, he kept many singing girls and concubines; the princess because of this was not on good terms with Mao.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed in the west Mao kept a large household of entertainers and concubines, which alienated the princess.

sentences.zh: 其後羣弟不遵禮度，楙數切責，弟懼見治，乃共構楙以誹謗，公主奏之，有詔收楙。

translations.literal: Afterward his brothers-in-law did not observe the rules of propriety; Mao repeatedly sternly rebuked them; the younger brothers feared punishment and together framed Mao for slander; the princess memorialized it, and there was an edict to arrest Mao.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife's brothers flouted decorum, Mao scolded them repeatedly; fearing punishment they conspired to accuse him of slander, the princess petitioned the throne, and an edict went out for his arrest.

sentences.zh: 帝意欲殺之，以問長水校尉京兆段默，默以爲「此必清河公主與楙不睦，出於譖構，冀不推實耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor intended to kill him, and asked Colonel of the Long River Duan Mo of Jingzhao; Mo thought: "This must be because the Princess of Qinghe and Mao were not on good terms, arising from slanderous framing, hoping it would not be pursued to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor meant to execute him and consulted Colonel of the Long River Duan Mo of Jingzhao, who said: "This surely stems from the princess's quarrel with Mao—a fabricated charge they hope no one will investigate.

sentences.zh: 且伏波與先帝有定天下之功，宜加三思」。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Pacifying-the-Waves General and the late Emperor had the merit of settling the realm; one ought to add threefold deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Mao's father served the late emperor in conquering the realm—think thrice before acting."

sentences.zh: 帝意解，曰：「吾亦以爲然。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was eased and he said: "I also think it so."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor relented: "I believe you are right."

sentences.zh: 乃發詔推問爲公主作表者，果其羣弟子臧、子江所構也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict to pursue inquiry into who had drafted the princess's memorial; indeed it was framed by her brothers-in-law Zizang and Zijiang.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation traced the memorial to Mao's brothers-in-law Zizang and Zijiang, who had fabricated the case.

sentences.zh: 充薨，子廙嗣。

translations.literal: Chong died; his son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong died his son Yi inherited.

sentences.zh: 廙薨，子劭嗣。

translations.literal: Yi died; his son Shao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died his son Shao inherited.

sentences.zh: 《晉陽秋》曰：泰始二年266年，高安鄉侯夏侯佐卒，惇之孫也，嗣絕。

translations.literal: The Annals of Jin says: In the second year of Taishi, 266, village marquis of Gao'an Xiahou Zuo died, was Dun's grandson, and the succession ended.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Jin record that in Taishi 2 (266) Xiahou Zuo, village marquis of Gao'an and Dun's grandson, died without heirs.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「惇，魏之元功，勳書竹帛。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Dun was Wei's paramount merit, his achievements written on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Dun was Wei's founding pillar; his deeds stand inscribed in the annals.

sentences.zh: 昔庭堅不祀，猶或悼之，況朕受禪於魏，而可以忘其功臣哉！

translations.literal: In former times when Ting Jian had no sacrifices, some still mourned him; how much more, since I received the abdication from Wei, can I forget its meritorious ministers!
translations.idiomatic: When Ting Jian went without sacrifice men still grieved—how could I, having received the mandate from Wei, forget its champions?

sentences.zh: 宜擇惇近屬劭封之。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to select Dun's close kinsman Shao and enfeoff him."
translations.idiomatic: Let Shao, Dun's nearest kin, be chosen to receive the enfeoffment."

sentences.zh: 韓浩者，河内人。

translations.literal: Han Hao was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hao came from Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 及沛國史渙與浩俱以忠勇顯。

translations.literal: Together with Shi Huan of Pei state, Hao became renowned for loyalty and courage.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shi Huan of Pei were both famed for loyal daring.

sentences.zh: 浩至中護軍，渙至中領軍，皆掌禁兵，封列侯。

translations.literal: Hao reached chief of the protectors army, Huan reached commander of the central army, both controlled the forbidden troops, and were enfeoffed as ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hao rose to chief of the protectors army and Shi Huan to commander of the central army; both held the palace guard and received ranked marquisates.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：韓浩字元嗣。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei says: Han Hao, courtesy name Yuansi.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei gives his style as Yuansi.

sentences.zh: 漢末兵起，縣近山藪，多寇，浩聚徒眾爲縣籓衛。

translations.literal: At the end of Han when troops arose, the county was near mountains and marshes with many bandits; Hao gathered followers to defend the county as a barrier.
translations.idiomatic: When war engulfed the Han, his county lay close to wild hills teeming with raiders; Hao rallied a militia to shield the district.

sentences.zh: 太守王匡以爲從事，將兵拒董卓於盟津。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Wang Kuang made him an assistant officer, leading troops to resist Dong Zhuo at Mengjin.
translations.idiomatic: The grand administrator Wang Kuang named him an aide and sent him with troops to block Dong Zhuo at Mengjin.

sentences.zh: 時浩舅杜陽爲河陰令，卓執之，使招浩，浩不從。

translations.literal: At that time Hao's maternal uncle Du Yang was magistrate of Heyin; Zhuo seized him and had him summon Hao; Hao did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo seized Hao's uncle Du Yang, magistrate of Heyin, and used him to summon Hao; Hao refused.

sentences.zh: 袁术聞而壯之，以爲騎都尉。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu heard and admired him, and made him commandant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu admired his stand and appointed him commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 夏侯惇聞其名，請與相見，大奇之，使領兵從征伐。

translations.literal: Xiahou Dun heard his name, requested to meet him, was greatly struck, and had him lead troops following on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Dun sought him out, was mightily impressed, and took him on campaign as a commander.

sentences.zh: 時大議損益，浩以爲當急田。

translations.literal: At that time there was great discussion of increase and decrease; Hao thought one should urgently farm fields.
translations.idiomatic: Amid debate over fiscal reform, Hao argued that agriculture must come first.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之，遷護軍。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved it and promoted him to protector of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao approved and promoted him to protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲討柳城，領軍史渙以爲道遠深入，非完計也，欲與浩共諫。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wished to punish Liucheng; army commander Shi Huan thought the road distant and penetration deep, not a complete plan, and wished together with Hao to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao planned an expedition to Liucheng, army commander Shi Huan judged the march too long and deep to be sound policy and urged Hao to join him in counseling against it.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「今兵勢彊盛，威加四海，戰勝攻取，無不如志，不以此時遂除天下之患，將爲後憂。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Now military strength is mighty and flourishing, prestige covers the four seas, in battle victorious and in attack taking—nothing fails to accord with intent; if we do not at this time then remove the realm's afflictions, there will be later worry.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hao replied: "Our armies are at their height and nothing resists us—if we do not crush the realm's enemies now, we will rue the delay.

sentences.zh: 且公神武，舉無遺策，吾與君爲中軍主，不宜沮眾。」

translations.literal: Moreover the lord is divinely martial; in every move no plan is left out; you and I are masters of the central army—one ought not discourage the host."
translations.idiomatic: The lord is invincible in counsel; as chiefs of staff we must not dampen the troops' spirit."

sentences.zh: 遂從破柳城，改其官爲中護軍，置長史、司馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed in breaking Liucheng; his office was changed to chief of the protectors army, and a chief clerk and marshal were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the victory at Liucheng, was retitled chief of the protectors army, and given chief clerk and marshal.

sentences.zh: 從討張魯，魯降。

translations.literal: He followed in punishing Zhang Lu; Lu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Zhang Lu, Lu submitted.

sentences.zh: 議者以浩智略足以綏邊，欲留使都督諸軍，鎮漢中。

translations.literal: Discussants thought Hao's wisdom and stratagem sufficient to pacify the borderlands, and wished to keep him to command the various armies and guard Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged keeping Han Hao in Hanzhong to command the western armies, trusting his talent for border affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「吾安可以無護軍？」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "How can I be without a protector of the army?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered: "How can I do without my protector of the army?"

sentences.zh: 乃與俱還。

translations.literal: Thereupon they returned together.
translations.idiomatic: Hao returned with him.

sentences.zh: 其見親任如此。

translations.literal: Such was the intimacy and trust shown him.
translations.idiomatic: That was how deeply he was trusted.

sentences.zh: 及薨，太祖愍惜之。

translations.literal: When he died, the Grand Progenitor pitied and mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Cao Cao grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 無子，以養子榮嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son; his adopted son Rong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he was succeeded by his adopted son Rong.

sentences.zh: 史渙字公劉。

translations.literal: Shi Huan, courtesy name Gongliu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Huan, styled Gongliu.

sentences.zh: 少任俠，有雄氣。

translations.literal: In youth he was a knight-errant, with heroic spirit.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he lived by the sword and bore a fierce temper.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起，以客從，行中軍校尉，從征伐，常監諸將，見親信，轉拜中領軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor first rose, he followed as a guest, acted as colonel of the central army, followed on campaigns, constantly supervised the generals, was seen as intimate and trusted, and was transferred and appointed commander of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao first raised his standard, Huan joined as a guest officer, served as acting colonel of the central army, joined every campaign, oversaw the commanders, won close trust, and rose to commander of the central army.

sentences.zh: 十四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 子静嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 夏侯淵字妙才，惇族弟也。

translations.literal: Xiahou Yuan, courtesy name Miaocai, was a clansman younger than Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Yuan, styled Miaocai, was a younger kinsman of Xiahou Dun.

sentences.zh: 太祖居家，曾有縣官事，淵代引重罪，太祖營救之，得免。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor was at home, there had been an affair with the county office; Yuan on his behalf assumed a heavy crime, and the Grand Progenitor worked to rescue him, so he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao was still a private gentleman he tangled with the county authorities; Yuan stepped forward and took the gravest charge on himself, and Cao Cao maneuvered until the sentence was lifted.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：時兖、豫大亂，淵以饑乏，棄其幼子，而活亡弟孤女。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary says: At that time Yan and Yu were in great turmoil; Yuan because of hunger and want abandoned his infant son and kept alive the orphaned daughter of a deceased younger brother.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei lüe relates that when Yan and Yu were convulsed by rebellion, famine forced Yuan to leave his own baby son to die while he saved the orphaned girl of a dead younger brother.〉

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵，以别部司馬、騎都尉從，遷陳留、潁川太守。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor raised troops, he followed as marshal of a separate division and chief of cavalry, was promoted grand administrator of Chenliu and Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao first mustered an army, Yuan joined him as chief of staff of an independent column and as chief of cavalry, then rose to governor of Chenliu and Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 及與袁紹戰於官渡，行督軍校尉。

translations.literal: When he fought Yuan Shao at Guandu, he acted as colonel who supervises the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Guandu he served as acting army inspector under Cao Cao’s command against Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹破，使督兖、豫、徐州軍糧；

translations.literal: When Shao was broken, he was sent to supervise the army grain of Yan, Yu, and Xu provinces;
translations.idiomatic: After Shao’s defeat he was put in charge of grain convoys for Yan, Yu, and Xu;

sentences.zh: 時軍食少，淵傳饋相繼，軍以復振。

translations.literal: at that time army food was scant, yet Yuan relayed supplies in succession, and the army thereby recovered.
translations.idiomatic: provisions were dangerously low, but Yuan kept the wagons moving without a break until the host could fight again.

sentences.zh: 昌豨反，遣于禁擊之，未拔，復遣淵與禁并力，遂擊豨，降其十餘屯，豨詣禁降。

translations.literal: Chang Xi rebelled; Yu Jin was sent to strike him but could not take him; again Yuan was sent with Jin to combine strength; thereupon they struck Xi, reduced more than ten of his stockades, and Xi went to Jin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Xi rose in revolt, Yu Jin was first sent and stalled; Yuan was dispatched to reinforce him. Together they stormed Chang Xi, overran a dozen of his camps, and drove the rebel to surrender to Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 淵還，拜典軍校尉。

translations.literal: Yuan returned and was appointed colonel of the headquarters guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan came back and was named colonel of the headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：淵爲將，赴急疾，常出敵之不意，故軍中爲之語曰：「典軍校尉夏侯淵，三日五百，六日一千。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei says: As a general Yuan rushed emergencies with extreme speed, often catching the enemy unawares, so the army made a saying of him: “The headquarters colonel Xiahou Yuan: five hundred in three days, a thousand in six days.”〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu notes that Yuan habitually moved faster than anyone expected; soldiers coined the rhyme: “Headquarters colonel Xiahou Yuan—five hundred li in three days, a thousand in six.”〉

sentences.zh: 濟南、樂安黄巾徐和、司馬俱等攻城，殺長吏，淵將泰山、齊、平原郡兵擊，大破之，斬和，平諸縣，收其糧穀以給軍士。

translations.literal: The Jinan and Le’an Yellow Turbans Xu He, Sima Ju, and others attacked cities and killed senior officials; Yuan led the troops of Mount Tai, Qi, and Pingyuan commanderies to strike them, greatly defeated them, beheaded He, pacified the various counties, and collected their grain to supply the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Turban remnants Xu He and Sima Ju in Jinan and Le’an were storming towns and murdering magistrates; Yuan led the Mount Tai, Qi, and Pingyuan levies against them, crushed their army, beheaded Xu He, restored order county by county, and seized their grain for the troops.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以淵爲行領軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Yuan was appointed acting commander of the guard army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the Jian’an era he was made acting commander of the guard army.

sentences.zh: 太祖征孫權還，使淵督諸將擊廬江叛者雷緒，緒破，又行征西護軍，督徐晃擊太原賊，攻下二十餘屯，斬賊帥商曜，屠其城。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Sun Quan and returned, he had Yuan supervise the generals to strike the rebel Lei Xu in Lujiang; when Xu was broken, again he acted as protector of the army on the west and supervised Xu Huang in striking the bandits of Taiyuan, attacking and taking more than twenty stockades, beheading their leader Shang Yao, and slaughtering his city.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao’s expedition against Sun Quan, he sent Yuan to direct the generals against the Lujiang mutineer Lei Xu. When Lei Xu fell, Yuan took the acting post of western army protector and oversaw Xu Huang’s sweep of the Taiyuan bandits—twenty stockades stormed, chieftain Shang Yao executed, and his stronghold put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 從征韓遂等，戰於渭南。

translations.literal: He followed on the campaign against Han Sui and others, fighting south of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Cao Cao against Han Sui’s coalition and fought on the south bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 又督朱靈平隃糜、汧氐。

translations.literal: Again he supervised Zhu Ling in pacifying the Di of Yumi and Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He also directed Zhu Ling in subduing the Di peoples of Yumi and along the Qian River.

sentences.zh: 與太祖會安定，降楊秋。

translations.literal: He joined the Grand Progenitor at Anding and reduced Yang Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: He met Cao Cao at Anding and accepted Yang Qiu’s surrender.

sentences.zh: 十七年，太祖乃還鄴，以淵行護軍將軍，督朱靈、路招等屯長安，擊破南山賊劉雄，降其眾。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Grand Progenitor then returned to Ye and appointed Yuan acting protector general, supervising Zhu Ling, Lu Zhao, and others encamped at Chang’an, smashing the southern-mountain bandit Liu Xiong and reducing his multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Cao Cao went back to Ye and named Yuan acting protector general with Zhu Ling, Lu Zhao, and others to hold Chang’an. They routed the bandit Liu Xiong in the southern hills and brought his followers to heel.

sentences.zh: 圍遂、超餘党梁興於鄠，拔之，斬興，封博昌亭侯。

translations.literal: He besieged the remaining party of Sui and Chao, Liang Xing, at Hu, took it, beheaded Xing, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Bochang.
translations.idiomatic: He bottled up Liang Xing, a remnant of Han Sui and Ma Chao’s faction, inside Hu, stormed the town, struck off Liang Xing’s head, and received the village marquisate of Bochang.

sentences.zh: 馬超圍涼州刺史韋康於冀，淵救康，未到，康敗。

translations.literal: Ma Chao besieged Inspector of Liangzhou Wei Kang at Ji; Yuan went to rescue Kang, but before he arrived Kang was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao penned Liangzhou Inspector Wei Kang inside Ji; Yuan raced to the relief but arrived too late—Wei Kang had already lost.

sentences.zh: 去冀二百餘里，超來逆戰，軍不利。

translations.literal: He was more than two hundred li from Ji; Chao came to oppose him in battle, and the army was unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: Still over two hundred li short of Ji, he collided with Ma Chao’s vanguard and suffered a reverse.

sentences.zh: 汧氐反，淵引軍還。

translations.literal: The Di of Qian rebelled, and Yuan led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di along the Qian rose, Yuan broke off and withdrew his column.

sentences.zh: 十九年，趙衢、尹奉等謀討超，姜叙起兵鹵城以應之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Zhao Qu, Yin Feng, and others plotted to punish Chao; Jiang Xu raised troops at Lucheng to respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Zhao Qu and Yin Feng conspired to destroy Ma Chao; Jiang Xu raised the standard at Lucheng to back them.

sentences.zh: 衢等譎說超，使出擊叙，於後盡殺超妻子。

translations.literal: Qu and others deceitfully persuaded Chao to go out and strike Xu, and in the rear entirely killed Chao’s wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qu’s party tricked Ma Chao into riding out against Jiang Xu, then slaughtered every member of his family left behind.

sentences.zh: 超奔漢中，還圍祁山。

translations.literal: Chao fled to Hanzhong and returned to besiege Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao bolted to Hanzhong, then swung back to invest Qishan.

sentences.zh: 叙等急求救，諸將議者欲湏太祖節度。

translations.literal: Xu and others urgently begged for rescue; among the generals in council some wished to await the Grand Progenitor’s orders.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xu’s men begged for immediate aid; several generals argued they must wait for orders from Cao Cao at Ye.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「公在鄴，反覆四千里，比報，叙等必敗，非救急也。」

translations.literal: Yuan said: “The lord is at Ye; going back and forth is four thousand li; by the time a report returns Xu and others will certainly have been defeated; it is not saving the urgent.”
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied, “The Duke is four thousand li away in Ye. By the time a messenger returns, Jiang Xu will be dust. That is no rescue at all.”

sentences.zh: 遂行，使張郃督步騎五千在前，從陳倉狹道入，淵自督糧在後。

translations.literal: Thereupon he proceeded, had Zhang He supervise five thousand infantry and cavalry in the van, enter by the narrow road from Cangcang, and Yuan himself supervised supplies in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: He moved at once, sent Zhang He ahead with five thousand horse and foot through the Cangcang defile, and himself shepherded the baggage train.

sentences.zh: 郃至渭水上，超將氐羌數千逆郃。

translations.literal: When He reached the north bank of the Wei, Chao’s generals, Di and Qiang numbering several thousand, opposed He.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He’s van reached the Wei’s north shore, where several thousand Di and Qiang troopers under Ma Chao barred the way.

sentences.zh: 未戰，超走，郃進軍收超軍器械。

translations.literal: Before battle, Chao fled; He advanced the army and collected Chao’s army equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Before the lines closed Ma Chao bolted; Zhang He pushed on and scooped up abandoned gear by the wagonload.

sentences.zh: 淵到，諸縣皆已降。

translations.literal: When Yuan arrived, the various counties had all already surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Yuan came up, every county along the route had capitulated.

sentences.zh: 韓遂在顯親，淵欲襲取之，遂走。

translations.literal: Han Sui was at Xianqin; Yuan wished to raid and take him, but Sui fled.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui was holding Xianqin; Yuan tried to fall on him by surprise, but Sui slipped away.

sentences.zh: 淵收遂軍糧，追至略陽城，去遂二十餘里，諸將欲攻之，或言當攻興國氐。

translations.literal: Yuan collected Sui’s army grain, pursued to the city of Lueyang, was more than twenty li from Sui; the generals wished to attack him, or some said they ought to attack the Di of Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan seized Han Sui’s granaries and chased him to Lueyang, closing to within twenty li. Some captains wanted to storm Sui’s camp; others urged a strike at the Di stronghold of Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 淵以爲遂兵精，興國城固，攻不可卒拔，不如擊長離諸羌。

translations.literal: Yuan thought Sui’s troops were elite and the city of Xingguo secure, that an attack could not be taken in haste, and that it was better to strike the various Qiang of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan judged Han Sui’s veterans too tough and the walls of Xingguo too high for a quick win; better to hit the Qiang settlements at Changli instead.

sentences.zh: 長離諸羌多在遂軍，必歸救其家。

translations.literal: The various Qiang of Changli for the most part were in Sui’s army and would certainly return to save their families.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Changli Qiang were serving in Han Sui’s ranks and would race home the moment their villages burned.

sentences.zh: 若羌獨守則孤，救長離則官兵得與野戰，可必虜也。

translations.literal: If the Qiang alone guard then they are isolated; if they rescue Changli then the officers and troops can obtain field battle with them and can be certain to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Leave the Qiang isolated on the heights, or draw them out to save Changli—either way our men fight them in the open and can break them for good.

sentences.zh: 淵乃留督將守輜重，輕兵步騎到長離，攻燒羌屯，斬获甚眾。

translations.literal: Yuan then left supervising generals to guard the baggage, and with light troops of infantry and cavalry reached Changli, attacked and burned the Qiang stockades, and beheaded and captured in very great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He left deputies to shield the train, took picked horse and foot to Changli, torched the Qiang camps, and piled up heads and prisoners beyond count.

sentences.zh: 諸羌在遂軍者，各還種落。

translations.literal: The various Qiang who had been in Sui’s army each returned to their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Every Qiang who had marched with Han Sui melted back toward his own tribe.

sentences.zh: 遂果救長離，與淵軍对陣。

translations.literal: Sui indeed rescued Changli and opposed Yuan’s army in battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui did hurry to Changli, where he drew up against Yuan’s host.

sentences.zh: 諸將見遂眾，惡之，欲結營作塹乃與戰。

translations.literal: The generals saw Sui’s multitude, detested it, and wished to bind camps and dig trenches before fighting with him.
translations.idiomatic: His officers blanched at Han Sui’s numbers and wanted to entrench and wait.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「我轉鬭千里，今復作營塹，則士眾罷弊，不可久。

translations.literal: Yuan said: “I have turned and fought a thousand li; now again to make camp trenches then the soldiers will be exhausted and weakened; it cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, “We have fought our way a thousand li. If we start digging lines now the men will be played out before a blow is struck.

sentences.zh: 賊雖眾，易與耳。」

translations.literal: Though the bandits are many, they are easy to deal with.”
translations.idiomatic: They outnumber us, but they are rabble we can break.”

sentences.zh: 乃鼓之，大破遂軍，得其旌麾，還略陽，進軍圍興國。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drummed them, greatly defeated Sui’s army, obtained his banners and standards, returned to Lueyang, advanced the army, and besieged Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the advance, shattered Han Sui’s line, seized his command banners, fell back to Lueyang, then swung the whole army against Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 氐王千萬逃奔馬超，餘眾降。

translations.literal: The Di king Qianwan fled to join Ma Chao, and the remaining multitude surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Qianwan bolted to Ma Chao; everyone else submitted.

sentences.zh: 轉擊高平屠各，皆散走，收其糧穀牛馬。

translations.literal: He turned to strike the Gaoping Tuge; all scattered and fled, and he collected their grain, cattle, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He next hit the Tuge tribesmen of Gaoping; they broke and ran, leaving grain, oxen, and horses for the taking.

sentences.zh: 乃假淵節。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuan was given the credentials of office.
translations.idiomatic: The court then invested him with formal insignia of command.

sentences.zh: 初，枹罕宋建因涼州亂，自號河首平漢王。

translations.literal: At first, Song Jian of Fuhan, because of turmoil in Liangzhou, styled himself King Who Pacifies Han at the Head of the River.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liangzhou dissolved into chaos, Song Jian of Fuhan had crowned himself “River-head King Who Pacifies the Han.”

sentences.zh: 太祖使淵帥諸將討建。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sent Yuan to lead the generals to punish Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao dispatched Yuan at the head of several columns to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 淵至，圍枹罕，月餘拔之，斬建及所置丞相已下。

translations.literal: When Yuan arrived, he besieged Fuhan, after more than a month took it, beheaded Jian and those down to the chancellor he had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan invested Fuhan, stormed it after a month, and executed Song Jian together with every minister he had named.

sentences.zh: 淵别遣張郃等平河關，渡河入小湟中，河西諸羌盡降，隴右平。

translations.literal: Yuan separately sent Zhang He and others to pacify Heguan, crossed the river and entered Little Huangzhong, all the Qiang west of the river surrendered, and the right of the Long was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He detached Zhang He to clear Heguan, crossed into Little Huangzhong, brought every Qiang tribe west of the river to terms, and quieted the Longyou corridor.

sentences.zh: 太祖下令曰：「宋建造爲亂逆三十餘年，淵一舉滅之，虎步關右，所向無前。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor issued an order saying: “Song Jian acted as a rebel traitor for more than thirty years; Yuan in one stroke destroyed him, tiger-stepped the right of the passes, and wherever he faced there was none before him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao proclaimed: “Song Jian wallowed in rebellion for thirty years; Xiahou Yuan wiped him out at a stroke, strode the Longyou like a tiger, and nothing stood in his path.

sentences.zh: 仲尼有言：『吾與尔不如也。』」

translations.literal: Confucius had a saying: ‘I am not his match; you are not like him."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius once admitted, “I am not his equal; you are not like him."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，增封三百户，并前八百户。

translations.literal: ’” In the twenty-first year, three hundred households were added to his fief, making eight hundred households in all with the previous.
translations.idiomatic: ’” In the twenty-first year three hundred new households were added to his fief, bringing the total to eight hundred.

sentences.zh: 還擊武都氐羌下辯，收氐穀十餘萬斛。

translations.literal: He returned and struck the Di and Qiang of Wu commandery at Xiabian, collecting more than one hundred thousand hu of Di grain.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he struck the Di and Qiang at Xiabian in Wu commandery and carried off well over a hundred thousand hu of their grain.

sentences.zh: 太祖西征張魯，淵等將涼州諸將侯王已下，與太祖會休亭。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned west against Zhang Lu, Yuan and others led the Liangzhou generals marquises and below to join the Grand Progenitor at Xiuting.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched west against Zhang Lu, Yuan shepherded every Liangzhou commander from marquis rank downward to rendezvous with him at Xiuting.

sentences.zh: 太祖每引見羌、胡，以淵畏之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Grand Progenitor led in Qiang and Hu for audience, they feared Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cao Cao paraded Qiang and Xiongnu chiefs before his tent, they went pale at the sight of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 會魯降，漢中平，以淵行都護將軍，督張郃、徐晃等平巴郡。

translations.literal: When it happened that Lu surrendered and Hanzhong was pacified, Yuan was appointed acting chief protector general and supervised Zhang He, Xu Huang, and others in pacifying Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Lu yielded and Hanzhong was settled, Yuan became acting chief protector general and oversaw Zhang He and Xu Huang in mopping up Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖還鄴，留淵守漢中，即拜淵征西將軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor returned to Ye, he left Yuan to guard Hanzhong, and immediately appointed Yuan general who campaigns west.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao went back to Ye but left Yuan to hold Hanzhong, promoting him on the spot to general who campaigns west.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，劉備軍陽平關，淵率諸將拒之，相守連年。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Liu Bei’s army was at Yangping Pass; Yuan led the generals to resist him, holding each other for successive years.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Liu Bei’s army camped at Yangping Pass; Yuan commanded the defense, and the two sides glared at each other year after year.

sentences.zh: 二十四年正月，備夜燒圍鹿角。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year, Bei by night burned the stockade palisades.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year Liu Bei sent men by night to burn the palisade around the camp.

sentences.zh: 淵使張郃護東圍，自將輕兵護南圍。

translations.literal: Yuan had Zhang He guard the eastern enclosure and himself led light troops to guard the southern enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan assigned Zhang He to the eastern sector while he took picked troops to the south face himself.

sentences.zh: 備挑郃戰，郃軍不利。

translations.literal: Bei challenged He to battle, and He’s army was unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei baited Zhang He into a sortie; Zhang He’s detachment came off worse.

sentences.zh: 淵分所將兵半助郃，爲備所襲，淵遂戰死。

translations.literal: Yuan divided half the troops he commanded to assist He, was raided by Bei, and Yuan thereupon died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan split his command to reinforce Zhang He, walked into an ambush laid by Liu Bei, and fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 諡曰愍侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was marquis compassionate.
translations.idiomatic: He was canonized as Marquis Min (the Compassionate).

sentences.zh: 初，淵雖數戰勝，太祖常戒曰：「爲將當有怯弱時，不可但恃勇也。

translations.literal: At first, although Yuan several times won in battle, the Grand Progenitor always admonished him saying: “As a general there ought to be times of timidity and weakness; one cannot rely only on courage.
translations.idiomatic: Even while Yuan was winning fight after fight, Cao Cao used to warn him: “A commander needs moments of caution; sheer daring is not enough.

sentences.zh: 將當以勇爲本，行之以智計；

translations.literal: A general ought to take courage as the root and carry it out with stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: Courage must be the base, but it has to be guided by calculation;

sentences.zh: 但知任勇，一匹夫敵耳。」

translations.literal: if one only knows to employ courage, one is a match for a single common fellow.”
translations.idiomatic: rely on nothing but brawn and you are no better than a common brawler.”

sentences.zh: 淵妻，太祖内妹。

translations.literal: 」Yuan's wife was the Grand Progenitor's younger sister by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: 」She was Cao Cao's sister-in-law.

sentences.zh: 長子衡，尚太祖弟海陽哀侯女，恩寵特隆。

translations.literal: The eldest son Heng married the daughter of the Grand Progenitor's younger brother, Marquis Ai of Haiyang, and received exceptional grace and favor.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Heng married a daughter of Cao Cao's brother, Marquis Ai of Haiyang, and enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 衡襲爵，轉封安寧亭侯。

translations.literal: Heng inherited the title and was transferred and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anning village.
translations.idiomatic: Heng inherited the line and was shifted to Marquis of Anning village.

sentences.zh: 黄初中，賜中子霸，太和中，賜霸四弟，爵皆關内侯。

translations.literal: In Huangchu times the middle son Ba was bestowed; in Taihe times Ba's four younger brothers were bestowed; all their titles were interior marquises.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangchu era the middle son Ba was ennobled; in Taihe his four younger brothers followed, all as interior marquises.

sentences.zh: 霸，正始中爲討蜀護軍右將軍，進封博昌亭侯，素爲曹爽所厚。

translations.literal: Ba, in Zhengshi times served as protector general against Shu and General of the Right, was advanced to Marquis of Bochang village, and had long been favored by Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era Ba served as protector general against Shu and General of the Right, was advanced to Marquis of Bochang village, and had long been a favorite of Cao Shuang.

sentences.zh: 聞爽誅，自疑，亡入蜀。

translations.literal: Hearing of Shuang's execution, he grew suspicious and fled into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang was executed he panicked and fled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 以淵舊勳赦霸子，徙樂浪郡。

translations.literal: Because of Yuan's old merit, Ba's sons were pardoned and relocated to Lelang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Yuan's old service his sons were spared and exiled to Lelang commandery.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：霸字仲權。

translations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei says: Ba, courtesy name Zhongquan.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei gives his style as Zhongquan.

sentences.zh: 淵爲蜀所害，故霸常切齒，欲有報蜀意。

translations.literal: Yuan was harmed by Shu; therefore Ba constantly gnashed his teeth and wished to have the intent of repaying Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuan had been killed by Shu, Ba burned to avenge him.

sentences.zh: 黄初中爲偏將軍。

translations.literal: In Huangchu times he was lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangchu era he was made lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 子午之役，霸召爲前鋒，進至興勢圍，安營在曲谷中。

translations.literal: In the battle of Ziwu, Ba was summoned as vanguard, advanced to the enclosure of Xingshi, and set camp in Qu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Ziwu he was called up as vanguard, reached the siege lines at Xingshi, and pitched camp in Qu Valley.

sentences.zh: 蜀人望知其是霸也，指下兵攻之。

translations.literal: Shu men looking afar knew it was Ba and pointed the troops below to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu scouts recognized Ba and directed an assault against his position.

sentences.zh: 霸手戰鹿角間，賴救至，然後解。

translations.literal: Ba fought hand-to-hand between the palisades; relying on rescue arriving, only then was he relieved.
translations.idiomatic: He fought hand to hand within the palisade until reinforcements arrived and extricated him.

sentences.zh: 後爲右將軍，屯隴西，其養士和戎，并得其歡心。

translations.literal: Later he was General of the Right, encamped in Longxi, nourished soldiers and harmonized with barbarians, and obtained the hearts of all.
translations.idiomatic: Later as General of the Right stationed in Longxi he won over his troops and pacified the frontier tribes alike.

sentences.zh: 至正始中，代夏侯儒爲征蜀護軍，統屬征西。

translations.literal: By Zhengshi times, he replaced Xiahou Ru as protector general against Shu and came under the command of the general who campaigns west.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi he succeeded Xiahou Ru as protector general against Shu under the western expedition command.

sentences.zh: 時征西將軍夏侯玄，於霸爲從子，而玄於曹爽爲外弟。

translations.literal: At that time General Who Campaigns West Xiahou Xuan was, to Ba, a nephew by a clanswoman, while Xuan to Cao Shuang was a younger brother by a sister.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Campaigns West Xiahou Xuan was Ba's clansman-nephew and Cao Shuang's cousin on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 及司馬宣王誅曹爽，遂召玄，玄來東。

translations.literal: When Sima the Illustrious King executed Cao Shuang, he then summoned Xuan; Xuan came east.
translations.idiomatic: When the Illustrious King of Jin executed Cao Shuang he summoned Xuan east to court.

sentences.zh: 霸聞曹爽被誅而玄又徵，以爲祸必轉相及，心既内恐；

translations.literal: Ba heard that Cao Shuang had been executed and Xuan was also summoned; he thought disaster must spread in succession, and his heart was already inwardly fearful;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Cao Shuang's death and Xuan's recall, Ba assumed the purge would reach him and was filled with dread;

sentences.zh: 又霸先與雍州刺史郭淮不和，而淮代玄爲征西，霸尤不安，故遂奔蜀。

translations.literal: Moreover Ba had earlier not been on good terms with Inspector of Yong Guo Huai, and when Huai replaced Xuan as commander west, Ba was especially uneasy; therefore he fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He had also feuded with Guo Huai, inspector of Yong, who now replaced Xuan in the west—and so he bolted to Shu.

sentences.zh: 南趣陰平而失道，入窮谷中，糧盡，殺馬步行，足破，臥巖石下，使人求道，未知何之。

translations.literal: He headed south toward Yinping but lost the road, entered a remote valley, grain was exhausted, he killed his horse and walked, feet broken, lay beneath cliff rocks, sent men seeking the road, not knowing where to go.
translations.idiomatic: He turned south toward Yinping, lost his way in a desolate gorge, ran out of food, killed his horse and went on foot with bleeding feet, and lay under a cliff while messengers searched in vain for a route.

sentences.zh: 蜀聞之，乃使人迎霸。

translations.literal: Shu heard of it and then sent men to welcome Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Shu heard of his plight and sent a party to receive him.

sentences.zh: 初，建安五年，時霸從妹年十三四，在本郡，出行樵採，爲張飛所得。

translations.literal: At first, in the fifth year of Jian'an, at that time Ba's cousin by a clanswoman was thirteen or fourteen, in the native commandery, went out to gather firewood and was taken by Zhang Fei.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 5, when Ba's cousin was thirteen or fourteen, she was gathering firewood in the district and was seized by Zhang Fei.

sentences.zh: 飛知其良家女，遂以爲妻，產息女，爲劉禪皇后。

translations.literal: Fei knew she was a good-family girl and then took her as wife; she bore a daughter who became Empress of Liu Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing her to be from a respectable house, Zhang Fei married her; their daughter became Empress of Liu Shan.

sentences.zh: 故淵之初亡，飛妻請而葬之。

translations.literal: Therefore when Yuan first perished, Fei's wife requested and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan first fell, Zhang Fei's wife obtained leave to bury him.

sentences.zh: 及霸入蜀，禪與相見，釋之曰：「卿父自遇害於行間耳，非我先人之手刃也。」

translations.literal: When Ba entered Shu, Shan met with him and explained, saying: "Your father himself met harm amid the ranks; it was not my forebears' hands that blade-slaughtered him."
translations.idiomatic: When Ba arrived in Shu, Liu Shan received him and said: "Your father fell in battle—it was not my forebears who killed him with their own hands."

sentences.zh: 指其兒子以示之曰：「此夏侯氏之甥也。」

translations.literal: Pointing to his son to show him, he said: "This is a nephew of the Xiahou clan."
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to his son and said: "This boy is your clan's nephew."

sentences.zh: 厚加爵寵。

translations.literal: He richly added titles and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan heaped honors upon him.

sentences.zh: 霸弟威，官至兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Ba's younger brother Wei reached the post of Inspector of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Ba's brother Wei rose to inspector of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：威字季權，任俠。

translations.literal: A Saying of the Age says: Wei, courtesy name Jiquan, was a knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: A Saying of the Age gives his style as Jiquan and calls him a man of the sword.

sentences.zh: 貴歷荆、兖二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Gui reign he served as inspector of Jing and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gui he held both Jing and Yan provincial inspectorates.

sentences.zh: 子駿，并州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Jun was Inspector of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun became inspector of Bing.

sentences.zh: 次莊，淮南太守。

translations.literal: The next, Zhuang, was Grand Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The next son Zhuang served as grand administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 莊子湛，字孝若，以才博文章，至南陽相、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Zhuang's son Zhan, courtesy name Xiaoruo, by talent broad and literary compositions, reached Chancellor of Nanyang and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang's son Zhan, styled Xiaoruo, won fame for learning and prose, rising to chancellor of Nanyang and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 莊，晉景陽皇后姊夫也。

translations.literal: Zhuang was the brother-in-law of Empress Jingyang of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was brother-in-law to Jin's Empress Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 由此一門侈盛於時。

translations.literal: From this the whole clan was extravagant and flourishing in the age.
translations.idiomatic: From that branch the clan flourished extravagantly.

sentences.zh: 威弟惠，樂安太守。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Hui was Grand Administrator of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's brother Hui was grand administrator of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 《文章叙錄》曰：惠字稚權，幼以才學見稱，善屬奏議。

translations.literal: Collected Sayings on Literature says: Hui, courtesy name Zhiquan, in youth was acclaimed for talent and learning, skilled at composing memorials and deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Sayings on Literature gives his style as Zhiquan, praising his precocious talent and skill at memorial writing.

sentences.zh: 歷散騎黄門侍郎，與锺毓數有辯駮，事多見從。

translations.literal: He successively served as Gentleman Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Yellow Gate, had repeated debates with Zhong Yu, and matters were often followed.
translations.idiomatic: He served as gentleman attendant of scattered cavalry and yellow gate attendant, debated repeatedly with Zhong Yu, and usually prevailed.

sentences.zh: 遷燕相、樂安太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of Yan and Grand Administrator of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to chancellor of Yan and grand administrator of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 年三十七卒。

translations.literal: At age thirty-seven he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 惠弟和，河南尹。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother He was Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's brother He was intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：和字義權，清辯有才論。

translations.literal: A Saying of the Age says: He, courtesy name Yiquan, was clear in debate and had talent for discourse.
translations.idiomatic: A Saying of the Age gives his style as Yiquan and describes him as sharp in debate and gifted in argument.

sentences.zh: 歷河南尹、太常。

translations.literal: He successively served as Intendant of Henan and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Henan intendant post and the ministry of ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 淵第三子稱，第五子榮。

translations.literal: Yuan's third son Cheng and fifth son Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's third son was Cheng and his fifth Rong.

sentences.zh: 從孫湛爲其

translations.literal: His clansman-grandson Zhan for him
translations.idiomatic: His clansman-grandson Zhan composed for him

translations.literal: 〈Preface〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Preface〉

sentences.zh: 曰：「稱字叔權。

translations.literal: says: "Cheng, courtesy name Shuquan.
translations.idiomatic: It reads: "Cheng, styled Shuquan.

sentences.zh: 自孺子而好合聚童兒，爲之渠帥，戲必爲軍旅戰陣之事，有違者輒嚴以鞭捶，眾莫敢逆。

translations.literal: From infancy he loved gathering children, became their chieftain; in play it was always army encampment and battle array matters; whoever disobeyed he immediately severely whipped, and none dared oppose.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he gathered boys about him as a warlord among children; play always meant battle lines, and any rebel he thrashed until none dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 淵陰奇之，使讀《項羽傳》及兵書，不肯，曰：『能則自爲耳，安能學人？』

translations.literal: Yuan inwardly marveled at him and had him read the biography of Xiang Yu and military books; he refused, saying: 'If able then act on one's own; how can one study others?'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan secretly admired him and set him to read the biography of Xiang Yu and the military classics; the boy refused: 'If I have the gift I'll rely on myself—why copy another man?'

sentences.zh: 年十六，淵與之田，見奔虎，稱驅馬逐之，禁之不可，一箭而倒。

translations.literal: At age sixteen, Yuan with him went to the fields, saw a fleeing tiger; Cheng drove his horse in pursuit; forbidding him was impossible; one arrow and it fell.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, out hunting with Yuan, he spurred after a fleeing tiger despite orders to stop and dropped it with a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 名聞太祖，太祖把其手喜曰：『我得汝矣！』

translations.literal: His name reached the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor grasped his hand delighted and said: 'I have obtained you!'
translations.idiomatic: Word reached Cao Cao, who seized his hand in delight and cried: 'I have found my man!'

sentences.zh: 與文帝爲布衣之交，每讌會，氣陵一坐，辯士不能屈。

translations.literal: With Emperor Wen he was friends as common cloth; at every banquet his spirit towered over the whole seat; debaters could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: He was a close friend of the future Emperor Wen; at every feast his presence dominated the room and no wit could best him.

sentences.zh: 世之高名者多從之游。

translations.literal: Many of the age's high names often associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the highest reputation sought his company.

sentences.zh: 年十八卒。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighteen.

sentences.zh: 弟榮，字幼權。

translations.literal: Younger brother Rong, courtesy name Youquan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Rong, styled Youquan.

sentences.zh: 幼聰惠，七歲能屬文，誦書日千言，經目輒識之。

translations.literal: In youth clever and gifted; at age seven able to compose prose; recited books a thousand words per day; once seen he always remembered.
translations.idiomatic: He was precocious: at seven he could compose prose, recited a thousand characters a day, and never forgot what he read.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞而請焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wen sent for him.

sentences.zh: 賓客百餘人，人一奏刺，悉書其鄉邑名氏，世所謂爵里刺也，客示之，一寓目，使之遍談，不謬一人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred guests, each presented a visiting card; he wrote all their native commanderies and surnames—the so-called card of fief and village of the age; when guests showed them, with one glance he had them discuss fully and not one was mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Before a hundred guests he was shown the visiting cards known as "fief-and-hometown tablets," glanced once, and named every man without error.

sentences.zh: 帝深奇之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply struck.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished.

sentences.zh: 漢中之敗，榮年十三，左右提之走，不肯，曰：『君親在難，焉所逃死！』

translations.literal: In the defeat at Hanzhong, Rong was thirteen; attendants pulled him to flee; he refused, saying: 'Lord and father are in peril; where is flight to death!'
translations.idiomatic: At the Hanzhong disaster, aged thirteen, attendants tried to drag him away; he refused: 'My lords and kin are in danger—where would I flee and live?'

sentences.zh: 乃奮劍而戰，遂沒陣。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he roused his sword and fought, and thereupon perished in the battle line."
translations.idiomatic: He seized a sword, fought, and fell on the field."

sentences.zh: 衡薨，子績嗣，爲虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: Heng died; his son Ji succeeded and was Commandant of the Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Heng died his son Ji inherited and became commandant of the tiger guard.

sentences.zh: 績薨，子褒嗣。

translations.literal: Ji died; his son Bao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji died his son Bao inherited.

sentences.zh: 曹仁字子孝，太祖從弟也。

translations.literal: Cao Ren, courtesy name Zixiao, was a cousin of the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren, styled Zixiao, was a younger cousin of Cao Cao on his father’s side.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：仁祖褒，潁川太守。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei says: Ren’s grandfather Cao Bao was grand administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu states that his grandfather Cao Bao had been governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父炽，侍中、長水校尉。〉

translations.literal: His father Chi was attendant-in-chief and colonel of the long river.〉
translations.idiomatic: His father Cao Chi served as attendant-in-chief and colonel of the Long River guards.〉

sentences.zh: 少好弓馬弋猎。

translations.literal: In youth he loved bow, horse, and hunting with hawks and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was devoted to horsemanship, archery, and the chase.

sentences.zh: 後豪杰并起，仁亦陰結少年，得千餘人，周旋淮、泗之間，遂從太祖爲别部司馬，行厉鋒校尉。

translations.literal: Afterward when heroes rose together, Ren also secretly gathered young men, obtained more than a thousand, and moved between the Huai and Si, then followed the Grand Progenitor as marshal of a separate division, acting colonel who displays the keen edge.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm filled with warlords, Ren quietly recruited a thousand restless youths and ranged the country between the Huai and the Si until he joined Cao Cao as chief of an independent column, with the acting title colonel of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 太祖之破袁术，仁所斬获颇多。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor defeated Yuan Shu, what Ren beheaded and captured was quite abundant.
translations.idiomatic: At Cao Cao’s victory over Yuan Shu, Ren’s tally of killed and captured ran unusually high.

sentences.zh: 從征徐州，仁常督騎，爲軍前鋒。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Xu province, Ren always supervised cavalry and was the army’s van.
translations.idiomatic: During the drive on Xu province he habitually led the cavalry screen and spearheaded every assault.

sentences.zh: 别攻陶謙將吕由，破之，還與大軍合彭城，大破謙軍。

translations.literal: Separately he attacked Tao Qian’s general Lü You, defeated him, returned and joined the great army at Pengcheng, and greatly defeated Qian’s army.
translations.idiomatic: He detached a column against Tao Qian’s officer Lü You, broke him, rejoined the main host at Pengcheng, and helped shatter Tao Qian’s field army.

sentences.zh: 從攻费、华、即墨、开陽，謙遣别將救諸縣，仁以騎擊破之。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Fei, Hua, Jimo, and Kaiyang; Qian sent separate generals to rescue the various counties, and Ren with cavalry defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He next joined the sieges of Fei, Hua, Jimo, and Kaiyang; when Tao Qian rushed relief columns to those towns, Ren rode them down in detail.

sentences.zh: 太祖征吕布，仁别攻句陽，拔之，生获布將劉何。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Lü Bu, Ren separately attacked Gouyang, took it, and captured alive Lü Bu’s general Liu He.
translations.idiomatic: During Cao Cao’s campaign against Lü Bu, Ren detached a column against Gouyang, stormed the town, and brought back Bu’s general Liu He as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太祖平黄巾，迎天子都许，仁數有功，拜广陽太守。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified the Yellow Turbans, welcomed the Son of Heaven, and established the capital at Xu, Ren repeatedly had merit and was appointed grand administrator of Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao crushed the Yellow Turbans, escorted the emperor to Xu, and set up his court there, Ren piled up enough victories to be named governor of Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖器其勇略，不使之郡，以議郎督騎。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor valued his courage and stratagem, did not send him to the commandery, and instead had him, as gentleman consultant, supervise cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao prized his dash and tactical sense, kept him from a provincial desk job, and left him at court as a gentleman consultant in charge of the horse troops.

sentences.zh: 太祖征張绣，仁别徇旁縣，虜其男女三千餘人。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Zhang Xiu, Ren separately toured neighboring counties and captured more than three thousand of their men and women.
translations.idiomatic: On the Zhang Xiu expedition Ren ranged the outlying counties on his own and rounded up over three thousand civilians and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 太祖軍還，爲绣所追，軍不利，士卒喪氣，仁率厉將士甚奮，太祖壯之，遂破绣。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor’s army returned, it was pursued by Xiu; the army was unsuccessful and the soldiers lost heart; Ren led and exhorted the officers and troops to great zeal; the Grand Progenitor thought him stalwart, and thereupon defeated Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home Cao Cao’s column was run down by Zhang Xiu and began to waver; Ren rallied the ranks until their spirit returned. Cao Cao admired the show of nerve and turned defeat into a rout of Zhang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 太祖與袁紹久相持於官渡，紹遣劉備徇㶏彊諸縣，多舉眾應之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor and Yuan Shao had long faced each other at Guandu; Shao sent Liu Bei to tour the counties along the Yin River region, and many raised hosts in response.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao and Yuan Shao glared at each other across the Guandu lines, Shao detached Liu Bei to sweep the counties south of the Yin, and town after town rose at his call.

sentences.zh: 自许以南，吏民不安，太祖以爲憂。

translations.literal: From Xu southward officials and commoners were uneasy, and the Grand Progenitor took it as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: South of Xu the countryside was in turmoil, and the unrest weighed on Cao Cao’s mind.

sentences.zh: 仁曰：「南方以大軍方有目前急，其勢不能相救，劉備以彊兵临之，其背叛固宜也。

translations.literal: Ren said: “In the south the great army has the crisis before its eyes and cannot shift strength to rescue them; Liu Bei presses them with a strong host; for them to turn rebel is indeed to be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Ren argued, “The southerners know our main force is pinned here and cannot march to their aid. Liu Bei is leaning on them with a heavy army, so of course they are tempted to defect.

sentences.zh: 備新將紹兵，未能得其用，擊之可破也。」

translations.literal: Bei has newly taken command of Shao’s troops and has not yet been able to employ them properly; if we strike him we can break him.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei has only just inherited Yuan Shao’s men; he has not welded them into a weapon. Hit him now and he will shatter.”

sentences.zh: 太祖善其言，遂使將騎擊備，破走之，仁盡復收諸叛縣而還。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved his words, then had him lead cavalry to strike Bei, defeated and drove him off, and Ren wholly recovered the various rebel counties and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed, gave Ren the cavalry, and sent him against Liu Bei. Ren broke his line, chased him off, and brought every mutinous county back under the flag.

sentences.zh: 紹遣别將韓荀钞斷西道，仁擊荀於鸡洛山，大破之。

translations.literal: Shao sent a separate general Han Xun to raid and cut the western supply road; Ren struck Xun at Mount Jiluo and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao ordered Han Xun to sever the western convoy route; Ren intercepted him on Mount Jiluo and tore his command apart.

sentences.zh: 由是紹不敢復分兵出。

translations.literal: On this account Shao no longer dared to divide his troops and send them out.
translations.idiomatic: After that Yuan Shao never again risked splitting his army for side operations.

sentences.zh: 復與史渙等钞紹运车，燒其糧穀。

translations.literal: Again with Shi Huan and others he raided Shao’s transport wagons and burned his grain.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Shi Huan in another sweep against Yuan Shao’s grain carts and put the stores to the torch.

sentences.zh: 河北既定，從圍壶關。

translations.literal: When the region north of the Yellow River was settled, he followed in besieging Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Hebei plain was secure, he took part in the siege of Huguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 太祖令曰：「城拔，皆坑之。」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor issued an order: “When the city is taken, bury everyone alive in the pit.”
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao’s order was blunt: “When the walls fall, put the entire population to the sword.”

sentences.zh: 連月不下。

translations.literal: For successive months it did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Month after month the assault failed to crack the defenses.

sentences.zh: 仁言於太祖曰：「圍城必示之活門，所以开其生路也。

translations.literal: Ren spoke to the Grand Progenitor: “When you besiege a city you must show the defenders a gate of life; that is how you open a road for them to choose survival.
translations.idiomatic: Ren urged Cao Cao, “A siege needs a face-saving exit; only then will the garrison think surrender is possible.

sentences.zh: 今公告之必死，將人自爲守。

translations.literal: Now if the lord announces to them certain death, every man will fight for his own survival.
translations.idiomatic: Tell them they are already as good as dead and every household will barricade itself for a last stand.

sentences.zh: 且城固而糧多，攻之則士卒傷，守之則引日久；

translations.literal: Moreover the walls are strong and grain plentiful; if we attack then the soldiers will be wounded; if we hold siege then the days will stretch on;
translations.idiomatic: The fort is high, the granaries deep: storming it will bleed us white, while sitting tight only stretches the calendar;

sentences.zh: 今顿兵堅城之下，以攻必死之虜，非良計也。」

translations.literal: now to halt troops beneath a stubborn rampart and throw them against enemies who are sure to die is not a good plan.”
translations.idiomatic: and freezing an army under a sheer citadel to batter men who believe they have nothing left to lose is poor generalship.”

sentences.zh: 太祖從之，城降。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor followed him, and the city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took the advice; the city opened its gates.

sentences.zh: 於是錄仁前後功，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ren’s achievements before and after were recorded and he was enfeoffed as village marquis of the metropolitan enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: His whole record of service was entered in the rolls and he received the village marquisate at the metropolitan enclosure.

sentences.zh: 從平荆州，以仁行征南將軍，留屯江陵，拒吴將周瑜。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Jing province; Ren was appointed acting general who campaigns south, was left to encamp at Jiangling, and resisted Wu general Zhou Yu.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Jing province he was named acting general of the southern expedition, left to hold Jiangling against Wu’s Zhou Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑜將數萬眾來攻，前鋒數千人始至，仁登城望之，乃募得三百人，遣部曲將牛金逆與挑戰。

translations.literal: Yu led several tens of thousands to attack; when several thousand of the van had just arrived, Ren ascended the wall and looked out, then recruited three hundred men and sent his retainers’ commander Niu Jin to go oppose and challenge them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu came up the river with tens of thousands; only the van had closed to the walls when Ren climbed the parapet, scraped together three hundred volunteers, and ordered his client officer Niu Jin to ride out and provoke a fight.

sentences.zh: 賊多，金眾少，遂爲所圍。

translations.literal: The bandits were many and Jin’s force small, so he was surrounded by them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy swarmed while Jin’s handful was swallowed in their midst.

sentences.zh: 長史陳矫俱在城上，望見金等垂沒，左右皆失色。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Chen Jiao was together on the city wall; seeing Jin and others about to be overwhelmed, those on his left and right all changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Chen Jiao stood beside him on the tower; as Niu Jin’s detachment sank beneath the odds, every face on the wall went grey.

sentences.zh: 仁意氣奮怒甚，謂左右取馬來，矫等共援持之。

translations.literal: Ren’s spirit was greatly roused with fury; he told those on his left and right to bring a horse; Jiao and others together seized and restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren flushed with battle fury and shouted for his horse; Chen Jiao and the staff grabbed his arms to hold him back.

sentences.zh: 謂仁曰：「賊眾盛，不可當也。

translations.literal: They said to Ren: “The bandits’ multitude is great; they cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: They pleaded, “The odds are impossible—no one could stand against that mass.

sentences.zh: 假使棄數百人何苦，而將軍以身赴之！」

translations.literal: Even if several hundred men were lost, what hardship would it be, yet the general would go in person to them!”
translations.idiomatic: What is the loss of a few hundred foot compared with throwing yourself into their teeth?”

sentences.zh: 仁不應，遂被甲上馬，將其麾下壯士數十騎出城。
