translations.literal: Ren did not answer, then donned armor, mounted a horse, and led several tens of picked horsemen of his command out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ren said nothing, strapped on his armor, swung into the saddle, and led a few dozen picked horsemen out through the gate.

sentences.zh: 去賊百餘步，迫沟，矫等以爲仁當住沟上，爲金形勢也，仁径渡沟直前，衝入賊圍，金等乃得解。

translations.literal: He came within a hundred paces of the bandits, pressed near a ditch; Jiao and others thought Ren would stop at the ditch to create a posture for Jin, but Ren crossed the ditch straight forward, charged into the bandit encirclement, and Jin and others then obtained relief.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred paces from the enemy line he reached a dry moat; Chen Jiao assumed he would halt on the near bank to screen Niu Jin, but Ren splashed straight across, rammed the ring of spears, and tore the noose open around Jin.

sentences.zh: 餘眾未盡出，仁復直還突之，拔出金兵，亡其數人，賊眾乃退。

translations.literal: The rest of the host had not all come out; Ren again charged straight back into them, extricated Jin’s troops, lost several of his own men, and the bandit multitude then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rest of his squad could follow, he wheeled and charged back through the melee, pulled Niu Jin’s men clear at the cost of a few lives, and the besiegers fell back.

sentences.zh: 矫等初見仁出，皆懼，及見仁還，乃叹曰：「將軍真天人也！」

translations.literal: When Jiao and others first saw Ren go out, they all were afraid; when they saw Ren return, they sighed and said: “The general is truly a man of Heaven!”
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiao had watched him ride out in horror; when he watched him ride home again he murmured, “That man belongs to another order of being!”

sentences.zh: 三軍服其勇。

translations.literal: The three armies admired his courage.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army stood in awe of his courage.

sentences.zh: 太祖益壯之，轉封安平亭侯。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor increasingly esteemed him and transferred his fief to village marquis of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao admired him all the more and moved his title to the village marquisate of Anping.

sentences.zh: 太祖討馬超，以仁行安西將軍，督諸將拒潼關，破超渭南。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor punished Ma Chao, he appointed Ren acting general who pacifies the west, supervised the generals in resisting Tong Pass, and defeated Chao south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Ma Chao he served as acting general of the western pacification, directed the defense of Tong Pass, and helped break Ma Chao on the south bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 苏伯、田银反，以仁行骁騎將軍，都督七軍討银等，破之。

translations.literal: Su Bo and Tian Yin rebelled; Ren was appointed acting general of swift cavalry, supervised the seven armies in punishing Yin and others, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Bo and Tian Yin rose in the north, Ren took the acting post of swift-cavalry general, commanded seven columns against them, and crushed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 復以仁行征南將軍，假節，屯樊，鎮荆州。

translations.literal: Again Ren was appointed acting general who campaigns south, was given the credentials of office, encamped at Fan, and guarded Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named acting general of the southern expedition, invested with formal baton, and stationed at Fan to anchor Jing province.

sentences.zh: 侯音以宛叛，略傍縣眾數千人，仁率諸軍攻破音，斬其首，還屯樊，即拜征南將軍。

translations.literal: Hou Yin rebelled with Wan, plundered several thousand of the neighboring counties’ people; Ren led the various armies to break Yin, beheaded him, returned to encamp at Fan, and was immediately appointed general who campaigns south.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yin seized Wan and dragged thousands from the neighboring districts into revolt; Ren led the combined hosts against him, took his head, returned to Fan, and was confirmed as full general of the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 關羽攻樊，時漢水暴溢，于禁等七軍皆沒，禁降羽。

translations.literal: Guan Yu attacked Fan; at that time the Han River suddenly overflowed; Yu Jin and the seven armies were all submerged, and Jin surrendered to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Yu closed on Fan, the Han burst its banks; Yu Jin’s seven armies were drowned in a night, and Yu Jin himself capitulated to Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 仁人馬數千人守城，城不沒者數板。

translations.literal: Ren had several thousand men and horses defending the city; only a few courses of the wall remained above the water.
translations.idiomatic: Ren held the town with a few thousand men while the flood lapped within a few planks of the parapet.

sentences.zh: 羽乘船临城，圍數重，外内斷絕，糧食欲盡，救兵不至。

translations.literal: Yu sailed boats up to the city, encircled it in several layers, inner and outer were cut off, provisions were about exhausted, and relief troops did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu brought war junks against the walls, ringed the city in depth, severed every line in or out, starved the garrison to the edge, and still no relief column appeared.

sentences.zh: 仁激厉將士，示以必死，將士感之皆無二。

translations.literal: Ren exhorted the officers and troops, showed them they must die, and the officers and troops were moved and had no second thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Ren harangued his officers, swore they would die where they stood, and the men answered him with a single will.

sentences.zh: 徐晃救至，水亦稍减，晃從外擊羽，仁得溃圍出，羽退走。

translations.literal: When Xu Huang’s relief arrived, the water also gradually fell; Huang struck Yu from outside, Ren was able to break the encirclement and get out, and Yu withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Huang’s corps finally fought its way in, the flood began to ebb; Huang hammered Guan Yu from the rear while Ren punched out of the ring, and Guan Yu drew off.

sentences.zh: 仁少時不脩行检，及長爲將，嚴整奉法令，常置科於左右，案以從事。

translations.literal: Ren in youth did not cultivate conduct and discipline; when grown as a general he was strict and orderly in upholding laws and commands, always kept regulations at his side, and judged cases accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Cao Ren was unruly, but once he took command he enforced the code rigorously, kept regulations at hand, and judged every infraction by the book.

sentences.zh: 鄢陵侯彰北征烏丸，文帝在東宫，爲書戒彰曰：「爲將奉法，不當如征南邪！」

translations.literal: Marquis of Yanling Zhang campaigned north against the Wuhuan; Emperor Wen was in the Eastern Palace and wrote a letter admonishing Zhang saying: "As a general upholding law, ought you not be like the general who campaigns south!"
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Yanling Cao Zhang marched north against the Wuhuan, Crown Prince Wen wrote warning him: "A general who upholds the law should take his cue from the southern expedition commander!"

sentences.zh: 及即王位，拜仁车騎將軍，都督荆、揚、益州諸軍事，進封陳侯，增邑二千，并前三千五百户。

translations.literal: When he took the royal throne, he appointed Ren General of Chariots and Cavalry, supervisor of military affairs for Jing, Yang, and Yi provinces, advanced him to Marquis of Chen, added two thousand households to his fief, making three thousand five hundred households in all with the previous.
translations.idiomatic: On taking the royal throne he named Ren General of Chariots and Cavalry, gave him overall command of Jing, Yang, and Yi, promoted him to Marquis of Chen, and added 2,000 households to his fief for a total of 3,500.

sentences.zh: 追賜仁父炽諡曰陳穆侯，置守冢十家。

translations.literal: He posthumously bestowed on Ren's father Chi the posthumous title Marquis Mu of Chen and established ten households to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He canonized Ren's father Cao Chi as Marquis Mu of Chen and assigned ten families to tend the tomb.

sentences.zh: 後召還屯宛。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned back to encamp at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled to garrison Wan.

sentences.zh: 孫權遣將陳邵据襄陽，詔仁討之。

translations.literal: Sun Quan sent General Chen Shao to hold Xiangyang; an edict ordered Ren to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan detached Chen Shao to seize Xiangyang, and an edict sent Cao Ren against him.

sentences.zh: 仁與徐晃攻破邵，遂入襄陽，使將軍高遷等徙漢南附化民於漢北，文帝遣使即拜仁大將軍。

translations.literal: Ren together with Xu Huang broke Shao, then entered Xiangyang, had General Gao Qian and others move the people who had submitted in the south of the Han to the north of the Han; Emperor Wen sent envoys and immediately appointed Ren grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren and Xu Huang routed Chen Shao, recovered Xiangyang, resettled submitted peoples from south of the Han to the north, and Emperor Wen's envoys promptly named Ren grand general.

sentences.zh: 又詔仁移屯临潁，遷大司馬，復督諸軍据烏江，還屯合肥。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered Ren to move encampment to Linying, transferred him to Grand Marshal, again supervised the armies in holding Wujiang, and returned to encamp at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to Linying, promoted to Grand Marshal, again given overall command to hold the line at Wujiang, and finally garrisoned Hefei.

sentences.zh: 黃初四年薨，諡曰忠侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangchu he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Huangchu 4 and was canonized as Marquis Zhong (the Loyal).

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：仁時年五十六。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei says: Ren was then fifty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei gives his age as fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 《傅子》曰：曹大司馬之勇，賁、育弗加也。

translations.literal: Master Fu says: Cao the Grand Marshal's courage—Ben and Yu could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu wrote that Grand Marshal Cao's valor exceeded even the legendary strongmen Ben and Yu.

sentences.zh: 張辽其次焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Liao was next to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao ranked second.

sentences.zh: 子泰嗣，官至鎮東將軍，假節，轉封甯陵侯。

translations.literal: His son Tai succeeded, reached the post of General Who Guards the East, was given credentials of office, and was transferred and enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tai inherited, rose to General Who Guards the East with baton of command, and was shifted to Marquis of Ningling.

sentences.zh: 泰薨，子初嗣。

translations.literal: Tai died; his son Chu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai died his son Chu inherited.

sentences.zh: 又分封泰弟楷、範，皆爲列侯，而牛金官至後將軍。

translations.literal: Again Tai's younger brothers Kai and Fan were separately enfeoffed, both becoming ranked marquises, while Niu Jin reached the post of General of the Rear.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's brothers Kai and Fan were also enfeoffed as marquises, and Niu Jin rose to General of the Rear.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：純字子和。

translations.literal: 〈The Records of Heroes states: Chun’s courtesy name was Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yingxiong ji records that he bore the courtesy name Zihe.

sentences.zh: 年十四而喪父，與同產兄仁别居。

translations.literal: At fourteen he lost his father and lived separately from his full elder brother Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at fourteen, he set up his own household apart from his elder brother Ren.

sentences.zh: 承父業，富於財，僮僕人客以百數，純纲紀督御，不失其理，鄉里咸以爲能。

translations.literal: He inherited his father’s estate, was rich in wealth, with retainers, servants, and guests numbering in the hundreds; Chun directed and controlled them without losing order, and his village and district all deemed him capable.
translations.idiomatic: He took over the family fortune, kept hundreds of retainers and clients in hand, and ran the household so tightly that neighbors praised his competence.

sentences.zh: 好學問，敬愛學士，學士多歸焉，由是爲遠近所稱。

translations.literal: He loved learning, respected and loved scholars, and many scholars came to him; on this account he was praised far and near.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books, honored men of learning, and drew scholars from every quarter until his name was known for counties around.

sentences.zh: 年十八，爲黄門侍郎。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he entered the palace as a gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 二十，從太祖到襄邑募兵，遂常從征戰。〉

translations.literal: At twenty he followed the Grand Progenitor to Xiangyi to recruit soldiers, and thereafter constantly followed on campaigns.〉
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he rode with Cao Cao to Xiangyi to raise troops, and from then on he was seldom absent from the field.〉

sentences.zh: 初以議郎参司空軍事，督虎豹騎從圍南皮。

translations.literal: At first as gentleman consultant he joined the office of the minister of works in military affairs, supervised the Tiger and Leopard Cavalry, and followed in besieging Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a gentleman consultant on the staff of the minister of works, took charge of the Tiger and Leopard Cavalry, and joined the siege of Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 袁譚出戰，士卒多死。

translations.literal: Yuan Tan came out to fight; many of the soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan sallied from the walls and the assault troops took heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲缓之，純曰：「今千里蹈敵，進不能克，退必喪威；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wished to slow the attack; Chun said: “Now we have marched a thousand li upon the foe; if we advance and cannot conquer, in retreat we are sure to lose prestige;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wanted to pause the attack; Chun warned, “We have marched a thousand li onto enemy soil: if we slacken the pressure we lose face,

sentences.zh: 且縣師深入，難以持久。

translations.literal: moreover a detached army deep in enemy territory is hard to maintain long.
translations.idiomatic: and a lone column this deep cannot sit idle forever.

sentences.zh: 彼勝而骄，我敗而懼，以懼敵骄，必可克也。」

translations.literal: They are victorious and therefore arrogant; we are beaten and therefore fearful; using fear against arrogance, we can surely conquer.”
translations.idiomatic: They are flush with victory and already careless; we are smarting from a check and therefore cautious—pit a wary army against a cocky one and we can still win.”

sentences.zh: 太祖善其言，遂急攻之，譚敗。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved his words, then pressed the attack urgently, and Tan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed, redoubled the assault, and broke Yuan Tan’s line.

sentences.zh: 純麾下騎斬譚首。

translations.literal: Chun’s cavalry under his command beheaded Tan.
translations.idiomatic: A trooper of Chun’s Tiger and Leopard riders struck off Yuan Tan’s head.

sentences.zh: 及北征三郡，純部騎获单於蹹顿。

translations.literal: When he campaigned north against the three commanderies, Chun’s cavalry detachment captured the Chanyu Tadun.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern expedition against the Wuhuan league, Chun’s horsemen ran down the chanyu Tadun.

sentences.zh: 以前後功封高陵亭侯，邑三百户。

translations.literal: For achievements before and after he was enfeoffed village marquis of Gaoling, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His cumulative merit earned the village marquisate of Gaoling with three hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 從征荆州，追劉備於長坂，获其二女輜重，收其散卒。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Jing province, pursued Liu Bei at Changban, captured his two daughters and baggage train, and gathered his scattered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the drive on Jing province he chased Liu Bei through Changban, seized the two princesses and the baggage train, and scooped up stragglers by the hundred.

sentences.zh: 進降江陵，從還譙。

translations.literal: He advanced and reduced Jiangling to submission, then followed in returning to Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to accept Jiangling’s surrender, then marched home with the army to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 建安十五年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifteenth year of Jian’an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of the Jian’an era.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，追諡曰威侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he posthumously bestowed the title marquis awe-inspiring (Wei).
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the throne he canonized him as Marquis Wei, “the Formidable.”

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：純所督虎豹騎，皆天下骁锐，或從百人將补之，太祖難其帥。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei states: The Tiger and Leopard Cavalry that Chun commanded were all the finest fighters under heaven; some were promoted from commanders of a hundred men, and the Grand Progenitor found it hard to pick a commander for them.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu notes that Chun’s Tiger and Leopard riders were picked champions from every army, often promoted from centurions, so that Cao Cao despaired of finding a worthy colonel for them.

sentences.zh: 純以选爲督，抚循甚得人心。

translations.literal: Chun was chosen as commander and in comforting and handling them won their hearts completely.
translations.idiomatic: Chun won the post by selection and led them with such tact that the corps would have followed him anywhere.

sentences.zh: 及卒，有司白选代，太祖曰：「純之比，何可復得！

translations.literal: When he died, the responsible officials reported the need to choose a successor; the Grand Progenitor said: “A match for Chun—how could one be found again!
translations.idiomatic: After his death the ministry proposed a replacement; Cao Cao snapped, “Where am I to find another man like Chun?

sentences.zh: 吾獨不中督邪？」

translations.literal: Am I alone unfit to serve as commander?”
translations.idiomatic: Am I myself unfit to command them?”

sentences.zh: 遂不选。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon none was chosen.〉
translations.idiomatic: No successor was named.〉

sentences.zh: 子演嗣，官至領軍將軍，正元中進封平樂鄉侯。

translations.literal: His son Yan succeeded; his office reached general who commands the army; in the Zhengyuan era he advanced to marquis of the village of Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan inherited the title, rose to general of the central army, and in the Zhengyuan period was advanced to marquis of Pingle village.

sentences.zh: 演薨，子亮嗣。

translations.literal: Yan died; his son Liang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan died, his son Liang became heir.

sentences.zh: 曹洪字子廉，太祖從弟也。

translations.literal: Cao Hong, courtesy name Zikang, was a younger cousin of the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong, styled Zikang, was a younger cousin of Cao Cao on his father's side.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：洪伯父鼎爲尚書令，任洪爲蕲春長。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Hong's paternal uncle Ding was director of the masters of writing and appointed Hong magistrate of Qichun.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu states that Hong's uncle Ding served as director of the masters of writing and secured him the post of Qichun magistrate.

sentences.zh: 太祖起義兵討董卓，至荥陽，爲卓將徐榮所敗。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor raised righteous troops to punish Dong Zhuo, he reached Xingyang and was defeated by Zhuo's general Xu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched against Dong Zhuo, he was routed at Xingyang by Dong Zhuo's general Xu Rong.

sentences.zh: 太祖失馬，賊追甚急，洪下，以馬授太祖，太祖辞讓，洪曰：「天下可無洪，不可無君。」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor lost his horse; the enemy pressed close in pursuit. Hong dismounted and offered his horse to the Grand Progenitor. The Grand Progenitor declined, and Hong said, "The realm can do without Hong; it cannot do without my lord."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao lost his mount with pursuers closing in. Hong leapt down and thrust the reins into his cousin's hand. Cao Cao refused; Hong insisted, "The world can spare me—it cannot spare you."

sentences.zh: 遂步從到汴水，水深不得渡，洪循水得船，與太祖俱濟，還奔譙。

translations.literal: They then went on foot after him to the Bian River. The water was deep and could not be crossed. Hong followed the bank until he found a boat, crossed together with the Grand Progenitor, and fled back to Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on foot to the Bian River, where the flood was too deep to ford. Hong scouted the bank, found a boat, ferried Cao Cao across, and they raced back to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史陳温素與洪善，洪將家兵千餘人，就温募兵，得廬江上甲二千人，東到丹楊復得數千人，與太祖會龍亢。

translations.literal: Chen Wen, inspector of Yang province, had long been on good terms with Hong. Hong led more than a thousand household troops, went to Wen to raise soldiers, obtained two thousand first-rate troops from Lujiang, and when he went east to Danyang obtained several thousand more, then joined the Grand Progenitor at Longkang.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Chen Wen of Yang province was an old friend. Hong marched with a thousand-odd household retainers, raised two thousand crack troops from Lujiang through Wen, gathered thousands more in Danyang, and rejoined Cao Cao at Longkang.

sentences.zh: 太祖征徐州，張邈舉兖州叛迎吕布。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Xu province, Zhang Miao raised Yan province in rebellion and welcomed Lü Bu.
translations.idiomatic: During Cao Cao's campaign against Xu province, Zhang Miao turned Yan province over to Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 時大饑荒，洪將兵在前，先据東平、範，聚糧穀以繼軍。

translations.literal: At the time there was great famine. Hong led troops in the van, first seized Dongping and Fan, and gathered grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the land. Hong pushed ahead, seized Dongping and Fan, and stockpiled grain to keep the host fed.

sentences.zh: 太祖討邈、布於濮陽，布破走，遂据東阿，轉擊濟陰、山陽、中牟、陽武、京、密十餘縣，皆拔之。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor attacked Miao and Bu at Puyang, Bu was broken and fled. Hong then seized Dong'e, turned to strike Jiyin, Shanyang, Zhongmou, Yangwu, Jing, Mi, and more than ten counties, and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: At Puyang Cao Cao shattered Lü Bu's force; Hong then held Dong'e and swept more than ten counties—Jiyin, Shanyang, Zhongmou, Yangwu, Jing, Mi, and others—clearing them one by one.

sentences.zh: 以前後功拜鹰揚校尉，遷揚武中郎將。

translations.literal: For his successive merits he was appointed colonel who soars and strikes, then promoted to martial might general of the household guards.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he was made colonel of the soaring hawk, then promoted to martial might general of the household guards.

sentences.zh: 天子都许，拜洪諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven made his capital at Xu, Hong was appointed remonstrating and consulting grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor moved the court to Xu, Hong received the post of remonstrating and consulting grandee.

sentences.zh: 别征劉表，破表别將於舞陽、陰葉、堵陽、博望，有功，遷厉鋒將軍，封國明亭侯。

translations.literal: On a separate campaign against Liu Biao he defeated Biao's detached generals at Wuyang, Yinye, Duyang, and Bowang. For his merit he was promoted to general who displays the keen edge and enfeoffed as village marquis of Guoming.
translations.idiomatic: On detached service against Liu Biao he crushed Biao's lieutenants at Wuyang, Yinye, Duyang, and Bowang, won promotion to general of the keen edge, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Guoming.

sentences.zh: 累從征伐，拜都護將軍。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed on campaigns and was appointed chief protector general.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign after campaign he followed the colors, until he was named chief protector general.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，爲衛將軍，遷骠騎將軍，進封野王侯，益邑千户，并前二千一百户，位特進；

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Hong became general of the guards, was transferred to general of swift cavalry, advanced in fief to marquis of Yewang, had his fief increased by a thousand households to a total of twenty-one hundred with the previous holdings, and was given the eminent position of special advancement;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen made him general of the guards, then general of swift cavalry, advanced his fief to marquis of Yewang with a thousand added households for twenty-one hundred in all, and granted him the eminent rank of special advancement;

sentences.zh: 後徙封都陽侯。

translations.literal: later his fief was moved to marquis of Duyang.
translations.idiomatic: later his fief was transferred to marquis of Duyang.

sentences.zh: 始，洪家富而性吝啬，文帝少時假求不稱，常恨之，遂以舍客犯法，下狱當死。

translations.literal: At the beginning Hong's family was wealthy yet his nature was stingy. When Emperor Wen was young he borrowed from him and was not satisfied, and he often resented this. Thereupon on the charge that a retainer had violated the law he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had been rich and notoriously tight-fisted. The young Cao Pi had borrowed from him and been refused; the grudge lingered. When a guest of Hong's broke the law, Pi seized the chance to have him jailed and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 羣臣并救莫能得。

translations.literal: The ministers all pleaded together but could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court interceded, yet none could move the throne.

sentences.zh: 卞太后謂郭后曰：「令曹洪今日死，吾明日敕帝废后矣。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Bian said to Empress Guo, "If Cao Hong dies today, tomorrow I shall order the emperor to depose you as empress."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bian told Empress Guo, "Let Cao Hong die today, and tomorrow I shall command the emperor to depose you."

sentences.zh: 於是泣涕屡請，乃得免官削爵土。

translations.literal: Thereupon with tears she repeatedly pleaded, and he was spared execution but stripped of office and fief.
translations.idiomatic: She wept and pleaded again and again until Hong was spared the blade but stripped of rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：文帝收洪，時曹真在左右，請之曰：「今誅洪，洪必以真爲譖也。」

translations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei states: When Emperor Wen seized Hong, Cao Zhen was at his side and pleaded for him, saying, "If Hong is executed now, Hong will surely think that Zhen slandered him."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe records that when Emperor Wen arrested Hong, Cao Zhen stood at his side and warned, "Execute Hong now, and he will believe I denounced him."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我自治之，卿何豫也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I shall handle this myself—what business is it of yours?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "I will judge this myself—what is that to you?"

sentences.zh: 會卞太后責怒帝，言「梁、沛之間，非子廉無有今日」。

translations.literal: Just then Empress Dowager Bian rebuked the emperor in anger, saying, "Between Liang and Pei, but for Zikang there would be no today."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bian then rebuked the emperor: "Between Liang and Pei, without Zikang there would be no you on the throne today."

sentences.zh: 詔乃釋之。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict at last set him free.

sentences.zh: 猶尚沒入其財產。

translations.literal: His property was nevertheless confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Even so his estates were seized.

sentences.zh: 太后又以爲言，後乃還之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager spoke again on his behalf, and afterward they were returned.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager spoke again, and in time his property was restored.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖爲司空時，以己率下，每歲发调，使本縣平赀。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the Grand Progenitor was minister of works, he led subordinates by his own example; each year when levies were issued he had the native county assess property equally.
translations.idiomatic: In Cao Cao's days as minister of works he set the tone from the top: each year's levy was assessed by the home county on an equal-property basis.

sentences.zh: 於時譙令平洪赀財與公家等，太祖曰：「我家赀那得如子廉耶！」

translations.literal: At that time the magistrate of Qiao assessed Hong's property as equal to the public household's, and the Grand Progenitor said, "How could my family's wealth match Zikang's!"
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Qiao rated Hong's wealth equal to the state's own holdings, and Cao Cao laughed, "How could our household ever equal Zikang's!"

sentences.zh: 文帝在東宫，尝從洪贷绢百匹，洪不稱意。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was in the eastern palace he once borrowed a hundred bolts of silk from Hong and was not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Cao Pi once borrowed a hundred bolts of silk from Hong and found the gift wanting.

sentences.zh: 及洪犯法，自分必死，既得原，喜，上書谢曰：「臣少不由道，过在人伦，長窃非任，遂蒙含贷。

translations.literal: When Hong violated the law he reckoned he would surely die. Once pardoned he rejoiced and submitted a memorial of thanks, saying, "Your servant in youth did not follow the Way; faults lay in human relations. For long I usurped an unfitting post and then received gracious pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong fell afoul of the law he was sure he would die. Spared, he submitted a grateful memorial: "In youth I strayed from the Way and failed in my duties. Long I held office I did not deserve, yet was shown mercy.

sentences.zh: 性無检度知足之分，而有豺狼無厌之質，老惛倍贪，触突國网，罪迫三千，不在赦宥，當就辜誅，棄諸市朝，猶蒙天恩，骨肉更生。

translations.literal: My nature lacks the sense of restraint and contentment, yet has the quality of a wolf that knows no satiety. In old age I am doubly muddled and greedy, and I have struck against the laws of the state. My offenses approach three thousand and lie outside amnesty; I ought to suffer execution and be cast out in the marketplace. Yet I still receive Heaven's grace, and flesh and bone are reborn.
translations.idiomatic: I never knew moderation, only the hunger of a wolf. Age made me greedier still, and I crashed into the law. My crimes approach three thousand counts and lie beyond pardon; I should die at the execution ground. Yet Heaven spared me, and bone and flesh live again.

sentences.zh: 臣仰视天日，愧負靈神，俯惟愆阙，惭愧怖悸，不能雉經以自裁割，谨涂颜阙門，拜章陳情。」

translations.literal: Your servant looks up at sun and sky and bears shame before the numinous spirits; looking down on my faults I am ashamed, fearful, and trembling. I cannot hang myself to cut off my own life, and so with face smeared in disgrace I come to your gate and bow in memorial to state my feelings."
translations.idiomatic: I lift my eyes to sun and sky and shame the spirits; looking on my faults I am afraid and ashamed. I cannot take my own life by the cord, and so with smeared face I come to your gate and bow this memorial."

sentences.zh: 洪先帝功臣，時人多爲觖望。

translations.literal: Hong was a meritorious minister of the former emperor, and at the time many were discontented on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had been a pillar of the founding reign, and many at court resented his treatment.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，拜後將軍，更封樂城侯，邑千户，位特進，復拜骠騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Hong was appointed general of the rear, had his fief changed to marquis of Lecheng with a thousand households, was given the position of special advancement, and was again appointed general of swift cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming restored him as general of the rear, refiefed him as marquis of Lecheng with a thousand households, granted special advancement, and again named him general of swift cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太和六年232年薨，諡曰恭侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe (232) he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe 6 (232) and was posthumously titled Marquis Gong.

sentences.zh: 子馥，嗣侯。

translations.literal: His son Fu succeeded to the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖分洪户封子震列侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning the Grand Progenitor divided households from Hong's fief and enfeoffed his son Zhen as a full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cao Cao had carved households from Hong's fief to enfeoff his son Zhen as a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 洪族父瑜，脩慎笃敬，官至衛將軍，封列侯。

translations.literal: Hong's clansman-uncle Yu was cautious, respectful, and sincere in conduct, rose to general of the guards, and was enfeoffed as a full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's kinsman Yu was grave and dutiful, rose to general of the guards, and held a full marquisate.

sentences.zh: 曹休字文烈，太祖族子也。

translations.literal: Cao Xiu, courtesy name Wenlie, was a clansman son of the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu, styled Wenlie, was a clansman of Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 天下亂，宗族各散去鄉里。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into chaos the clans all scattered to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire collapsed, the clan scattered to their native places.

sentences.zh: 休年十餘歲，喪父，獨與一客担喪假葬，携將老母，渡江至吴。

translations.literal: Xiu was just over ten when his father died. Alone with one guest he shouldered the coffin for a provisional burial, then took his aged mother and crossed the river to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was barely into his teens when his father died. With a single companion he shouldered the coffin for a makeshift burial, then crossed the Yangzi with his mother to Wu.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：休祖父尝爲吴郡太守。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Xiu's grandfather had once been grand administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu states that Xiu's grandfather had once governed Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 休於太守舍，見壁上祖父画像，下榻拜涕泣，同坐者皆嘉叹焉。

translations.literal: At the grand administrator's residence Xiu saw his grandfather's portrait on the wall, came down from the couch, bowed, and wept; those seated with him all praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: In the governor's hall he saw his grandfather's portrait on the wall, rose from his seat, bowed, and wept until all present sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 以太祖舉義兵，易姓名轉至荆州，間行北歸，見太祖。

translations.literal: Because the Grand Progenitor had raised righteous troops, he changed his name and made his way to Jing province, traveled secretly north, and saw the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao raised his banner, Xiu changed his name, slipped through Jing province, and made his way north in secret to join him.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂左右曰：「此吾家千里驹也。」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said to those at his side, "This is a thousand-league colt of our house."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told his attendants, "Here is a thousand-league colt of our clan."

sentences.zh: 使與文帝同止，見待如子。

translations.literal: He had him lodge with Emperor Wen and treated him like a son.
translations.idiomatic: He lodged him with the heir apparent and treated him as a son.

sentences.zh: 常從征伐，使領虎豹騎宿衛。

translations.literal: He often followed on campaigns and was made to lead the tiger-and-leopard cavalry as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rode on campaign after campaign and was set to command the tiger-and-leopard cavalry as palace guard.

sentences.zh: 劉備遣將吴兰屯下辯，太祖遣曹洪征之，以休爲騎都尉，参洪軍事。

translations.literal: Liu Bei sent the general Wu Lan to encamp at Xiabian. The Grand Progenitor sent Cao Hong to campaign against him and made Xiu colonel of cavalry to take part in Hong's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei posted Wu Lan at Xiabian, Cao Cao sent Cao Hong against him and attached Xiu as colonel of cavalry on Hong's staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂休曰：「汝雖参軍，其實帥也。」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor told Xiu, "Though you are staff officer, in truth you are commander."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told Xiu, "You hold the title of staff officer, but in truth you are the commander."

sentences.zh: 洪聞此令，亦委事於休。

translations.literal: When Hong heard this order he also entrusted affairs to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that, Hong handed the real command to Xiu.

sentences.zh: 備遣張飛屯固山，欲斷軍後。

translations.literal: Bei sent Zhang Fei to encamp at Gushan, intending to cut off the army's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei to Gushan, aiming to sever the army's line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 眾議狐疑，休曰：「賊實斷道者，當伏兵潜行。

translations.literal: In council many were doubtful. Xiu said, "If the enemy truly meant to cut the road they would have lain in ambush and moved in secret.
translations.idiomatic: The staff wavered. Xiu said, "Men who mean to cut a road move in ambush and silence.

sentences.zh: 今乃先張声勢，此其不能也。

translations.literal: Now they have first made a great show of force—this shows they cannot do it.
translations.idiomatic: They have blared their intentions first—they cannot do it.

sentences.zh: 宜及其未集，促擊兰，兰破則飛自走矣。」

translations.literal: We ought to strike Lan before they gather, and when Lan is broken Fei will flee of himself."
translations.idiomatic: Strike Lan before they mass; once Lan falls, Fei will run on his own."

sentences.zh: 洪從之，進兵擊兰，大破之，飛果走。

translations.literal: Hong followed this plan, advanced and struck Lan, and broke him greatly; Fei indeed fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hong agreed, attacked Lan, and routed him; Zhang Fei fled as predicted.

sentences.zh: 太祖拔漢中，諸軍還長安，拜休中領軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor took Hanzhong the various armies returned to Chang'an, and Xiu was appointed central leader of the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanzhong fell and the armies withdrew to Chang'an, Xiu was named central leader of the army.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，爲領軍將軍，錄前後功，封東陽亭侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingship, Xiu became general of the leader of the army, his earlier and later merits were recorded, and he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the kingship, Xiu became general of the leader of the army, his services were entered on the rolls, and he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 夏侯惇薨，以休爲鎮南將軍，假節都督諸軍事，车驾临送，上乃下舆執手而别。

translations.literal: When Xiahou Dun died, Xiu was made general who guards the south, given the credential and made supervisor of all military affairs. The imperial carriage came to see him off; the emperor descended from the carriage, took his hand, and parted.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiahou Dun's death Xiu was made general who guards the south with credential and overall command. The emperor came in person to send him off, stepped down from the carriage, took his hand, and bade farewell.

sentences.zh: 孫權遣將屯歷陽，休到，擊破之，又别遣兵渡江，燒賊芜湖營數千家。

translations.literal: Sun Quan sent a general to encamp at Liyang. When Xiu arrived he defeated him, and separately sent troops across the river to burn several thousand households in the enemy camp at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan posted a force at Liyang; Xiu broke it, then sent troops across the river to burn thousands of enemy shelters at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 遷征東將軍，領揚州刺史，進封安陽鄉侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to general who campaigns east, concurrently inspector of Yang province, and advanced in fief to village marquis of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who campaigns east and inspector of Yang province, and advanced to village marquis of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：休喪母至孝。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: In mourning for his mother Xiu was supremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu says that in mourning his mother Xiu showed supreme filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 帝使侍中夺喪服，使饮酒食肉，休受詔而形体益憔悴。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an attendant-in-ordinary to take away his mourning garments and had him drink wine and eat meat. Xiu received the edict yet his body grew ever more wasted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an attendant to strip his mourning garb and ordered wine and meat; Xiu obeyed, yet wasted away.

sentences.zh: 乞歸譙葬母，帝復遣越騎校尉薛乔奉詔節其憂哀，使歸家治喪，一宿便葬，葬讫詣行在所。

translations.literal: He begged to return to Qiao to bury his mother. The emperor again sent Colonel of the Rapid Guard Xue Qiao with an edict to moderate his grief, let him return home to conduct the funeral, buried her after one night's rest, and when the burial was finished went to the emperor's traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave to bury his mother at Qiao. The emperor sent Colonel Xue Qiao to temper his grief, let him go home, buried her after a single night, and when the rites were done Xiu presented himself at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 帝見，親自宽慰之。

translations.literal: When the emperor saw him he personally comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him and comforted him in person.

sentences.zh: 其見愛重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the regard in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem he commanded.

sentences.zh: 帝征孫權，以休爲征東大將軍，假黄钺，督張辽等及諸州郡二十餘軍，擊權大將吕範等於洞浦，破之。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Sun Quan he made Xiu grand general who campaigns east, gave him the yellow battle-axe, and had him supervise Zhang Liao and more than twenty armies from the various provinces and commanderies. He struck Sun Quan's great general Lü Fan and others at Dongpu and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Sun Quan, the emperor named Xiu grand general who campaigns east, gave him the yellow battle-axe, and set him over Zhang Liao and more than twenty provincial hosts. At Dongpu he shattered Sun Quan's great general Lü Fan.

sentences.zh: 拜揚州牧。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，進封長平侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Xiu was advanced in fief to marquis of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming advanced his fief to marquis of Changping.

sentences.zh: 吴將审德屯皖，休擊破之，斬德首，吴將韓綜、翟丹等前後率眾詣休降。

translations.literal: Wu general Shen De encamped at Wan; Xiu defeated him and beheaded De. Wu generals Han Zong, Zhai Dan, and others before and after led their hosts to surrender to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu general Shen De held Wan; Xiu defeated him and took his head. Wu generals Han Zong, Zhai Dan, and others came over to him in succession.

sentences.zh: 增邑四百，并前二千五百户，遷大司馬，都督揚州如故。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by four hundred households to a total of twenty-five hundred with the previous holdings, and he was transferred to grand marshal while continuing to supervise Yang province as before.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred households were added to his fief for twenty-five hundred in all, and he was made grand marshal while retaining supervision of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 太和二年228年，帝爲二道征吴，遣司馬宣王從漢水下，〔休督〕諸軍向尋陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe (228) the emperor campaigned against Wu on two routes, sending Sima Yi down the Han River while [Xiu supervised] the various armies toward Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 (228) the emperor opened a two-pronged campaign against Wu, sending Sima Yi down the Han while Xiu led the main host toward Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 賊將僞降，休深入，戰不利，退還宿石亭。

translations.literal: An enemy general feigned surrender. Xiu advanced deep, the battle went badly, and he withdrew to lodge at Shiting.
translations.idiomatic: A Wu officer pretended to defect. Xiu pushed deep, met defeat, and fell back to Shiting.

sentences.zh: 軍夜惊，士卒亂，棄甲兵輜重甚多。

translations.literal: That night the army was startled; the soldiers fell into disorder and abandoned armor, weapons, and baggage in great quantity.
translations.idiomatic: That night panic swept the camp; troops threw away armor, arms, and wagons in heaps.

sentences.zh: 休上書谢罪，帝遣屯騎校尉楊暨慰谕，禮賜益隆。

translations.literal: Xiu submitted a memorial apologizing for his fault. The emperor sent Colonel of the Dappled Cavalry Yang Ji to console and instruct him, and his honors and gifts grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu submitted a confession of fault. The emperor sent Colonel Yang Ji to console him and heaped fresh honors upon him.

sentences.zh: 休因此痈发背薨，諡曰壯侯。

translations.literal: Xiu thereupon died of a carbuncle on his back; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: A carbuncle on his back killed him; he was posthumously titled Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子肇嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：肇字長思。

translations.literal: The Accounts of the Age states: Zhao's courtesy name was Changsi.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu records that Zhao's courtesy name was Changsi.

sentences.zh: 肇有當世才度，爲散騎常侍、屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: Zhao had the talent and measure of the age and served as attendant cavalier and colonel of the encampment cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had talent fit for his generation and served as attendant cavalier and colonel of the encampment cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明帝寝疾，方與燕王宇等屬以後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming lay gravely ill he was on the point of entrusting the succession to the Prince of Yan, Yu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Ming lay dying he was about to entrust the succession to the Prince of Yan, Yu, and others.

sentences.zh: 帝意尋变，詔肇以侯歸第。

translations.literal: The emperor's intent soon changed, and an edict sent Zhao home as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind soon shifted, and an edict sent Zhao home with his marquisate.

sentences.zh: 正始中薨。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Zhengshi era.

sentences.zh: 追赠衛將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title general of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the title general of the guards.

sentences.zh: 子興嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝分休户三百封肇弟纂爲列侯，後爲殄吴將軍，薨，追赠前將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning Emperor Wen divided three hundred households from Xiu's fief and enfeoffed Zhao's younger brother Zuan as a full marquis. Later he became general who exterminates Wu, died, and was posthumously granted the title former general.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had carved three hundred households from Xiu's fief to enfeoff Zhao's brother Zuan as a full marquis. Zuan later became general who exterminates Wu; at his death he was posthumously named former general.

sentences.zh: 張隐《文士傳》曰：肇孫摅，字颜遠，少厉志操，博學有才藻。

translations.literal: Zhang Yin's Account of Literary Men states: Zhao's grandson Shu, courtesy name Yanyuan, in youth set his will on integrity, was broadly learned and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yin's Wenshi zhuan records that Zhao's grandson Shu, styled Yanyuan, was studious, principled, and accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 仕晉，辟公府，歷洛陽令，有能名。

translations.literal: He served Jin, was summoned to the government offices, and successively served as magistrate of Luoyang with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin he entered the bureaucracy, served as magistrate of Luoyang, and won a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 大司馬齊王冏辅政，摅與齊人左思俱爲记室督。

translations.literal: When Grand Marshal Prince of Qi, Jiong, assisted in government, Shu together with Zuo Si of Qi both served as recorder supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Sima Jiong of Qi held the regency, Shu and the Qi native Zuo Si both served as recorder supervisors.

sentences.zh: 從中郎出爲襄陽太守、征南司馬。

translations.literal: From gentleman consultant he went out as grand administrator of Xiangyang and marshal of the army campaigning south.
translations.idiomatic: He left office as gentleman consultant to become governor of Xiangyang and marshal of the army campaigning south.

sentences.zh: 值天下亂，摅討賊向吴，戰敗死。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into chaos Shu campaigned against bandits toward Wu, was defeated in battle, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire dissolved he marched against bandits toward Wu, was defeated, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 曹真字子丹，太祖族子也。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen, courtesy name Zidan, was a clansman son of the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen, styled Zidan, was a clansman of Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵，真父邵募徒眾，爲州郡所殺。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor raised troops, Zhen's father Shao recruited followers and was killed by the province and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao first raised arms, Zhen's father Shao recruited followers and was killed by provincial authorities.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：真本姓秦，養曹氏。

translations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei states: Zhen's original surname was Qin; he was adopted into the Cao clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe says Zhen was born a Qin and raised into the Cao clan.

sentences.zh: 或云其父伯南夙與太祖善。

translations.literal: Some say his father Bonan had long been on good terms with the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Some say his father Bonan had been an old friend of Cao Cao's.

sentences.zh: 興平末，袁术部党與太祖攻劫，太祖出，爲寇所追，走入秦氏，伯南开門受之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xingping era, Yuan Shu's faction together with the Grand Progenitor raided and plundered. The Grand Progenitor went out and was pursued by bandits, ran into the Qin household, and Bonan opened the door to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xingping, partisans of Yuan Shu joined Cao Cao in a raid. Pursued by brigands, he fled into the Qin house; Bonan opened the door.

sentences.zh: 寇問太祖所在，答云：「我是也。」

translations.literal: The bandits asked where the Grand Progenitor was, and he answered, "I am he."
translations.idiomatic: Asked where Cao Cao was, Bonan answered, "I am he."

sentences.zh: 遂害之。

translations.literal: They thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The brigands killed him.

sentences.zh: 由此太祖思其功，故变其姓。

translations.literal: Because of this the Grand Progenitor remembered his merit and therefore changed his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao never forgot the sacrifice and had the boy take the Cao surname.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：邵以忠笃有才智，爲太祖所親信。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Shao was loyal, sincere, and possessed of wisdom and ability, and was trusted by the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu says Shao was loyal, capable, and trusted by Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 初平中，太祖興義兵，邵募徒眾，從太祖周旋。

translations.literal: In the Chuping era the Grand Progenitor raised righteous troops; Shao recruited followers and followed the Grand Progenitor in his movements.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuping, when Cao Cao raised righteous troops, Shao recruited men and rode at his side.

sentences.zh: 時豫州刺史黄琬欲害太祖，太祖避之而邵獨遇害。

translations.literal: At the time Inspector Huang Wan of Yu province wished to harm the Grand Progenitor. The Grand Progenitor avoided it, but Shao alone met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Huang Wan of Yu province plotted against Cao Cao. Cao Cao escaped; Shao alone was killed.

sentences.zh: 太祖哀真少孤，收養與諸子同，使與文帝共止。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor pitied Zhen for being orphaned young, took him in and raised him together with his own sons, and had him lodge with Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying the orphan, Cao Cao raised Zhen with his own sons and lodged him with the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 常猎，爲虎所逐，顧射虎，應声而倒。

translations.literal: Once while hunting he was chased by a tiger; he turned and shot the tiger, which fell at the sound.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the hunt a tiger chased him; he wheeled, shot, and the beast dropped at the crack of the bow.

sentences.zh: 太祖壯其鸷勇，使將虎豹騎。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor admired his fierce courage and had him command the tiger-and-leopard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marveled at his nerve and set him over the tiger-and-leopard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 討靈丘賊，拔之，封靈壽亭侯。

translations.literal: He campaigned against the bandits of Lingqiu, took it, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Lingshou.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced the bandits of Lingqiu, took the place, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Lingshou.

sentences.zh: 以偏將軍將兵擊劉備别將於下辯，破之，拜中堅將軍。

translations.literal: As lieutenant general he led troops and struck Liu Bei's detached general at Xiabian, defeated him, and was appointed general of the resolute center.
translations.idiomatic: As lieutenant general he smashed Liu Bei's detached commander at Xiabian and was made general of the resolute center.

sentences.zh: 從至長安，領中領軍。

translations.literal: He followed to Chang'an and led the central army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the court to Chang'an and led the central army.

sentences.zh: 是時，夏侯淵沒於陽平，太祖憂之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiahou Yuan perished at Yangping, and the Grand Progenitor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Yuan fell at Yangping, Cao Cao was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 以真爲征蜀護軍，督徐晃等破劉備别將高详於陽平。

translations.literal: He made Zhen protector general campaigning against Shu, supervised Xu Huang and others, and defeated Liu Bei's detached general Gao Xiang at Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zhen protector general campaigning against Shu, set Xu Huang under him, and broke Liu Bei's lieutenant Gao Xiang at Yangping.

sentences.zh: 太祖自至漢中，拔出諸軍，使真至武都迎曹洪等還屯陳倉。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor himself reached Hanzhong he withdrew the various armies and sent Zhen to Wudu to meet Cao Hong and the others and return to encamp at Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao reached Hanzhong himself he pulled the armies back and sent Zhen to Wudu to meet Cao Hong and bring the columns home to Chencang.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，以真爲鎮西將軍，假節都督雍、涼州諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingship he made Zhen general who guards the west, gave him the credential, and made him supervisor of the military affairs of Yong and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: At Cao Pi's accession as king, Zhen became general who guards the west with credential and command over Yong and Liang.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，進封東鄉侯。

translations.literal: His earlier and later merits were recorded and he was advanced in fief to marquis of Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His services were entered on the rolls and his fief advanced to marquis of Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 張進等反於酒泉，真遣费曜討破之，斬進等。

translations.literal: Zhang Jin and others rebelled at Jiuquan; Zhen sent Fei Yao to campaign against and defeat them and beheaded Jin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin rebelled at Jiuquan; Zhen sent Fei Yao to crush the revolt and beheaded Jin and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 黃初三年還京都，以真爲上軍大將軍，都督中外諸軍事，假節钺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu he returned to the capital and was made grand general of the upper army, supervisor of all military affairs within and without, with credential and battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he returned to the capital as grand general of the upper army, commander of all forces at court and in the field, with credential and battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 與夏侯尚等征孫權，擊牛渚屯，破之。

translations.literal: Together with Xiahou Shang and others he campaigned against Sun Quan, struck the encampment at Niuzhu, and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiahou Shang he campaigned against Sun Quan, stormed Niuzhu, and broke the camp.

sentences.zh: 轉拜中軍大將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand general of the central army and added as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand general of the central army and added as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 七年，文帝寝疾，真與陳羣、司馬宣王等受遺詔辅政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Emperor Wen lay gravely ill; Zhen together with Chen Qun, Sima Yi, and others received the deathbed edict to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, as Emperor Wen lay dying, Zhen with Chen Qun, Sima Yi, and others received the deathbed charge to govern.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，進封邵陵侯，臣松之案：真父名邵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Zhen was advanced in fief to marquis of Shaoling. Your subject Songzhi notes: Zhen's father's name was Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming advanced his fief to marquis of Shaoling. Your subject Songzhi notes: Zhen's father was named Shao.

sentences.zh: 封邵陵侯，若非書误，則事不可論。

translations.literal: To enfeoff him as marquis of Shaoling—if this is not a scribal error, then the matter cannot be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: A fief named Shaoling for a man whose father was Shao—unless the text is corrupt, the honor is hard to explain.

sentences.zh: 遷大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮圍祁山，南安、天水、安定三郡反應亮。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang besieged Qishan; Nan’an, Tianshui, and Anding commanderies rebelled in response to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuge Liang pinned Qishan, Nan’an, Tianshui, and Anding threw off Wei and declared for Shu.

sentences.zh: 帝遣真督諸軍軍郿，遣張郃擊亮將馬谡，大破之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Zhen to supervise the various armies encamped at Mei, sent Zhang He to strike Liang’s general Ma Su, and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Cao Zhen to marshal the hosts at Mei while Zhang He fell on Zhuge Liang’s lieutenant Ma Su and broke him decisively.

sentences.zh: 安定民楊条等略吏民保月支城，真進軍圍之。

translations.literal: The Anding commoner Yang Tiao and others seized officials and people and held Yuezhi city; Zhen advanced the army and besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tiao of Anding dragged officials and townsfolk into revolt and barricaded Yuezhi city; Zhen invested the place.

sentences.zh: 条謂其眾曰：「大將軍自來，吾原早降耳。」

translations.literal: Tiao said to his multitude: “When the grand general comes in person, I originally wished to surrender early.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tiao told his followers, “If the grand general comes in person I mean to yield at once.”

sentences.zh: 遂自缚出。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bound himself and came out.
translations.idiomatic: He then walked out with his hands tied behind his back.

sentences.zh: 三郡皆平。

translations.literal: The three commanderies were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All three mutinous commanderies were brought back under control.

sentences.zh: 真以亮惩於祁山，後出必從陳倉，乃使將軍郝昭、王生守陳倉，治其城。

translations.literal: Zhen thought Liang, chastened at Qishan, on a later thrust would certainly come by Chencang, so he sent generals Hao Zhao and Wang Sheng to guard Chencang and repair its walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen reasoned that Zhuge Liang, smarting from Qishan, would next thrust through Chencang; he stationed Hao Zhao and Wang Sheng there and rebuilt the fortifications.

sentences.zh: 明年春，亮果圍陳倉，已有備而不能克。

translations.literal: Next spring Liang indeed besieged Chencang, but defenses were already in place and he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Liang did lay siege to Chencang, yet the garrison was ready and he could not force an entry.

sentences.zh: 增邑，并前二千九百户。

translations.literal: His fief was increased; together with the previous it came to two thousand nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was enlarged until it totaled two thousand nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 四年，朝洛陽，遷大司馬，賜劍履上殿，入朝不趋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he had audience at Luoyang, was promoted grand marshal, was granted the sword and shoes for ascending the hall, and need not hasten his steps when entering court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he was summoned to Luoyang, promoted to grand marshal, and honored with the privilege of wearing sword and shoes in the throne hall and walking the court at an easy pace.

sentences.zh: 真以「蜀連出侵邊境，宜遂伐之。

translations.literal: Zhen held that “Shu has repeatedly come out to raid the border; it should forthwith be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen argued that “Shu keeps raiding our frontier and ought to be struck now,

sentences.zh: 數道并入，可大克也」。

translations.literal: Several routes advancing together can achieve a great victory.”
translations.idiomatic: with several columns converging for a decisive blow.”

sentences.zh: 帝從其計。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the strategy.

sentences.zh: 真當发西討，帝親临送。

translations.literal: Zhen was about to set out on the western expedition; the emperor personally came to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhen prepared to march west, the sovereign himself attended the farewell.

sentences.zh: 真以八月发長安，從子午道南入。

translations.literal: Zhen set out from Chang’an in the eighth month and entered south by the Ziwu road.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he left Chang’an and drove south through the Ziwu defile.

sentences.zh: 司馬宣王溯漢水，當會南郑。

translations.literal: Sima Yi went up the Han River and was to join him at Nan Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi was to move up the Han and link with him at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 諸軍或從斜穀道，或從武威入。

translations.literal: The various armies either went by the Xie valley road or entered from Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Other corps were to debouch from the Xie Valley or advance from Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 會大霖雨三十餘日，或栈道斷絕，詔真還軍。

translations.literal: It happened that great continuous rain fell thirty-odd days, some plank roads were severed, and an edict ordered Zhen to return the army.
translations.idiomatic: Weeks of pounding rain washed out the plank roads; an edict recalled Zhen’s army.

sentences.zh: 真少與宗人曹遵、鄉人朱赞并事太祖。

translations.literal: In youth Zhen together with his clansman Cao Zun and his townsman Zhu Zan all served the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zhen served Cao Cao alongside his kinsman Cao Zun and his townsman Zhu Zan.

sentences.zh: 遵、赞早亡，真愍之，乞分所食邑封遵、赞子。

translations.literal: Zun and Zan died early; Zhen pitied them and begged to divide the households of his fief to enfeoff Zun's and Zan's sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Zun and Zan died young, Zhen asked to carve from his own fief and enfeoff their sons.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「大司馬有叔向抚孤之仁，笃晏平久要之分。

translations.literal: An edict said, "The grand marshal has the kindness of Shuxiang in nurturing the orphaned and the steadfast friendship of Yan Ping in long-tested bonds.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "The grand marshal shows Shuxiang's kindness to the orphaned and Yan Ping's constancy in old friendship.

sentences.zh: 君子成人之美，听分真邑賜遵、赞子爵關内侯，各百户。」

translations.literal: A gentleman completes another's excellence; permit the division of Zhen's fief to grant Zun's and Zan's sons the rank of secondary marquis within the passes, each with a hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Let a gentleman crown another's merit: divide Zhen's fief and make Zun's and Zan's sons secondary marquises within the passes, a hundred households each."

sentences.zh: 真每征行，與將士同劳苦，軍赏不足，輒以家財班賜，士卒皆原爲用。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhen campaigned he shared hardship and toil with generals and soldiers. When military rewards were insufficient he would distribute his household wealth as gifts, and the soldiers all willingly served him.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign Zhen marched and slept as his men did. When bonuses ran short he paid from his own purse, and the ranks followed him willingly.

sentences.zh: 真病還洛陽，帝自幸其第省疾。

translations.literal: When Zhen fell ill and returned to Luoyang the emperor personally visited his residence to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: When illness drove him back to Luoyang, the emperor came in person to his house.

sentences.zh: 真薨，諡曰元侯。

translations.literal: Zhen died; his posthumous title was Marquis Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Marquis Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子爽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shuang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 帝追思真功，詔曰：「大司馬蹈履忠節，佐命二祖，内不恃親戚之寵，外不骄白屋之士，可謂能持盈守位，劳謙其德者也。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled Zhen's merit and issued an edict saying, "The grand marshal trod the path of loyal integrity, aided the Mandate of the two founders, inwardly did not rely on favor as kin, outwardly did not exalt himself over men of humble birth—he may be called one who could hold fullness and keep his place, whose merit was labor and whose virtue was humility.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering Zhen's service, the emperor decreed, "The grand marshal walked in loyalty, served both founders, neither traded on kinship nor looked down on humble men—he held his fullness and kept his place through labor and modesty.

sentences.zh: 其悉封真五子羲、训、則、彦、皑皆爲列侯。」

translations.literal: Let all five of Zhen's sons—Xi, Xun, Ze, Yan, and Kai—be enfeoffed as full marquises."
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoff all five sons—Xi, Xun, Ze, Yan, and Kai—as full marquises."

sentences.zh: 初，文帝分真邑二百户，封真弟彬爲列侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning Emperor Wen divided two hundred households from Zhen's fief and enfeoffed Zhen's younger brother Bin as a full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had earlier carved two hundred households from Zhen's fief to enfeoff his brother Bin as a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 爽字昭伯，少以宗室謹重，明帝在東宮，甚親愛之。

translations.literal: Shuang, courtesy name Zhaobo, in youth because of his clansmanship was careful and grave. When Emperor Ming was in the eastern palace he was deeply beloved.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang, styled Zhaobo, was grave and dutiful by birth. Emperor Ming cherished him while still heir.

sentences.zh: 及即位，爲散騎侍郎，累遷城門校尉，加散騎常侍，轉武衞將軍，寵待有殊。

translations.literal: When Ming ascended the throne Shuang became attendant cavalier, was repeatedly promoted to colonel of the city gates, added as attendant cavalier at the palace, transferred to general of the martial guard, and received extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: At Ming's accession he became attendant cavalier, rose through colonel of the city gates and attendant at the palace to general of the martial guard, with favor beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，乃引爽入臥內，拜大將軍，假節鉞，都督中外諸軍事，錄尚書事，與太尉司馬宣王並受遺詔輔少主。

translations.literal: When the emperor lay gravely ill he summoned Shuang into the inner chamber, appointed him grand general, gave him the credential and battle-axe, made him supervisor of all military affairs within and without and recorder of the masters of writing, and together with Grand Commandant Sima Yi he received the deathbed edict to assist the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed the emperor drew Shuang to his couch, named him grand general with credential and battle-axe, set him over all armies and the masters of writing, and joined Sima Yi as co-regent for the boy emperor.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，齊王即位，加爽侍中，改封武安侯，邑萬二千戶，賜劒履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died and the Prince of Qi ascended, Shuang was added as palace attendant, his fief was changed to marquis of Wu'an with twelve thousand households, and he was granted sword and shoes in the hall, exemption from hurrying at court audience, and exemption from having his name spoken in salutation.
translations.idiomatic: At Ming's death and the Qi king's accession, Shuang became palace attendant, was refiefed as marquis of Wu'an with twelve thousand households, and received sword and shoes in the hall, freedom from hurried court approach, and salutation without naming.

sentences.zh: 丁謐畫策，使爽白天子，發詔轉宣王爲太傅，外以名號尊之，內欲令尚書奏事，先來由己，得制其輕重也。

translations.literal: Ding Mi devised the plan to have Shuang tell the Son of Heaven to issue an edict transferring Sima Yi to grand tutor—outwardly honoring him by title, inwardly intending that memorials to the masters of writing should first come through himself so that he could control their weight.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Mi plotted for Shuang to have the emperor name Sima Yi grand tutor—honor in title, but power in routing memorials through Shuang first so he could weigh every matter.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：爽使弟羲爲表曰：「臣亡父真，奉事三朝，入備冢宰，出爲上將。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei states: Shuang had his younger brother Xi draft a memorial saying: “My deceased father Zhen served three courts, within prepared the role of chief steward, without was a senior general.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu relates that Shuang had his brother Xi compose a memorial: “My late father Zhen served three reigns, at court stood ready to act as chief minister, in the field held supreme command.

sentences.zh: 先帝以臣肺腑遺緒，獎飭拔擢，典兵禁省，進無忠恪積累之行，退無羔羊自公之節。

translations.literal: The late emperor, because I was flesh and blood left over from his line, encouraged and promoted me, put me in charge of troops in the forbidden precincts; forward I had no conduct of accumulated loyal scruple, backward I had no lamb-and-purity, self-for-duke demeanor.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, seeing me as kin left on the stem, heaped favors on me and gave me troops inside the palace; yet I have shown neither steady loyalty in advance nor the unstained integrity expected of a high minister.

sentences.zh: 先帝聖體不豫，臣雖奔走，侍疾嘗藥，曾無精誠翼日之應，猥與太尉懿俱受遺詔，且慙且懼，靡所厎告。

translations.literal: When the late emperor’s sacred person was unwell, though your servant ran about and tended illness tasting drugs, there was not the response of sincere devotion aiding the next day; basely I together with Grand Commandant Yi received the testamentary edict, now shamed now fearful, with nowhere to declare it.
translations.idiomatic: When his majesty lay ill I hurried to his bedside and tasted his physic, yet offered nothing that could compare with dutiful sons of old; unworthily I received the deathbed edict together with Grand Commandant Sima Yi, and I live torn between shame and dread with no place to unburden myself.

sentences.zh: 臣聞虞舜序賢，以稷、契爲先，成湯襃功，以伊、呂爲首，審選博舉，優劣得所，斯誠輔世長民之大經，錄勳報功之令典，自古以來，未之或闕。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Shun of Yu ordered worthies with Ji and Xie first, Tang of Cheng ennobled merit with Yi and Lü first; careful selection and broad recommendation so that the excellent and inferior each found their place—this is truly the great constant for aiding the age and ruling the people, the fine code for recording deeds and rewarding merit; from antiquity until now it has rarely been lacking.
translations.idiomatic: I have read that Shun ranked worthies with Ji and Xie at the top, and Tang rewarded service with Yi and Lü foremost: careful choice and wide recommendation, fitting each man to his grade, is the great principle for ordering the realm and the shining precedent for honoring merit—through all ages it has seldom been neglected.

sentences.zh: 今臣虛闇，位冠朝首，顧惟越次，中心愧惕，敢竭愚情，陳寫至實。

translations.literal: Now your servant is empty and dim, his rank crowns the head of court; looking back I have overleapt order; my heart is torn with shame and fear; I dare exhaust my foolish sincerity and set forth the utmost truth.
translations.idiomatic: Today I am a hollow man whose title tops the court; I know I have outstripped my deserts, and my heart quails with mingled shame and fear; yet I must speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 夫天下之達道者三，謂德、爵、齒也。

translations.literal: The thoroughfares of the empire are three: they are called virtue, noble rank, and seniority.
translations.idiomatic: The world recognizes three measures of standing—moral weight, noble rank, and gray hair.

sentences.zh: 懿本以高明中正，處上司之位，名足鎮衆，義足率下，一也。

translations.literal: Yi fundamentally, by being lofty and bright, upright at center, occupies the position of superior office; his name suffices to awe the host, his principle suffices to lead those below—first.
translations.idiomatic: First, Sima Yi is by nature judicious and upright; in high office his name alone steadies the host and his sense of duty draws men after him.

sentences.zh: 包懷大略，允文允武，仍立征伐之勳，遐邇歸功，二也。

translations.literal: Embracing a grand strategy, truly civil and truly martial, he moreover established the merit of campaigning; far and near return credit to him—second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, he combines breadth of design with gifts both civil and military and has repeatedly proved himself in the field; credit for those victories runs from the capital to the marches.

sentences.zh: 萬里旋斾，親受遺詔，翼亮皇家，內外所向，三也。

translations.literal: Ten thousand li he turned his banners, personally received the testamentary edict, wings-brighten the imperial house; inner and outer turn to him—third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, he marched ten thousand li at the head of the host, took the late emperor’s testament in his own hands, and has steadied the throne; court and camp alike look to him.

sentences.zh: 加之耆艾，紀綱邦國，體練朝政；

translations.literal: Added to that, he is advanced in years, sets the pattern for the state, and is thoroughly versed in court governance;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, he is a graybeard who sets the tone for the realm and knows every turn of government from long practice;

sentences.zh: 論德則過於吉甫、樊仲；

translations.literal: judged by virtue he surpasses Jifu and Fanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: by moral stature he outshines Jifu and Fanzhong of old;

sentences.zh: 課功則踰於方叔、召虎：凡此數者，懿實兼之。

translations.literal: reckoned by merit he exceeds Fangshu and Zhaohu: in all these several respects Yi truly combines them.
translations.idiomatic: reckoned by deeds he surpasses Fangshu and Zhaohu—Sima Yi embodies every one of these qualities.

sentences.zh: 臣抱空名而處其右，天下之人將謂臣以宗室見私，知進而不知退。

translations.literal: Your servant embraces an empty name yet stands to his right; the people of the world will say your servant, as a member of the imperial house, received private favor, knowing advance but not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: If I keep a hollow title and still rank above him, everyone will say the imperial clan is playing favorites—that I know how to climb but not how to step down.

sentences.zh: 陛下岐嶷，克明克類，如有以察臣之言，臣以爲宜以懿爲太傅、大司馬，上昭陛下進賢之明，中顯懿身文武之實，下使愚臣免於謗誚。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is discerning and wise, able to illuminate and classify; if there is means to examine your servant’s words, your servant thinks it fitting to appoint Yi grand tutor and grand marshal, above to display your Majesty’s brightness in advancing worthies, in the middle to manifest Yi’s substance in civil and military affairs, below to enable your foolish servant to escape slander.”
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is astute enough to weigh what I say: appoint Sima Yi Grand Tutor and Grand Marshal—so the throne shows the world it honors true talent, so Yi’s civil and military gifts are displayed in full, and so I may escape the charge of cronyism.”

sentences.zh: 於是帝使中書監劉放令孫資爲詔曰：「昔吳漢佐光武，有征定四方之功，爲大司馬，名稱於今。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor had Director of the Secretariat Liu Fang order Sun Zi to draft an edict saying: “In the past Wu Han assisted Guangwu, had merit in campaigning and settling the four quarters, became grand marshal, and his name is spoken of to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had Liu Fang of the Secretariat instruct Sun Zi to draft an edict: “Wu Han aided Emperor Guangwu, conquered the four corners, and became Grand Marshal—a name still honored today.

sentences.zh: 太尉體履正直，功蓋海內，先帝本以前後欲更其位者，輒不彌久，是以遲遲不施行耳。

translations.literal: The grand commandant in person and conduct is upright; his merit covers within the seas; the late emperor originally because of circumstances before and after wished to change his position, yet each time it did not last long, therefore it was delayed and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant is upright in deed and word, and his service fills the realm. The late emperor more than once meant to change his post, yet each plan fell through before long, so the promotion hung fire.

sentences.zh: 今大將軍薦太尉宜爲大司馬，旣合先帝本旨，又放推讓，進德尚勳，乃欲明賢良、辯等列、順長少也。

translations.literal: Now the grand general recommends the grand commandant as fitting for grand marshal; it both accords with the late emperor’s original intent, and moreover releases yielding, advancing virtue and esteeming merit; it is moreover wishing to clarify worthies, distinguish grades, and accord with senior and junior.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand General urges that the Grand Commandant become Grand Marshal—honoring the late emperor’s purpose, rewarding modest refusal, prizing virtue and merit, and sorting rank between elder statesman and rising men.

sentences.zh: 雖旦、奭之屬，宗師呂望，念在引領以處其下，何以過哉！

translations.literal: Though they were of the class of Dan and Shi, the patriarch Lü Wang, thinking to stretch the neck and stand beneath them—how could one surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, even the patriarch Lü Wang, would gladly take second place to such a man—what higher praise could there be?

sentences.zh: 朕甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: We greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: We heartily approve.

sentences.zh: 朕惟先帝固知君子樂天知命，纖介細疑，不足爲忌，當顧栢人彭亡之文，故用低佪，有意未遂耳！

translations.literal: We consider that the late emperor firmly knew the gentleman rejoices in Heaven and knows fate; fine trifling doubts are not worth taking as taboo; one ought to heed the text on Bairen and Pengwang’s death, therefore used hesitation, and intentions were not yet fulfilled!
translations.idiomatic: We reflect that the late emperor knew a gentleman accepts Heaven’s will: petty scruples must not become superstition—he recalled the old omen of Bairen and “Peng’s death,” and therefore hesitated until his purpose went unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 斯亦先帝敬重大臣，恩愛深厚之至也。

translations.literal: This too is the utmost of the late emperor’s reverence for great ministers and deep kindness and love.
translations.idiomatic: That too was how deeply he respected his chief ministers and cherished them.

sentences.zh: 昔成王建保傅之官，近漢顯宗以鄧禹爲太傅，皆所以優崇儁乂，必有尊也。

translations.literal: In the past King Cheng established the offices of protector and tutor; in recent Han Emperor Ming made Deng Yu grand tutor; all were means thereby to honor and exalt outstanding men, for there must be dignity.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou created the offices of protector and tutor; Emperor Ming of Later Han named Deng Yu Grand Tutor—both moves exalted the worthiest men with fitting dignity.

sentences.zh: 其以太尉爲太傅。」〉

translations.literal: Let the grand commandant be grand tutor.”〉"
translations.idiomatic: Let the Grand Commandant be promoted Grand Tutor.”〉"

sentences.zh: 爽弟羲爲中領軍，訓武衞將軍，彥散騎常侍侍講，其餘諸弟皆以列侯侍從，出入禁闥，貴寵莫盛焉。

translations.literal: Shuang’s younger brother Xi was chief of the palace guards, Xun general who guards martial majesty, Yan attendant-in-chief and expositor; the rest of the younger brothers all as full marquises attended and followed, going in and out of the forbidden gates; none was more honored and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang’s brother Xi commanded the palace guard, Xun became general of the martial guard, Yan was a supernumerary attendant and lecturer, and every other brother entered the inner palace as a full marquis—no clan ever basked in such favor.

sentences.zh: 南陽何晏、鄧颺、李勝、沛國丁謐、東平畢軌咸有聲名，進趣於時，明帝以其浮華，皆抑黜之；

translations.literal: He Yan of Nanyang, Deng Yang, Li Sheng, Ding Mi of Pei, Bi Gui of Dongping all had reputations and advanced with the fashion; Emperor Ming because they were flashy and hollow all suppressed and dismissed them;
translations.idiomatic: He Yan of Nanyang, Deng Yang, Li Sheng, Ding Mi of Pei, and Bi Gui of Dongping were famous men on the make; Emperor Ming had judged them shallow and shelved them;

sentences.zh: 及爽秉政，乃復進叙，任爲腹心。

translations.literal: when Shuang took power, then again they were advanced in order and employed as his heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: but once Shuang seized the government he brought them back and made them his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 颺等欲令爽立威名於天下，勸使伐蜀，爽從其言，宣王止之不能禁。

translations.literal: Yang and others wished to have Shuang establish awe-inspiring name in the world, urged him to campaign against Shu, and Shuang followed their words; the King of Xuan stopped him but could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang’s clique wanted Shuang to win glory abroad and talked him into invading Shu; Shuang agreed, and though Sima Yi argued against it he could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 正始五年，爽乃西至長安，大發卒六七萬人，從駱穀入。
