translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengshi, Shuang then went west to Chang’an, greatly issued soldiers sixty or seventy thousand, and entered by Luogu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi 5 Shuang moved his headquarters to Chang’an, levied sixty or seventy thousand men, and marched them in through the Luogu defile.

sentences.zh: 是時，關中及氐、羌轉輸不能供，牛馬騾驢多死，民夷號泣道路。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong and the Di and Qiang in relay transport could not supply; oxen, horses, mules, and donkeys mostly died, and commoners and tribesmen wailed on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The supply line through Guanzhong and the Di and Qiang country broke down; draft animals died by the thousands, and Han and non-Han alike wept along the highways.

sentences.zh: 入穀行數百里，賊因山爲固，兵不得進。

translations.literal: Having entered the valley they marched several hundred li; the bandits relied on the mountains for strength, and the troops could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: They had gone only a few hundred li up the valley when Shu’s defenders, dug into the heights, blocked every forward step.

sentences.zh: 爽參軍楊偉爲爽陳形勢，宜急還，不然將敗。

translations.literal: Shuang’s army adviser Yang Wei for Shuang set forth the situation: it was fitting to return in haste, otherwise there would be defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Yang Wei laid the facts before Shuang: withdraw at once or face ruin.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：偉字世英，馮翊人。

translations.literal: 〈The Worldly Talk states: Wei’s courtesy name was Shiying; he was a man of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Shiyu names him Yang Wei, styled Shiying, from Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 明帝治宮室，偉諫曰：「今作宮室，斬伐生民墓上松柏，毀壞碑獸石柱，辜及亡人，傷孝子心，不可以爲後世之法則。」〉

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming built palace halls, Wei remonstrated saying: “Now constructing palace halls, cutting the pines and cypresses on commoners’ graves above the living, destroying stone beasts and pillars of steles, extends guilt to the dead and wounds filial sons’ hearts; it cannot be taken as a model for later generations.”〉
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming raised new palaces, Wei protested: “You are felling the pines on people’s ancestral graves and smashing tomb guardians and stele columns—an outrage to the dead and a wound to the living. Such work must not become precedent for later ages.”〉

sentences.zh: 颺與偉爭於爽前，偉曰：「颺、勝將敗國家事，可斬也。」

translations.literal: Yang argued with Wei before Shuang; Wei said: “Yang and Sheng are about to ruin the state’s affairs; they can be beheaded.”
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang quarreled with Yang Wei in Shuang’s presence; Wei snapped, “Deng Yang and Li Sheng will wreck the realm—they deserve execution.”

sentences.zh: 爽不恱，乃引軍還。

translations.literal: Shuang was not pleased, then led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang took offense and marched his army home.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：司馬宣王謂夏侯玄曰：「春秋責大德重，昔武皇帝再入漢中，幾至大敗，君所知也。

translations.literal: 〈The Han–Jin Annals states: Sima Yi, King of Xuan, said to Xiahou Xuan: “The Spring and Autumn Annals hold great virtue weighty; in the past Emperor Wu twice entered Hanzhong and nearly suffered great defeat, as you know.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Han–Jin chunqiu records Sima Yi telling Xiahou Xuan: “The classic holds great men to a stern standard—your own Emperor Wu twice invaded Hanzhong and nearly came to grief, as you recall.

sentences.zh: 今興平路勢至險，蜀已先據；

translations.literal: Now the Xingping road’s terrain is extremely perilous, and Shu already holds it first;
translations.idiomatic: Today the Xingping route is sheer murder, and Shu already holds the heights;

sentences.zh: 若進不獲戰，退見徼絕，覆軍必矣。

translations.literal: if advancing one does not obtain battle, retreating one sees interception cut off, the overturned army is certain.
translations.idiomatic: if you fail to force a battle going in, you will be cut to pieces pulling out—the army is doomed.

sentences.zh: 將何以任其責！」

translations.literal: How will you bear the responsibility!”
translations.idiomatic: How will you answer for that?”

sentences.zh: 玄懼，言於爽，引軍退。

translations.literal: Xuan was afraid, spoke to Shuang, and led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan took fright, repeated the warning to Shuang, and the column retreated.

sentences.zh: 費禕進兵據三嶺以截爽，爽爭嶮苦戰，僅乃得過。

translations.literal: Fei Yi advanced troops and held the three ridges to intercept Shuang; Shuang contended the narrows and fought bitterly, only then was able to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi pushed forward and sealed the three ridges to trap Shuang; Shuang had to fight his way through defile after defile before scraping clear.

sentences.zh: 所發牛馬運轉者，死失略盡，羌、胡怨歎，而關右悉虛耗矣。〉

translations.literal: Of the oxen and horses sent for transport, dead and lost were nearly all; the Qiang and Hu groaned in resentment, and the right of the passes was utterly drained.〉
translations.idiomatic: The draft animals requisitioned for the march were almost all lost; Qiang and Hu cursed the expedition, and the Longyou corridor was left empty.〉

sentences.zh: 初，爽以宣王年德並高，恒父事之，不敢專行。

translations.literal: At first, because the King of Xuan was advanced in years and virtue together, Shuang always treated him as a father and did not dare act on his own.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shuang deferred to Sima Yi’s age and prestige and treated him almost as a father, never daring to act alone.

sentences.zh: 及晏等進用，咸共推戴，說爽以權重不宜委之於人。

translations.literal: When Yan and others were advanced in employment, all together pushed and supported him, persuading Shuang that heavy authority ought not be entrusted to another person.
translations.idiomatic: Once He Yan and his friends rose to power they flattered Shuang with the argument that supreme authority must not rest in anyone else’s hands.

sentences.zh: 乃以晏、颺、謐爲尚書，晏典選舉，軌司隷校尉，勝河南尹，諸事希復由宣王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan, Yang, and Mi were made secretaries; Yan directed selection and appointment; Gui was colonel of the metropolitan province; Sheng was governor of Henan; in various matters hope rarely again passed through the King of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi were named secretaries—He Yan ran appointments, Bi Gui took the metropolitan colonelcy, Li Sheng governed Henan—and business seldom reached Sima Yi’s desk.

sentences.zh: 宣王遂稱疾避爽。

translations.literal: The King of Xuan then claimed illness to avoid Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi thereupon pleaded illness and withdrew from Shuang’s affairs.

sentences.zh: 〈初，宣王以爽魏之肺腑，每推先之，爽以宣王名重，亦引身卑下，當時稱焉。

translations.literal: 〈At first the King of Xuan, because Shuang was the flesh and blood of Wei, always deferred to him first; Shuang because the King of Xuan’s name was weighty also drew himself low, and the age praised them.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Earlier Sima Yi had treated Shuang as the dynasty’s own flesh and blood and always yielded precedence; Shuang, awed by Yi’s reputation, kept his own manner humble, and contemporaries praised the pair.

sentences.zh: 丁謐、畢軌等旣進用，數言於爽曰：「宣王有大志而甚得民心，不可以推誠委之。」

translations.literal: Ding Mi, Bi Gui, and others, once advanced in employment, repeatedly spoke to Shuang saying: “The King of Xuan has great ambitions and has won the people’s hearts extremely; he cannot be entrusted with sincerity.”
translations.idiomatic: After Ding Mi and Bi Gui won office they kept telling Shuang, “Sima Yi harbors grand designs and commands deep popular loyalty—never trust him with real power.”

sentences.zh: 由是爽恒猜防焉。

translations.literal: On this account Shuang always suspected and guarded against him.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Shuang watched him with unrelenting suspicion.

sentences.zh: 禮貌雖存，而諸所興造，皆不復由宣王。

translations.literal: Courtesy and demeanor though remained, yet in all that was begun and built, none again passed through the King of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The courtesies continued, yet every new project bypassed Sima Yi entirely.

sentences.zh: 宣王力不能爭，且懼其禍，故避之。〉

translations.literal: The King of Xuan in strength could not contend, and moreover feared their disaster, therefore avoided them.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi lacked the leverage to fight back and feared their malice, so he feigned withdrawal.〉

sentences.zh: 晏等專政，共分割洛陽、野王典農部桑田數百頃，及壞湯沐地以爲產業，承勢竊取官物，因緣求欲州郡。

translations.literal: Yan and others monopolized government, together carved up several hundred qing of mulberry fields of the Luoyang and Yewang agricultural colonies, and ruined hot-spring fiefs to make private estates, riding power to steal official goods, and by connections sought whatever they wished from provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan’s ring ran the court, carved up hundreds of qing of state mulberry land around Luoyang and Yewang, seized imperial bath demesnes for private farms, looted the treasury under color of authority, and pulled strings in every province.

sentences.zh: 有司望風，莫敢忤旨。

translations.literal: The responsible officials watched the wind; none dared disobey the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates read which way the wind blew and never dared defy them.

sentences.zh: 晏等與廷尉盧毓素有不平，因毓吏微過，深文致毓法，使主者先收毓印綬，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: Yan and others with Commandant of Justice Lu Yu had long been at odds; because of a petty fault of Yu’s clerks, they twisted the text of the law deep against Yu’s law, had the chief first seize Yu’s seal and ribbon, then reported it.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan’s faction hated Commandant of Justice Lu Yu; they seized on a trivial slip by one of Yu’s clerks, tortured the statutes to indict Yu, confiscated his seal and sash before the throne ever heard the case.

sentences.zh: 其作威如此。

translations.literal: Their making awe was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the swagger of their power.

sentences.zh: 爽飲食車服擬於乘輿，尚方珍玩充牣其家，妻妾盈後庭，又私取先帝才人七八人，及將吏、師工、鼓吹、良家子女三十三人，皆以爲伎樂。

translations.literal: Shuang’s drink, food, chariot, and clothing were modeled on the imperial equipage; rare treasures of the imperial workshop filled his house; wives and concubines filled the rear court; moreover he privately took seven or eight of the late emperor’s talented ladies, and officers, artisans, musicians, and thirty-three sons and daughters of good families, all to make performers and musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang’s table, wardrobe, and carriages aped the emperor’s; the imperial workshops emptied their curios into his halls; his harem overflowed the inner courts; he helped himself to seven or eight of the late emperor’s palace women and impressed thirty-three officers’ children, craftsmen, musicians, and daughters of respectable houses into his private troupe.

sentences.zh: 詐作詔書，發才人五十七人送鄴臺，使先帝倢伃教習爲伎。

translations.literal: He forged an edict and issued fifty-seven talented persons to the Ye terrace, making the late emperor’s handmaids instructed to practice as performers.
translations.idiomatic: He forged an order shipping fifty-seven palace ladies to the Ye terrace to drill the late emperor’s maids as entertainers.

sentences.zh: 擅取太樂樂器、武庫禁兵。

translations.literal: He seized without authority instruments of the grand music and forbidden weapons of the armory.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped the court orchestra of its instruments and the arsenal of weapons reserved for the throne.

sentences.zh: 作窟室，綺疏四周，數與晏等會其中，飲酒作樂。

translations.literal: He made a vaulted chamber with carved lattices on four sides, and repeatedly with Yan and others met therein, drinking wine and making music.
translations.idiomatic: He dug a pleasure vault ringed with pierced panels where he and He Yan’s set met night after night for drinking and revelry.

sentences.zh: 羲深以爲大憂，數諫止之。

translations.literal: Xi deeply took this as great worry and repeatedly remonstrated to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi saw disaster in this and remonstrated again and again.

sentences.zh: 又著書三篇，陳驕淫盈溢之致禍敗，辭旨甚切，不敢斥爽，託戒諸弟以示爽。

translations.literal: Again he wrote three essays setting forth how arrogance, debauchery, and excess bring calamity and defeat; the wording was very cutting; he did not dare rebuke Shuang directly, but entrusted admonition to the younger brothers to show Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: He composed three essays on how pride and excess invite ruin—sharp pieces in which he never named Shuang but ostensibly lectured his brothers, intending Shuang to overhear the lesson.

sentences.zh: 爽知其爲己發也，甚不恱。

translations.literal: Shuang knew it was issued for himself and was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang knew the essays were aimed at him and took deep offense.

sentences.zh: 羲或時以諫喻不納，涕泣而起。

translations.literal: Xi sometimes because remonstrance and persuasion were not accepted, wept and rose.
translations.idiomatic: When his blunt advice went unheeded Xi would rise in tears.

sentences.zh: 宣王密爲之備。

translations.literal: The King of Xuan secretly made preparations for him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi meanwhile laid his plans in secret.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，李勝出爲荊州刺史，往詣宣王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, winter, Li Sheng went out as inspector of Jing province and went to visit the King of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year’s winter Li Sheng left for his post as Jing provincial inspector and called on Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 宣王稱疾困篤，示以羸形。

translations.literal: The King of Xuan claimed illness critically severe and displayed a wasted form.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi played the moribund invalid and let Li Sheng see a wasted frame.

sentences.zh: 勝不能覺，謂之信然。

translations.literal: Sheng could not perceive it and deemed it truly so.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng swallowed the act whole.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏末傳》曰：爽等令勝辭宣王，并伺察焉。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei End Transmission states: Shuang and others ordered Sheng to take leave of the King of Xuan and also to spy on him.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei mo zhuan says Shuang sent Li Sheng to bid Sima Yi farewell while using the visit to spy on him.

sentences.zh: 宣王見勝，勝自陳無他功勞，橫蒙時恩，當爲本州，詣閤拜辭，不悟加恩，得蒙引見。

translations.literal: The King of Xuan saw Sheng; Sheng himself stated he had no other merit, had undeservedly received the age’s favor, was about to become governor of his home province, came to the gate to bow in farewell, did not realize added favor, and was able to receive a personal audience.
translations.idiomatic: When they met Li Sheng disclaimed any merit, said he owed his rise to the times alone, explained that he was bound for his home province as governor, had come to the gate for a parting audience, and never expected the honor of a private interview.

sentences.zh: 宣王令兩婢侍邊，持衣，衣落；

translations.literal: The King of Xuan ordered two maids to attend at his side and hold his clothes; the clothes fell;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi had two maids hold his robe; the robe slipped from his shoulders;

sentences.zh: 復上指口，言渴求飲，婢進粥，宣王持杯飲粥，粥皆流出沾胷。

translations.literal: again he pointed upward to his mouth, saying he thirsted and begged drink; the maids brought gruel; the King of Xuan held the cup and drank gruel, and the gruel all flowed out and wet his chest.
translations.idiomatic: he jabbed a finger at his mouth to mime thirst; a maid brought porridge; he lifted the bowl and let the gruel spill down his chest.

sentences.zh: 勝愍然，爲之涕泣，謂宣王曰：「今主上尚幼，天下恃賴明公。

translations.literal: Sheng was moved with pity, wept for him, and said to the King of Xuan: “Now the ruler is still young; the world relies on your excellency.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng was moved to pity, wept, and said, “The emperor is still a child; the realm leans on you, my lord.

sentences.zh: 然衆情謂明公方舊風疾發，何意尊體乃爾！」

translations.literal: Yet the multitude’s feeling says your excellency’s old wind illness has flared; how could your honored body be thus!”
translations.idiomatic: Yet rumor had it your old palsy had returned—who could imagine you reduced to this?”

sentences.zh: 宣王徐更寬言，才令氣息相屬，說：「年老沈疾，死在旦夕。

translations.literal: The King of Xuan slowly changed to broader speech, only then letting breath link in succession, saying: “Old age and sinking illness; death is before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi then spoke in a thin, broken voice: “Age and sickness have me by the throat; I may not see another dawn.

sentences.zh: 君當屈并州，并州近胡，好善爲之，恐不復相見，如何！」

translations.literal: You are about to bend to Bing province; Bing province is near the Hu; do well and be kind; I fear we will not meet again—what to do!”
translations.idiomatic: You are headed for Bing province on the Hu frontier—treat the tribes kindly. I doubt we shall meet again—ah, what is to be done?”

sentences.zh: 勝曰：「當還忝本州，非并州也。」

translations.literal: Sheng said: “I am returning disgracefully to my home province, not Bing province.”
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng said, “I am ashamed to say I go to my home province as governor, not to Bing.”

sentences.zh: 宣王乃復陽爲昏謬，曰：「君方到并州，努力自愛！」

translations.literal: The King of Xuan again feigned confusion and error, saying: “You have just arrived at Bing province; strive to love yourself!”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi pretended greater confusion: “So you have reached Bing province—take good care of yourself there!”

sentences.zh: 錯亂其辭，狀如荒語。

translations.literal: He scrambled his words so the condition was like wild speech.
translations.idiomatic: He jumbled his phrases until he sounded senile.

sentences.zh: 勝復曰：「當忝荊州，非并州也。」

translations.literal: Sheng again said: “I am disgracefully to be inspector of Jing, not Bing province.”
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng repeated, “My post is Jing province, not Bing.”

sentences.zh: 宣王乃若微悟者，謂勝曰：「懿年老，意荒忽，不解君言。

translations.literal: The King of Xuan then as if slightly comprehending said to Sheng: “Yi is old; intention is wild and confused; I do not understand your words.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi feigned a flicker of understanding: “Yi is old and his wits wander; I no longer follow what you say.

sentences.zh: 今還爲本州刺史，盛德壯烈，好建功勳。

translations.literal: Now returning as inspector of your home province, you have abundant virtue and fierce ardor, and love to establish merit and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: You return as governor of your own province—noble spirit, fierce zeal, a man who loves to win glory on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 今當與君別，自顧氣力轉微，後必不更會，因欲自力，設薄主人，生死共別。

translations.literal: Now I must part with you; looking at myself my breath and strength turn ever weaker; afterward we are sure not to meet again; therefore I wish myself to force strength, set a thin feast as host, and with you part for life and death together.
translations.idiomatic: Now we must part: I feel my strength ebbing and know we shall never meet again. Let me rouse myself to play host at a humble farewell—we will toast life and death together.

sentences.zh: 令師、昭兄弟結君爲友，不可相舍去，副懿區區之心。」

translations.literal: Let the masters Shi and Zhao brothers bind you as friends; you must not leave each other, answering to Yi’s petty heart.”
translations.idiomatic: I ask my sons Shi and Zhao to befriend you—do not part from them; that would ease this old man’s heart.”

sentences.zh: 因流涕哽咽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept with choked sobs.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into wracking sobs.

sentences.zh: 勝亦長歎，荅曰：「輒當承教，須待勑命。」

translations.literal: Sheng also sighed long and answered: “I will receive your instruction; I must await the ordered mandate.”
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng sighed and replied, “I shall obey your charge—once the edict is issued.”

sentences.zh: 勝辭出，與爽等相見，說：「太傅語言錯誤，口不攝杯，指南爲北。

translations.literal: When Sheng took leave and came out, met Shuang and others, he said: “The grand tutor’s speech is mistaken, his mouth cannot hold the cup, points south calling it north.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng emerged and met Shuang’s circle he reported, “The Grand Tutor’s mind is gone—he cannot keep the cup to his lips and mistakes south for north.

sentences.zh: 又云吾當作并州，吾荅言當還爲荊州，非并州也。

translations.literal: Again he said I was about to go to Bing province; I answered saying I was about to return as inspector of Jing, not Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted I was bound for Bing; I told him again and again my post was Jing, not Bing.

sentences.zh: 徐徐與語，有識人時，乃知當還爲荊州耳。

translations.literal: Slowly talking with him, when there was a moment he was lucid, then he knew I was about to return as inspector of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Only when I spoke slowly and caught a lucid interval did he grasp that my governorship was Jing.

sentences.zh: 又欲設主人祖送。

translations.literal: Again he wished to set a host and perform the road-offering farewell.
translations.idiomatic: He even wanted to host a farewell feast on the road.

sentences.zh: 不可舍去，宜須待之。」

translations.literal: You must not leave; it is fitting to wait for it.”
translations.idiomatic: Do not rush away—wait for that kindness.”

sentences.zh: 更向爽等垂淚云：「太傅患不可復濟，令人愴然。」〉

translations.literal: Again toward Shuang and others he shed tears saying: “The grand tutor’s illness cannot again be helped; it makes one mournful.”〉
translations.idiomatic: Turning again to Shuang’s men with tears he said, “The Grand Tutor cannot recover—how it wrings the heart.”〉

sentences.zh: 十年正月，車駕朝高平陵，爽兄弟皆從。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, the imperial carriage had audience at Gaoping Mausoleum; Shuang and his brothers all followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year the emperor went to sacrifice at the Gaoping tombs, and Shuang with every brother of his rode in the train.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：爽兄弟先是數俱出游，桓範謂曰：「總萬機，典禁兵，不宜並出，若有閉城門，誰復內人者？」

translations.literal: 〈The Worldly Talk states: Shuang’s brothers before this several times all went out touring together; Huan Fan said to them: “You hold the myriad threads and command the forbidden troops; it is not fitting to go out together; if someone closes the city gates, who again will let you in?”
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Shiyu notes that Shuang’s brothers often left the capital together; Huan Fan warned, “You control the government and the palace guard—you should never leave town at once: if someone slammed the gates, who would let you back in?”

sentences.zh: 爽曰：「誰敢爾邪！」

translations.literal: Shuang said: “Who would dare do thus!”
translations.idiomatic: Shuang laughed, “Who would dare?”

sentences.zh: 由此不復並行。

translations.literal: On this account they no longer went out in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: After that they avoided traveling in a pack.

sentences.zh: 至是乃盡出也。〉

translations.literal: At this time then they all went out.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, however, they all rode out together.

sentences.zh: 宣王部勒兵馬，先據武庫，遂出屯洛水浮橋。

translations.literal: The King of Xuan deployed troops and horses, first seized the armory, then went out and encamped at the floating bridge on the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi struck first: he seized the imperial arsenal, then marched his men to the floating bridge over the Luo.

sentences.zh: 奏爽曰：「臣昔從遼東還，先帝詔陛下、秦王及臣升御牀，把臣臂，深以後事爲念。

translations.literal: He memorialized Shuang saying: “Your servant in the past followed from Liaodong’s return; the late emperor ordered your Majesty, the Prince of Qin, and your servant to ascend the imperial couch, grasped your servant’s arm, and deeply took the later affair to heart.
translations.idiomatic: He laid charges against Shuang: “When I returned from Liaodong the late emperor called Your Majesty, the Prince of Qin, and me to his couch, took my arm, and spoke of what must come after his death.

sentences.zh: 臣言『二祖亦屬臣以後事爲念，此自陛下所見，無所憂苦；

translations.literal: Your servant said: ‘The two ancestors also charged your servant to take the later affair to heart; this is what your Majesty personally saw; there is nothing to worry or suffer;
translations.idiomatic: I answered, ‘Your two imperial forebears gave me the same charge—Your Majesty witnessed it—so set your mind at rest;

sentences.zh: 萬一有不如意，臣當以死奉明詔』。

translations.literal: if in ten thousand there is one unanticipated matter, your servant ought to die carrying out the enlightened edict’.
translations.idiomatic: should anything go amiss, I will give my life to execute your clear command.

sentences.zh: 黃門令董箕等，才人侍疾者，皆所聞知。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Director Dong Ji and others, the talented ladies who attended illness, all heard and knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Yellow Gates Dong Ji and the palace women who nursed him heard every word.

sentences.zh: 今大將軍爽背棄顧命，敗亂國典，內則僭擬，外專威權；

translations.literal: Now the grand general Shuang has betrayed the testamentary charge, ruined and disordered the state’s norms; within he usurps and imitates, without he monopolizes awe-inspiring authority;
translations.idiomatic: Now Grand General Shuang has torn up the deathbed trust and trampled the law: inside the palace he apes the sovereign, outside it he wields unchecked power;

sentences.zh: 破壞諸營，盡據禁兵，羣官要職，皆置所親；

translations.literal: he has broken the various camps, wholly seized the forbidden troops, in group offices and crucial posts all placed his intimates;
translations.idiomatic: he has dismantled the guard battalions, pocketed the palace army, and stuffed every key office with his creatures;

sentences.zh: 殿中宿衞，歷世舊人皆復斥出，欲置新人以樹私計；

translations.literal: the palace night guards, men of age-old standing through generations, have all again been expelled, wishing to place new men to plant private schemes;
translations.idiomatic: the night watch inside the halls—men who had served for generations—he has cashiered wholesale in order to plant his own men;

sentences.zh: 根據槃牙，縱恣日甚。

translations.literal: roots grip and fangs interlock; wanton license grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: his roots and teeth are everywhere, and his arrogance grows by the day.

sentences.zh: 外旣如此，又以黃門張當爲都監，專共交關，看察至尊，候伺神器，離間二宮，傷害骨肉。

translations.literal: Externally as this, moreover he has made Yellow Gate Zhang Dang chief overseer, exclusively together weaving connections, watching the supreme one, spying on the divine vessel, estranging the two palaces, harming flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, he set the eunuch Zhang Dang over all liaison with the throne, spying on Your Majesty, coveting the regalia, driving wedge between the two palaces, and wounding the imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 天下汹汹，人懷危懼，陛下但爲寄坐，豈得久安！

translations.literal: The world boils; people harbor peril and fear; your Majesty is only a lodged seat—how can there be long peace!
translations.idiomatic: The realm seethes with fear while Your Majesty sits as a mere figurehead—how can that endure?

sentences.zh: 此非先帝詔陛下及臣升御牀之本意也。

translations.literal: This is not the late emperor’s intent in ordering your Majesty and your servant to ascend the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: This was never what the late emperor meant when he took our hands on that couch.

sentences.zh: 臣雖朽邁，敢忘往言？

translations.literal: Your servant though decayed and aged, how dare forget the words of the past?
translations.idiomatic: Though I am old and worn, dare I forget the oath I swore then?

sentences.zh: 昔趙高極意，秦氏以滅；

translations.literal: In the past Zhao Gao carried his will to the extreme, and the house of Qin thereby perished;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Gao ran amok, the house of Qin fell;

sentences.zh: 呂、霍早斷，漢祚永世。

translations.literal: the Lüs and Huos were cut off early, and the Han mandate lasted for ages.
translations.idiomatic: the Lü and Huo clans were destroyed in time, and the Han line endured for generations.

sentences.zh: 此乃陛下之大鑒，臣受命之時也。

translations.literal: This is your Majesty’s great mirror; it is the moment when your servant received his charge.
translations.idiomatic: These are warnings writ large for Your Majesty—and the very hour I accepted my charge from the throne.

sentences.zh: 太尉臣濟、尚書令臣孚等，皆以爽爲有無君之心，兄弟不宜典兵宿衞，奏永寧宮。

translations.literal: Your servant the grand commandant Ji, Secretary Director your servant Fu, and others all because Shuang harbors a heart without a lord, his brothers are not fitting to command troops and night guard, memorialized the Palace of Eternal Peace.
translations.idiomatic: I, Grand Commandant Jiang Ji, Secretary Director Sima Fu, and the rest have memorialized the empress dowager at Yongning: Cao Shuang shows disloyalty to the throne; his brothers must not hold military command or the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 皇太後令勑臣如奏施行。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered your servant to carry out as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager has ordered me to execute that memorial to the letter.

sentences.zh: 臣輒勑主者及黃門令罷爽、羲、訓吏兵，以侯就第，不得逗留以稽車駕；

translations.literal: Your servant then ordered the responsible officials and the Yellow Gate director to dismiss the clerks and soldiers of Shuang, Xi, and Xun, to go to their mansions as marquises, and not to linger so as to delay the imperial carriage;
translations.idiomatic: I have instructed the proper bureaus and the director of the Yellow Gates to strip Shuang, Xi, and Xun of their guards and staff, confine them to their marquisates as nobles without office, and forbid them to loiter and obstruct the imperial train;

sentences.zh: 敢有稽留，便以軍法從事。

translations.literal: if any dare delay, then let military law be applied.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who tarries will answer under military law.

sentences.zh: 臣輙力疾，將兵屯洛水浮橋，伺察非常。」

translations.literal: Your servant then, forcing strength through illness, leads troops encamped at the floating bridge on the Luo River to watch for the extraordinary.”
translations.idiomatic: Though ill, I have mustered the strength to bring troops to the Luo floating bridge to guard against any coup.”

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：初，宣王勒兵從闕下趣武庫，當爽門，人逼車住。

translations.literal: 〈The Worldly Talk states: At first the King of Xuan deployed troops from below the gate towers hastening to the armory; when at Shuang’s gate, men pressed the carriage to stop.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Shiyu relates that Sima Yi first marched his men from under the palace gate toward the arsenal; at the gate of Shuang’s mansion retainers blocked the carriage.

sentences.zh: 爽妻劉怖，出至廳事，謂帳下守督曰：「公在外。

translations.literal: Shuang’s wife Liu was frightened, came out to the reception hall, and said to the guard commander under the tent: “The lord is outside.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang’s wife Liu ran panic-stricken to the outer hall and told the house guard, “My husband is still away with the court.

sentences.zh: 今兵起，如何？」

translations.literal: Now soldiers have risen; what is to be done?”
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers are moving in the capital—what are we to do?”

sentences.zh: 督曰：「夫人勿憂。」

translations.literal: The commander said: “Madam, do not worry.”
translations.idiomatic: The captain answered, “Do not fear, my lady.”

sentences.zh: 乃上門樓，引弩注箭欲發。

translations.literal: Then he ascended the gate tower, drew crossbows, nocked arrows, and wished to shoot.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed to the gate tower, strung crossbows, and prepared to loose.

sentences.zh: 將孫謙在後牽止之曰：「天下事未可知！」

translations.literal: General Sun Qian behind pulled and stopped him saying: “Affairs under Heaven are not yet to be known!”
translations.idiomatic: Behind him general Sun Qian seized his arm and cried, “No one yet knows how the day will fall!”

sentences.zh: 如此者三，宣王遂得過去。〉

translations.literal: Thus three times; the King of Xuan then was able to pass through.〉
translations.idiomatic: He repeated the plea three times until Sima Yi’s column was allowed through.〉

sentences.zh: 爽得宣王奏事，不通，迫窘不知所爲。

translations.literal: Shuang obtained the King of Xuan’s memorial matter, but it did not get through; pressed and cornered he did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang never received Sima Yi’s memorial in time; trapped and bewildered, he could not think of a move.

sentences.zh: 〈干寶《晉紀》曰：爽留車駕宿伊水南，伐木爲鹿角，發屯甲兵數千人以爲衞。

translations.literal: 〈Gan Bao’s Jin Annals states: Shuang kept the imperial carriage overnight south of the Yi River, cut wood for deer-horn palisades, and issued several thousand armored soldiers of the encampment as guards.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Gan Bao’s Jin ji says Shuang halted the emperor south of the Yi, felled timber for chevaux-de-frise, and threw up a cordon of several thousand armored men.

sentences.zh: 魏末傳曰：宣王語弟孚，「陛下在外不可露宿，促送帳幔、太官食具詣行在所」。〉

translations.literal: The Wei End Transmission states: the King of Xuan spoke to his younger brother Fu, “The Son of Heaven is outside and cannot sleep in the open; hasten to send curtains and the grand provisioner’s utensils to the traveling encampment.”〉
translations.idiomatic: The Wei mo zhuan adds that Sima Yi told Sima Fu, “The emperor must not bivouac in the cold—rush tents and the imperial kitchen gear to his camp.”〉

sentences.zh: 大司農沛國桓範聞兵起，不應太後召，矯詔開平昌門，拔取劒戟，略將門候，南奔爽。

translations.literal: Grand minister of agriculture Huan Fan of Pei heard troops had risen, did not answer the empress dowager’s summons, forged an edict to open the Pingchang Gate, seized swords and halberds, coerced the gate warden, and fled south to Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Fan of Pei, the grand minister of agriculture, hearing of the coup, ignored the dowager’s call, forged an order to open Pingchang Gate, armed himself at sword point, impressed the gate officer, and galloped south to Shuang.

sentences.zh: 宣王知，曰：「範畫策，爽必不能用範計。」

translations.literal: The King of Xuan knew it and said: “Fan will draw up plans, but Shuang is sure not to be able to use Fan’s plan.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi heard the news and said, “Huan Fan will offer counsel—but Shuang lacks the wit to follow it.”

sentences.zh: 範說爽使車駕幸許昌，招外兵。

translations.literal: Fan urged Shuang to have the imperial carriage go to Xuchang and summon outside troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Fan urged him to escort the emperor to Xuchang and call in armies from the provinces.

sentences.zh: 爽兄弟猶豫未決，範重謂羲曰：「當今日，卿門戶求貧賤復可得乎？

translations.literal: Shuang’s brothers hesitated and could not decide; Fan again spoke to Xi saying: “On this day, can you still seek poverty and lowliness for your house?
translations.idiomatic: The brothers dithered; Fan turned to Xi and demanded, “Do you imagine you can sink back into obscurity after this day?

sentences.zh: 且匹夫持質一人，尚欲望活，今卿與天子相隨，令於天下，誰敢不應者？」

translations.literal: Moreover a common fellow holding one man hostage still hopes to live; now you follow the Son of Heaven, command the world—who would dare not respond?”
translations.idiomatic: A common kidnapper with a single hostage still bargains for his life—yet you hold the emperor and could issue orders to the realm. Who would refuse you?”

sentences.zh: 羲猶不能納。

translations.literal: Xi still could not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi still would not act.

sentences.zh: 侍中許允、尚書陳泰說爽，使早自歸罪。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Xu Yun and Secretary Chen Tai urged Shuang to return guilt early on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants Xu Yun and Secretary Chen Tai talked Shuang into surrendering at once.

sentences.zh: 爽於是遣允、泰詣宣王，歸罪請死，乃通宣王奏事。

translations.literal: Shuang thereupon sent Yun and Tai to visit the King of Xuan, returned guilt begging death, and then the King of Xuan’s memorial matter got through.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang dispatched Xu and Chen to Sima Yi, confessed his crimes, offered his life, and only then did Yi’s memorial reach him.

sentences.zh: 〈干寶《晉書》曰：桓範出赴爽，宣王謂蔣濟曰：「智囊往矣。」

translations.literal: 〈Gan Bao’s Book of Jin states: When Huan Fan went out to join Shuang, the King of Xuan said to Jiang Ji: “The strategy satchel has gone.”
translations.idiomatic: 〈Gan Bao’s Jin shu notes that when Huan Fan rode to Shuang, Sima Yi told Jiang Ji, “The brains of the plot have arrived.”

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「範則智矣，駑馬戀棧豆，爽必不能用也。」

translations.literal: Ji said: “Fan is indeed wise, but a sorry nag loves its stable beans; Shuang is sure not to be able to use him.”
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji answered, “Fan is clever—but a broken-down nag clings to its manger; Shuang will never heed him.”

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：宣王使許允、陳泰解語爽，蔣濟亦與書達宣王之旨，又使爽所信殿中校尉尹大目謂爽，唯免官而已，以洛水爲誓。

translations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: the King of Xuan had Xu Yun and Chen Tai explain terms to Shuang; Jiang Ji also sent a letter conveying the King of Xuan’s intent, and again had Yin Damu, the palace colonel Shuang trusted, tell Shuang that only dismissal from office was intended, with oath on the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu adds that Sima Yi sent Xu Yun and Chen Tai with terms, Jiang Ji wrote privately, and palace colonel Yin Damu, whom Shuang trusted, swore on the Luo that only office would be lost.

sentences.zh: 爽信之，罷兵。

translations.literal: Shuang believed it and dismissed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang believed them and stood his army down.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：爽旣罷兵，曰：「我不失作富家翁。」

translations.literal: The Wei Family Spring and Autumn states: after Shuang had dismissed the troops, he said: “I will not fail to become a rich householder.”
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu records that after laying down arms Shuang said, “At worst I retire a very rich commoner.”

sentences.zh: 範哭曰：「曹子丹佳人，生汝兄弟，犢耳！

translations.literal: Fan wept saying: “Cao Zidan was a fine man; he begat you brothers, calves’ ears!
translations.idiomatic: Huan Fan wept, “Cao Zhen was a hero among men—yet he sired you two calves!

sentences.zh: 何圖今日坐汝等族滅矣！」〉

translations.literal: Who would have thought today sitting you would bring clan extermination!”〉"
translations.idiomatic: Who could have dreamed that listening to you would wipe out our houses!”〉"

sentences.zh: 遂免爽兄弟，以侯還第。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shuang and his brothers were dismissed and returned to their mansions as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang and his brothers were stripped of office and sent home under marquis’ titles only.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏末傳》曰：爽兄弟歸家，勑洛陽縣發民八百人，使尉部圍爽第四角，角作高樓，令人在上望視爽兄弟舉動。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei End Transmission states: when Shuang’s brothers returned home, they ordered Luoyang county to conscript eight hundred commoners, had the constabulary surround Shuang’s mansion at the four corners, at each corner making a high tower, and had men on top watch Shuang’s brothers’ movements.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei mo zhuan says the county impressed eight hundred civilians to ring Shuang’s compound, building watchtowers at each corner from which guards spied on every move.

sentences.zh: 爽計窮愁悶，持彈到後園中，樓上人便唱言「故大將軍東南行！」

translations.literal: Shuang’s plans were exhausted, anxious and depressed; he took a pellet bow to the rear garden; the man on the tower then sang out “The former grand general goes southeast!”
translations.idiomatic: Shuang, at his wits’ end, wandered the rear garden with a pellet bow while a voice from the tower cried, “The ex–grand general is moving southeast!”

sentences.zh: 爽還廳事上，與兄弟共議，未知宣王意深淺，作書與宣王曰：「賤子爽哀惶恐怖，無狀招禍，分受屠滅，前遣家人迎糧，於今未反，數日乏匱，當煩見餉，以繼旦夕。」

translations.literal: Shuang returned to the reception hall, with his brothers jointly deliberated, did not know the King of Xuan’s intent deep or shallow, and wrote a letter to the King of Xuan saying: “Your worthless son Shuang is in sorrow, panic, and terror, having without propriety brought calamity, dividing to receive slaughter and extinction; previously I sent family members to meet grain transports; to this day they have not returned; for several days supplies have been lacking; I must trouble you to send provisions to continue morning and evening.”
translations.idiomatic: Shuang went back to the hall, huddled with his brothers, still unsure how far Sima Yi meant to go, and wrote Yi begging, “Your worthless son Shuang trembles with guilt. I brought this ruin on myself and deserve extinction. Servants I sent to meet a grain convoy have not returned; we are hungry. Please send food to tide us over.”

sentences.zh: 宣王得書大驚，即荅書曰：「初不知乏糧，甚懷踧踖。

translations.literal: The King of Xuan, obtaining the letter, was greatly startled, immediately answered the letter saying: “At first I did not know grain was lacking; I am deeply embarrassed.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi feigned shock and replied at once, “I had no idea you were short of grain—how mortifying.

sentences.zh: 令致米一百斛，并肉脯、鹽豉、大豆。」

translations.literal: Order to deliver one hundred hu of rice, together with dried meat, salted beans and sauce, and soybeans.”
translations.idiomatic: I am sending a hundred hu of rice, dried meat, salted beans, and soy.”

sentences.zh: 尋送。

translations.literal: Shortly it was delivered.
translations.idiomatic: The supplies arrived almost immediately.

sentences.zh: 爽兄弟不達變數，即便喜歡，自謂不死。〉

translations.literal: Shuang’s brothers did not comprehend the shifting numbers, then rejoiced, deeming themselves not to die.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers failed to read the omen, rejoiced at the gift, and told each other they would live.

sentences.zh: 初，張當私以所擇才人張、何等與爽。

translations.literal: At first Zhang Dang privately gave to Shuang the talented women Zhang and He whom he had chosen.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhang Dang privately presented to Shuang the talented women Zhang and He whom he had selected.

sentences.zh: 疑其有姦，收當治罪。

translations.literal: Suspecting he had improper relations, they seized Dang to punish his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting impropriety, authorities arrested Zhang Dang for punishment.

sentences.zh: 當陳爽與晏等陰謀反逆，並先習兵，須三月中欲發，於是收晏等下獄。

translations.literal: Dang stated that Shuang with Yan and others secretly plotted rebellion and treason, and all had beforehand practiced troops, intending to rise in the third month; thereupon Yan and others were seized and sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Dang testified that Shuang, He Yan, and others had secretly plotted rebellion, trained troops, and planned to rise in the third month; Yan and the rest were jailed.

sentences.zh: 會公卿朝臣廷議，以爲「春秋之義，『君親無將，將而必誅』。

translations.literal: The assembled dukes, ministers, and court officials deliberated in court, holding that "the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is, 'The ruler and parent allow no general; if there is a general, he must be executed.'
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated under Spring and Autumn principle: "Against ruler or parent, no armed defiance is permitted; defiance demands execution."

sentences.zh: 爽以支屬，世蒙殊寵，親受先帝握手遺詔，託以天下，而包藏禍心，蔑棄顧命，乃與晏、颺及當等謀圖神器，範黨同罪人，皆爲大逆不道」。

translations.literal: Shuang as a branch lineage through generations received extraordinary favor, personally received the late emperor's handclasp testamentary edict, entrusted with All under Heaven, yet harbored treacherous hearts, despised and cast aside the dying charge, and therefore with Yan, Yang, and Dang and others plotted the regalia; Fan's faction were fellow criminals—all were great rebellion without the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Shuang, a collateral kinsman long favored, had received the late emperor's handclasp charge to govern the realm, yet harbored treason, scorned that trust, and with Yan, Yang, Dang, and others sought the throne; Huan Fan's faction shared the crime—all were capital traitors."

sentences.zh: 於是收爽、羲、訓、晏、颺、謐、軌、勝、範、當等，皆伏誅，夷三族。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shuang, Xi, Xun, Yan, Yang, Mi, Gui, Sheng, Fan, Dang, and others were all seized; all were executed and exterminated to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang, Xi, Xun, Yan, Yang, Mi, Gui, Sheng, Fan, Dang, and others were seized, executed, and exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：鄧颺字玄茂，鄧禹後也。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: Deng Yang's courtesy name was Xuanmao; he was a descendant of Deng Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe names Deng Yang, courtesy name Xuanmao, a descendant of Deng Yu.

sentences.zh: 少得士名於京師。

translations.literal: In youth he early won gentlemen's fame in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He won scholarly fame in the capital while young.

sentences.zh: 明帝時爲尚書郎，除洛陽令，坐事免，拜中郎，又入兼中書郎。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time he was a gentleman of the Masters of Writing, appointed magistrate of Luoyang; because of an affair he was dismissed, appointed central gentleman, and again entered concurrently as gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he served as a Masters of Writing gentleman, then Luoyang magistrate; dismissed for an offense, he became a central gentleman and later concurrent Secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 初，颺與李勝等爲浮華友，及在中書，浮華事發，被斥出，遂不復用。

translations.literal: At first Yang with Li Sheng and others were flashy friends; when he was in the Secretariat the flashy affair broke out, he was expelled and dismissed, and thereafter was not again employed.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Sheng had been flashy companions; when the "flashy" scandal broke in the Secretariat he was expelled and never re-employed.

sentences.zh: 正始初，乃出爲潁川太守，轉大將軍長史，遷侍中尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he then went out as grand administrator of Yingchuan, transferred grand general's chief clerk, and was promoted palace attendant and secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhengshi he became governor of Yingchuan, then the grand general's chief clerk, then palace attendant and secretary.

sentences.zh: 颺爲人好貨，前在內職，許臧艾授以顯官，艾以父妾與颺，故京師爲之語曰：「以官易婦鄧玄茂。」

translations.literal: Yang as a man loved goods; formerly in inner office he promised Zang Ai an eminent office; Ai gave his father's concubine to Yang—therefore the capital made a saying for them: "Trade office for a wife—Deng Xuanmao."
translations.idiomatic: Yang loved profit; while in inner office he promised Zang Ai a high post in exchange for Ai's father's concubine—hence the capital jingle: "Trade office for a wife—Deng Xuanmao."

sentences.zh: 每所薦達，多如此比。

translations.literal: Each time he recommended and advanced men, mostly it was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his promotions followed that pattern.

sentences.zh: 故何晏選舉不得人，頗由颺之不公忠，遂同其罪，蓋由交友非其才。

translations.literal: Therefore He Yan's selections did not obtain worthy men—largely because of Yang's lack of fairness and loyalty; he therefore shared their crime, probably from befriending men not of their talent.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan's appointments failed largely because Yang was unfair; Yang shared their guilt for choosing unworthy friends.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：丁謐，字彥靖。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: Ding Mi, courtesy name Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe names Ding Mi, courtesy name Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 父斐，字文侯。

translations.literal: His father Fei, courtesy name Wenhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fei bore the courtesy name Wenhou.

sentences.zh: 初，斐隨太祖，太祖以斐鄉里，特饒愛之。

translations.literal: At first Fei followed the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor because Fei was of his home village especially indulged and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Fei had followed Cao Cao, who favored him as a townsman.

sentences.zh: 斐性好貨，數請求犯法，輒得原宥。

translations.literal: Fei's nature loved goods; he repeatedly requested and committed offenses and always obtained pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Fei loved profit, repeatedly offended, and was always pardoned.

sentences.zh: 爲典軍校尉，總攝內外，每所陳說，多見從之。

translations.literal: He was colonel of the army of records, comprehensively controlling inner and outer affairs; each time he stated proposals, mostly they were followed.
translations.idiomatic: As colonel of the army of records he controlled inner and outer affairs, and his proposals were usually followed.

sentences.zh: 建安末，從太祖征吳。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jian'an era he followed the Grand Progenitor campaigning against Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jian'an he followed the campaign against Wu.

sentences.zh: 斐隨行，自以家牛羸困，乃私易官牛，爲人所白，被收送獄，奪官。

translations.literal: Fei followed on the march; thinking his household oxen were weak and weary, he privately exchanged official oxen; someone reported him, he was seized and sent to prison, and his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he swapped his weak household oxen for official ones, was reported, jailed, and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 其後太祖問斐曰：「文侯，印綬所在？」

translations.literal: Afterward the Grand Progenitor asked Fei, saying: "Wenhou, where are the seals and ribbon?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao later asked, "Wenhou, where are your seals?"

sentences.zh: 斐亦知見戲，對曰：「以易餅耳。」

translations.literal: Fei also knew he was being teased and answered: "Exchanged for cakes, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the jest, Fei answered, "Traded for cakes."

sentences.zh: 太祖笑，顧謂左右曰：「東曹毛掾數白此家，欲令我重治，我非不知此人不清，良有以也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor laughed, turned and said to his attendants: "Eastern Bureau Clerk Mao several times reported this family, wishing to have me punish heavily; I am not unaware this man is not clean—there is good reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed and told attendants: "Clerk Mao of the Eastern Bureau keeps denouncing this man; I know he is crooked, yet I keep him.

sentences.zh: 我之有斐，譬如人家有盜狗而善捕鼠，盜雖有小損，而完我囊貯。」

translations.literal: My having Fei is like a household having a thieving dog that is good at catching rats—the theft though has small loss, yet it completes my bags and stores."
translations.idiomatic: Fei is like a thieving dog that catches rats—the petty theft is worth the full granary."

sentences.zh: 遂復斐官，聽用如初。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fei's office was restored and he was heard and employed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，病亡。

translations.literal: Several years later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness several years later.

sentences.zh: 謐少不肯交游，但博觀書傳。

translations.literal: Mi in youth would not associate; he only broadly viewed books and records.
translations.idiomatic: Mi in youth shunned company and read widely.

sentences.zh: 爲人沈毅，頗有才略。

translations.literal: As a man he was deep and resolute, with considerable talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was deep, resolute, and strategically gifted.

sentences.zh: 太和中，常住鄴，借人空屋，居其中。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he constantly dwelt at Ye, borrowed another's empty house, and lived within it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he lived at Ye in a borrowed empty house.

sentences.zh: 而諸王亦欲借之，不知謐已得，直開門入。

translations.literal: The various princes also wished to borrow it, not knowing Mi had already obtained it, and went straight in opening the door.
translations.idiomatic: Princes also wanted the house, unaware Mi had it, and walked straight in.

sentences.zh: 謐望見王，交脚臥而不起，而呼其奴客曰：「此何等人？

translations.literal: Mi saw the prince, lay cross-legged and did not rise, and called his servant-guests, saying: "What sort of people are these?
translations.idiomatic: Mi saw a prince, lay cross-legged without rising, and shouted to servants, "What sort are these?

sentences.zh: 促呵使去。」

translations.literal: Hurry—shout and make them leave."
translations.idiomatic: Drive them out!"

sentences.zh: 王怒其無禮，還具上言。

translations.literal: The prince was angry at his lack of courtesy and on returning fully reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, furious at the insult, reported him.

sentences.zh: 明帝收謐，繫鄴獄，以其功臣子，原出。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming seized Mi and imprisoned him in Ye jail; because he was a meritorious minister's son, he was pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming jailed him at Ye but released him as a hero's son.

sentences.zh: 後帝聞其有父風，召拜度支郎中。

translations.literal: Later the emperor heard he had his father's manner and summoned and appointed him gentleman of the revenue department.
translations.idiomatic: Later, hearing he had his father's ways, the emperor made him a revenue-department gentleman.

sentences.zh: 曹爽宿與相親，時爽爲武衞將軍，數爲帝稱其可大用。

translations.literal: Cao Shuang for long had been close to him; at that time Shuang was general who guards martial majesty and repeatedly for the emperor praised him as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang, long his friend while general who guards martial majesty, repeatedly praised him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，爽輔政，乃拔謐爲散騎常侍，遂轉尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Shuang assisted government, and thereupon promoted Mi supernumerary cavalry attendant and then transferred him secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died and Shuang took power, Mi was made supernumerary cavalry attendant, then secretary.

sentences.zh: 謐爲人外似踈略，而內多忌。

translations.literal: Mi as a man outwardly seemed careless and broad, yet inwardly bore much jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly careless, Mi was inwardly jealous.

sentences.zh: 其在臺閣，數有所彈駮，臺中患之，事不得行。

translations.literal: When he was in the terrace offices he repeatedly had impeachments and rebuttals; the terrace offices resented him and affairs could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the central offices he blocked business with constant impeachments.

sentences.zh: 又其意輕貴，多所忽略，雖與何晏、鄧颺等同位，而皆少之，唯以勢屈於爽。

translations.literal: Moreover his intent slighted the honored; he on many occasions neglected them; though with He Yan and Deng Yang he was of equal rank, he all looked down on them—only because of power bowed to Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: He looked down on peers such as He Yan and Deng Yang, bowing only to Shuang's power.

sentences.zh: 爽亦敬之，言無不從。

translations.literal: Shuang also respected him; his words were without any not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang respected him and followed his every word.

sentences.zh: 故於時謗書，謂「臺中有三狗，二狗崖柴不可當，一狗憑默作疽囊。」

translations.literal: Therefore at the time lampoons said: "In the terrace offices there are three dogs—two dogs cliff firewood cannot be withstood, one dog relying on Mo becomes a carbuncle sack."
translations.idiomatic: A lampoon ran: "Three dogs in the offices—two dogs' cliff firewood none can withstand; one dog leans on Mo and festers like a boil."

sentences.zh: 三狗，謂何、鄧、丁也。

translations.literal: The three dogs mean He, Deng, and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The three dogs were He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi.

sentences.zh: 默者，爽小字也。

translations.literal: Mo is Shuang's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was Shuang's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 其意言三狗皆欲嚙人，而謐尤甚也。

translations.literal: Its meaning said the three dogs all wished to bite men, and Mi was especially so.
translations.idiomatic: All three bit at others; Mi most of all.

sentences.zh: 奏使郭太後出居別宮，及遣樂安王使北詣鄴，又遣文欽令還淮南，皆謐之計。

translations.literal: Memorializing to have Empress Dowager Guo move out to a separate palace, and dispatching Prince of Le'an north to Ye, and also dispatching Wen Qin to order return to Huainan—all were Mi's plans.
translations.idiomatic: Mi planned the dowager's removal to a separate palace, Prince of Le'an's dispatch north to Ye, and Wen Qin's recall to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 司馬宣王由是特深恨之。

translations.literal: Sima Yi, King of Xuan, on this account especially deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi therefore hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 畢軌，字昭先。

translations.literal: Bi Gui, courtesy name Zhaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Gui bore the courtesy name Zhaoxian.

sentences.zh: 父字子禮，建安中爲典農校尉。

translations.literal: His father's courtesy name was Zili; in the Jian'an era he was colonel of the agricultural colonies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zili had been an agricultural colonel in Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 軌以才能，少有名聲。

translations.literal: Gui because of talent and ability in youth had reputation and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Gui won early fame for talent.

sentences.zh: 明帝在東宮時，軌在文學中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was in the Eastern Palace, Gui was in the literary academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was crown prince, Gui served in the literary academy.

sentences.zh: 黃初末，出爲長史。

translations.literal: At the end of Huangchu he went out as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Huangchu he became a chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，入爲黃門郎，子尚公主，居處殷富。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming assumed the throne, he entered as gentleman of the Yellow Gates; his son married an imperial princess and his dwelling was rich.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he became a Yellow Gate gentleman; his son married a princess and his household grew wealthy.

sentences.zh: 遷并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred inspector of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Bing.

sentences.zh: 其在并州，名爲驕豪。

translations.literal: When he was in Bing province he was famed as arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: In Bing he earned a name for arrogance.

sentences.zh: 時雜虜數爲暴，害吏民，軌輒出軍擊鮮卑軻比能，失利。

translations.literal: At that time mixed barbarians repeatedly made raids and harmed officials and commoners; Gui then led troops out to strike the Xianbei Kebineng and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When barbarians raided, he marched against the Xianbei leader Kebineng and lost.

sentences.zh: 中護軍蔣濟表曰：「畢軌前失，旣往不咎，但恐是後難可以再。

translations.literal: Protector of the Army Jiang Ji memorialized, saying: "Bi Gui's former fault—what is past is not blamed; only I fear afterward it will be hard to have again.
translations.idiomatic: Protector of the Army Jiang Ji memorialized: "Gui's past fault should be forgiven, but repetition would be dangerous.

sentences.zh: 凡人材有長短，不可彊成。

translations.literal: Human talent has long and short; it cannot be forced to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Talents differ and cannot be forced.

sentences.zh: 軌文雅志意，自爲美器。

translations.literal: Gui's literary elegance of intent is in itself a fine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's cultivated mind makes him a fine instrument.

sentences.zh: 今失并州，換置他州，若入居顯職，不毀其德，於國事實善。

translations.literal: Now having lost Bing province, if he is exchanged and placed in another province, if he enters and occupies an eminent post without destroying his virtue, for state affairs it is truly good.
translations.idiomatic: Transfer him from Bing to another post without ruining his gifts, and the state will benefit.

sentences.zh: 此安危之要，唯聖恩察之。」

translations.literal: This is the crux of safety and peril—may the sage grace examine it."
translations.idiomatic: This bears on safety and peril—please consider it."

sentences.zh: 至正始中，入爲中護軍，轉侍中尚書，遷司隷校尉。

translations.literal: By the Zhengshi era he entered as protector of the army, transferred palace attendant and secretary, and was promoted commandant of Yong and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhengshi he was protector of the army, then palace attendant and secretary, then metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 素與曹爽善，每言於爽，多見從之。

translations.literal: He for long was on good terms with Cao Shuang; each time he spoke to Shuang, mostly he was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Long friendly with Shuang, he was usually obeyed.

sentences.zh: 李勝字公昭。

translations.literal: Li Sheng, courtesy name Gongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng bore the courtesy name Gongzhao.

sentences.zh: 父休字子朗，有智略。

translations.literal: His father Xiu, courtesy name Zilang, had wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiu, styled Zilang, was a strategist.

sentences.zh: 張魯前爲鎮北將軍，休爲司馬，家南鄭。

translations.literal: Before Zhang Lu was general who guards the north, Xiu was marshal; his family was at Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Lu was general who guards the north, Xiu served as his marshal at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 時漢中有甘露降，子朗見張魯精兵數萬人，有四塞之固，遂建言赤氣久衰，黃家當興，欲魯舉號，魯不聽。

translations.literal: At that time in Hanzhong sweet dew descended; Zilang saw Zhang Lu's crack troops numbered tens of thousands and had the strength of four passes, and thereupon advised that red vapor had long declined and the Yellow House ought to rise, wishing Lu to assume title; Lu did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When sweet dew fell in Hanzhong, Zilang urged Zhang Lu, with tens of thousands of troops and a fortress in four directions, to declare himself emperor as the Han mandate waned; Lu refused.

sentences.zh: 會魯破，太祖以其勸魯內附，賜爵關內侯，署散官騎從，詣鄴。

translations.literal: When Lu was broken, the Grand Progenitor because he had urged Lu to submit inward bestowed the rank of marquis within the passes, appointed him supernumerary cavalry follower, and sent him to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu's defeat Cao Cao enfeoffed Xiu as a marquis within the passes for urging submission and sent him to Ye.

sentences.zh: 至黃初中，仕歷上黨、鉅鹿二郡太守，後以年老還，拜議郎。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Huangchu he served successively as grand administrator of Shangdang and Julu commanderies; afterward because of old age he returned and was appointed adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu he governed Shangdang and Julu, then retired as an adviser.

sentences.zh: 勝少游京師，雅有才智，與曹爽善。

translations.literal: Sheng in youth traveled the capital, elegantly had talent and wisdom, and was on good terms with Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng traveled the capital in youth, showed talent, and befriended Shuang.

sentences.zh: 明帝禁浮華，而人白勝堂有四䆫八達，各有主名。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming forbade flashiness, and someone reported Sheng's hall had four-window eight-path openings, each with a master's name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming banned flashy display; someone reported that Sheng's hall had "four windows and eight openings," each named for a patron.

sentences.zh: 用是被收，以其所連引者多，故得原，禁錮數歲。

translations.literal: On this account he was seized; because those he implicated in succession were many, he obtained pardon, and was confined for several years.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested but pardoned because many were implicated; he was confined several years.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，曹爽輔政，勝爲洛陽令。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Cao Shuang assisted government; Sheng was magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death Shuang made him Luoyang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 夏侯玄爲征西將軍，以勝爲長史。

translations.literal: Xiahou Xuan was General Who Conquers the West and made Sheng chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xuan as General Who Conquers the West made Sheng his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 玄亦宿與勝厚。

translations.literal: Xuan also for long had been thick with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had long been close to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 駱穀之役，議從勝出，由是司馬宣王不恱於勝。

translations.literal: In the Luogu campaign the deliberation followed Sheng's proposal to advance; on this account Sima Yi, King of Xuan, was not pleased with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the Luogu campaign Sheng's plan was adopted, and Sima Yi disliked him for it.

sentences.zh: 累遷熒陽太守、河南尹。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted grand administrator of Yingyang and governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Yingyang and then Henan.

sentences.zh: 勝前後所宰守，未嘗不稱職，爲尹歲餘，廳事前屠蘇壞，令人更治之，小材一枚激墮，正檛受符吏石虎頭，斷之。

translations.literal: Where Sheng before and after administered and guarded, never was he not called competent; as governor for more than a year, the suzu before the hall office broke; he had men repair it; a small timber piece was struck and fell, just striking the clerk receiving credentials Shi Hutou and breaking him.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held won praise; as Henan governor, a repair timber in his hall fell and killed clerk Shi Hutou who was receiving credentials.

sentences.zh: 後旬日，遷爲荊州刺史，未及之官而敗也。

translations.literal: After ten days he was transferred governor of Jing province; before he could reach office he was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he was made governor of Jing but fell before taking office.

sentences.zh: 桓範字元則，世爲冠族。

translations.literal: Huan Fan, courtesy name Yuanze, for generations a leading clan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Fan, styled Yuanze, came from a leading clan.

sentences.zh: 建安末，入丞相府。

translations.literal: At the end of Jian'an he entered the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jian'an he entered the chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 延康中，爲羽林左監。

translations.literal: In the Yankang era he was left colonel of the feathered forest.
translations.idiomatic: In Yankang he was left colonel of the feathered forest.

sentences.zh: 以有文學，與王象等典集皇覽。

translations.literal: Because he had literary learning, together with Wang Xiang and others he directed compilation of the Imperial Overview.
translations.idiomatic: For his scholarship he helped Wang Xiang compile the Imperial Overview.

sentences.zh: 明帝時爲中領軍尚書，遷征虜將軍、東中郎將，使持節都督青、徐諸軍事，治下邳。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time he was chief of the palace guard and secretary, transferred General Who Captures Barbarians and east central commander, bearing credentials as commander-in-chief directing Qing and Xu military affairs, administering at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was chief of the palace guard and secretary, then general who captures barbarians and east central commander with credentials over Qing and Xu from Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 與徐州刺史鄭岐爭屋，引節欲斬岐，爲岐所奏，不直，坐免還。

translations.literal: With Inspector of Xu Province Zheng Qi he quarreled over a house; drawing his credentials he wished to behead Qi; Qi memorialized against him; he was not in the right and sat dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with Xu inspector Zheng Qi over a house, drew credentials to behead him, was impeached, found in the wrong, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 復爲兖州刺吏，怏怏不得意。

translations.literal: He again became inspector of Yan province, discontent and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: He became inspector of Yan, sullen and unhappy.

sentences.zh: 又聞當轉爲冀州牧。

translations.literal: He also heard he was about to be transferred provincial shepherd of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He then heard he was to become shepherd of Ji.

sentences.zh: 是時冀州統屬鎮北，而鎮北將軍呂昭才實仕進，本在範後。

translations.literal: At that time Ji province was under the general who guards the north, and General Who Guards the North Lü Zhao's talent and substance in official advancement originally came after Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was then under General Who Guards the North Lü Zhao, whom Fan outranked in seniority yet resented.

sentences.zh: 範謂其妻仲長曰：「我寧作諸卿，向三公長跪耳，不能爲呂子展屈也。」

translations.literal: Fan said to his wife Zhongchang: "I would rather be among you gentlemen, facing the three dukes kneeling long, than bow to Lü Zizhan."
translations.idiomatic: Fan told his wife Zhongchang, "I would rather kneel before the Three Excellencies than bow to Lü Zizhan."

sentences.zh: 其妻曰：「君前在東，坐欲擅斬徐州刺史，衆人謂君難爲作下，今復羞爲呂屈，是復難爲作上也。」

translations.literal: His wife said: "Your lordship before in the east, sitting, wished on his own authority to behead the inspector of Xu province; the multitude said your lordship would be hard to make a subordinate—now again ashamed to bow to Lü, this again is hard to make a superior."
translations.idiomatic: His wife replied, "In the east you nearly beheaded Xu's inspector and were called unfit to serve below—now you refuse to bow to Lü; are you fit to rule above?"

sentences.zh: 範忿其言觸實，乃以刀環撞其腹。

translations.literal: Fan was angry that her words touched reality and thereupon struck her belly with a knife ring.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged that she spoke truth, Fan struck her pregnant belly with a knife ring.

sentences.zh: 妻時懷孕，遂墮胎死。

translations.literal: His wife at the time was pregnant; thereupon she miscarried and died.
translations.idiomatic: She miscarried and died.

sentences.zh: 範亦竟稱疾，不赴冀州。

translations.literal: Fan also in the end claimed illness and did not go to Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Fan claimed illness and never went to Ji.

sentences.zh: 正始中拜大司農。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was appointed grand minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi he became grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 範前在臺閣，號爲曉事，及爲司農，又以清省稱。

translations.literal: Fan before in the terrace offices was called one who understood affairs; when he became minister of agriculture he was again famed for purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Once famed in the central offices for knowing affairs, as minister of agriculture he was praised for frugality.

sentences.zh: 範嘗抄撮《漢書》中諸雜事，自以意斟酌之，名曰世要論。

translations.literal: Fan once copied and gathered miscellaneous matters from the Book of Han, weighed them by his own intent, and titled it Essentials of the Age Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled excerpts from the Book of Han into his Essentials of the Age Treatise.

sentences.zh: 蔣濟爲太尉，嘗與範會社下，羣卿列坐有數人，範懷其所撰，欲以示濟，謂濟當虛心觀之。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji was grand commandant; he once with Fan met below the altar to the soil god; the assembled ministers sat in rows numbering several men; Fan carried what he had composed and wished to show Ji, thinking Ji ought to view it with an open mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Commandant Jiang Ji met Fan at an earth-god rite, Fan meant to show him his book.

sentences.zh: 範出其書以示左右，左右傳之示濟，濟不肯視，範心恨之。

translations.literal: Fan took out his book and showed it to his attendants; the attendants passed it to show Ji; Ji would not look; Fan inwardly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan passed the book along; Ji refused to read it, and Fan resented him.

sentences.zh: 因論他事，乃發怒謂濟曰：「我祖薄德，公輩何似邪？」

translations.literal: Because they discussed other matters, he thereupon grew angry and said to Ji: "My ancestor's thin virtue—what are you gentlemen like?"
translations.idiomatic: Changing the subject in anger, Fan snapped, "My house has thin virtue—what are men like you?"

sentences.zh: 濟性雖彊毅，亦知範剛毅，睨而不應，各罷。

translations.literal: Ji's nature though was strong and resolute, he also knew Fan was firm and resolute; he glanced and did not answer; each withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji, though tough, knew Fan's temper; he glanced away and they parted.

sentences.zh: 範於沛郡，仕次在曹真後。

translations.literal: Fan in Pei commandery in official seniority came after Cao Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In Pei commandery Fan ranked after Cao Zhen.

sentences.zh: 於時曹爽輔政，以範鄉里老宿，於九卿中特敬之，然不甚親也。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Shuang assisted government; because Fan was an elder of the home village, among the nine ministers he especially respected him, yet was not very close.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang governed he respected Fan as a hometown elder but was not intimate.

sentences.zh: 及宣王起兵，閉城門，以範爲曉事，乃指召之，欲使領中領軍。

translations.literal: When the King of Xuan raised troops and closed the city gates, because Fan was called one who understood affairs, he was pointed to and summoned, wishing to have him lead the chief of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi closed the gates, he summoned Fan, famed for knowing affairs, to lead the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 範欲應召，而其子諫之，以車駕在外，不如南出。

translations.literal: Fan wished to answer the summons, but his son remonstrated, saying the imperial carriage was outside and it was better to go south.
translations.idiomatic: Fan meant to obey, but his son urged flight south while the emperor was abroad.

sentences.zh: 範疑有頃，兒又促之。

translations.literal: Fan hesitated a moment; the son again urged him.
translations.idiomatic: He hesitated; his son urged again.

sentences.zh: 範欲去而司農丞吏皆止範。

translations.literal: Fan wished to go but the minister of agriculture's clerks all stopped Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks tried to stop him.

sentences.zh: 範不從，乃突出至平昌城門，城門已閉。

translations.literal: Fan did not follow, and thereupon burst out reaching Pingchang city gate; the city gate was already closed.
translations.idiomatic: Fan broke through to Pingchang Gate, already shut.

sentences.zh: 門候司蕃，故範舉吏也，範呼之，舉手中版以示之，矯曰：「有詔召我，卿促開門！」

translations.literal: Gate warden Si Fan was formerly Fan's nominated clerk; Fan called him, raised the tablet in his hand to show him, and falsely said: "There is an edict summoning me—you hurry and open the gate!"
translations.idiomatic: Gate warden Si Fan, once Fan's nominee, was hailed with a forged summons: "Open the gate!"

sentences.zh: 蕃欲求見詔書，範呵之，言「卿非我故吏邪，何以敢爾？」

translations.literal: Fan wished to see the edict document; Fan shouted at him, saying "Are you not my old clerk—how dare you thus?"
translations.idiomatic: When Si Fan asked to see the edict, Fan roared, "You were my clerk—how dare you?"

sentences.zh: 乃開之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened it.
translations.idiomatic: The gate opened.

sentences.zh: 範出城，顧謂蕃曰：「太傅圖逆，卿從我去！」

translations.literal: Fan left the city, turned and said to Fan: "The Grand Tutor plots rebellion—you follow me and go!"
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the city Fan called back, "The Grand Tutor rebels—come with me!"

sentences.zh: 蕃徒行不能及，遂避側。

translations.literal: Fan went on foot and could not catch up; thereupon he avoided to the side.
translations.idiomatic: Si Fan on foot could not catch up and hid aside.

sentences.zh: 範南見爽，勸爽兄弟以天子詣許昌，徵四方以自輔。

translations.literal: Fan went south and saw Shuang; he urged Shuang's brothers to take the Son of Heaven to Xuchang and summon the four quarters to assist themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Fan rode south to Shuang and urged him to take the emperor to Xuchang and summon armies from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 爽疑，羲又無言。

translations.literal: Shuang hesitated; Xi again had no words.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang hesitated; Xi said nothing.

sentences.zh: 範自謂羲曰：「事昭然，卿用讀書何爲邪！

translations.literal: Fan himself said to Xi: "The affair is obvious—what use is your reading books!
translations.idiomatic: Fan told Xi, "The case is clear—what good is all your reading?

sentences.zh: 於今日卿等門戶倒矣！」

translations.literal: On this day your house's gate is overturned!"
translations.idiomatic: Today your house is finished!"

sentences.zh: 俱不言。

translations.literal: Both did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Neither answered.

sentences.zh: 範又謂羲曰：「卿別營近在闕南，洛陽典農治在城外，呼召如意。

translations.literal: Fan again said to Xi: "Your separate camp is near south of the palace; Luoyang's agricultural directorate administers outside the city—calling and summoning would be as wished.
translations.idiomatic: Fan added, "Your separate camp lies south of the palace; Luoyang's agricultural office is outside the walls—call them at will.

sentences.zh: 今詣許昌，不過中宿，許昌別庫，足相被假；

translations.literal: Now going to Xuchang, not passing midnight lodging; Xuchang's separate storehouses are enough to lend to each other;
translations.idiomatic: Reach Xuchang by midnight; its storehouses can supply you;

sentences.zh: 所憂當在穀食，而大司農印章在我身。」

translations.literal: what ought to be worried about is grain food, yet the grand minister of agriculture's seal is on my person."
translations.idiomatic: grain is the worry, and I hold the minister of agriculture's seal."

sentences.zh: 羲兄弟默然不從，中夜至五鼓，爽乃投刀於地，謂諸從駕羣臣曰：「我度太傅意，亦不過欲令我兄弟向己也。

translations.literal: Xi's brothers were silent and did not follow; at midnight until the fifth watch Shuang then threw his knife to the ground and said to the various ministers following the carriage: "I gauge the Grand Tutor's intent—nothing more than wishing to have us brothers turn toward himself.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers stayed silent; at the fifth watch Shuang threw down his sword and told the court, "I think the Grand Tutor only wants us to submit.

sentences.zh: 我獨有以不合於遠近耳！」

translations.literal: I alone have what does not accord with near and far!"
translations.idiomatic: I alone have failed the realm!"

sentences.zh: 遂進謂帝曰：「陛下作詔免臣官，報皇太後令。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced and said to the emperor: "Your Majesty compose an edict dismissing our offices and report the empress dowager's order."
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor, "Issue an edict dismissing us and report the empress dowager's order."

sentences.zh: 範知爽首免而己必坐唱義也。

translations.literal: Fan knew Shuang would be the first dismissed and he himself would surely sit for advocating righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Fan knew Shuang would surrender first and he would pay for urging resistance.

sentences.zh: 範乃曰：「老子今茲坐卿兄弟族矣！」

translations.literal: Fan then said: "Laozi this year sits your brothers' clans!"
translations.idiomatic: Fan cried, "This year I sit with your whole clan!"

sentences.zh: 爽等旣免，帝還宮，遂令範隨從。

translations.literal: When Shuang and the others were dismissed, the emperor returned to the palace and thereupon ordered Fan to follow.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuang surrendered, the emperor returned to the palace with Fan in tow.

sentences.zh: 到洛水浮橋北，望見宣王，下車叩頭而無言。

translations.literal: Reaching north of the Luoshui floating bridge, he saw the King of Xuan, descended from the carriage, kowtowed, and had no words.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Luoshui floating bridge he saw Sima Yi, descended, and kowtowed in silence.

sentences.zh: 宣王呼範姓曰：「桓大夫何爲爾邪！」

translations.literal: The King of Xuan called Fan's surname, saying: "Grandee Huan—why act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi called, "Grandee Huan—why act thus?"

sentences.zh: 車駕入宮，有詔範還復位。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage entered the palace; there was an edict that Fan return and resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Fan to office.

sentences.zh: 範詣闕拜章謝，待報。

translations.literal: Fan went to the palace gate, bowed in a memorial apologizing, and awaited reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fan submitted an apology at the palace gate and waited.

sentences.zh: 會司蕃詣鴻臚自首，具說範前臨出所道。

translations.literal: It happened that Si Fan went to the grand herald to surrender himself and fully stated what Fan had said on leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Si Fan surrendered to the grand herald and reported Fan's words at the gate.

sentences.zh: 宣王乃忿然曰：「誣人以反，於法何應？」

translations.literal: The King of Xuan thereupon said in anger: "Falsely accusing a man of rebellion—in law what is the response?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi demanded, "What is the penalty for falsely crying rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 主者曰：「科律，反受其罪。」

translations.literal: The responsible officer said: "In statute law, the false accuser receives the crime."
translations.idiomatic: The officer answered, "The accuser suffers the crime."

sentences.zh: 乃收範於闕下。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fan was seized below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was seized below the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 時人持範甚急，範謂部官曰：「徐之，我亦義士耳。」

translations.literal: Men of the time seized Fan very urgently; Fan said to the office officers: "Slowly—I am also a man of righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: As officers seized him, Fan said, "Slowly—I too am a man of honor."

sentences.zh: 遂送廷尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：初，爽夢二虎銜雷公，雷公若二升椀，放著庭中。

translations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: At first Shuang dreamed two tigers held the Lord of Thunder; the Lord of Thunder was like a two-sheng bowl, placed in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Shuang dreamed two tigers holding the Thunder Lord, sized like a two-sheng bowl, set in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 爽惡之，以問占者，靈臺丞馬訓曰：「憂兵。」

translations.literal: Shuang hated it and asked the diviner; Director of the Spirit Terrace Ma Xun said: "Worry over troops."
translations.idiomatic: He asked diviners; Ma Xun of the Spirit Terrace said, "Troops bring trouble."

sentences.zh: 訓退，告其妻曰：「爽將以兵亡，不出旬日。」

translations.literal: Xun withdrew and told his wife: "Shuang will perish by troops, not outside ten days."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun withdrew and told his wife, "Shuang will die by arms within ten days."

sentences.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：安定皇甫謐以九年冬夢至洛陽，自廟出，見車騎甚衆，以物呈廟云：「誅大將軍曹爽。」
