translations.literal: The Han–Jin Annals states: Huangfu Mi of Anding in the winter of the ninth year dreamed he reached Luoyang; from the temple he went out and saw chariots and horsemen very numerous; he presented an object to the temple saying: "Execute the grand general Cao Shuang."
translations.idiomatic: The Han–Jin chunqiu says Huangfu Mi of Anding dreamed in winter of the ninth year that he reached Luoyang, left a temple amid vast chariots, and presented an offering: "Execute Grand General Cao Shuang."

sentences.zh: 寤而以告其邑人，邑人曰：「君欲作曹人之夢乎！

translations.literal: Awakening, he told his townsman; the townsman said: "Your lordship wishes to make a Cao man's dream!
translations.idiomatic: Awake, he told a townsman, who scoffed, "You dream like a Cao man!

sentences.zh: 朝無公孫彊如何？

translations.literal: At court there is no Gongsun Jiang—how so?
translations.idiomatic: Where is there a Gongsun Jiang at court?

sentences.zh: 且爽兄弟典重兵，又權尚書事，誰敢謀之？」

translations.literal: Moreover Shuang's brothers control heavy troops and again hold power over the Masters of Writing—who dares plot against them?"
translations.idiomatic: Shuang and his brothers hold the army and the Secretariat—who would dare plot?"

sentences.zh: 謐曰：「爽無叔振鐸之請，苟失天機則離矣，何恃於彊？

translations.literal: Mi said: "Shuang has no uncle Zhen Duo's request; if he loses Heaven's opportunity then he is separated—what reliance on strength?
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied, "Shuang lacks an uncle's plea for mercy; lose Heaven's moment and power avails nothing.

sentences.zh: 昔漢之閻顯，倚母後之尊，權國威命，可謂至重矣，閹人十九人一旦尸之，況爽兄弟乎？」

translations.literal: In the past Han's Yan Xian relied on the empress dowager's honor, wielded the state's awesome command—one may say extremely heavy; nineteen eunuchs in one morning made corpses of them—how much more Shuang's brothers?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xian of Han leaned on the empress dowager yet nineteen eunuchs slew him in a morning—how much less can Shuang rely on force?"

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：初，爽出，司馬魯芝留在府，聞有事，將營騎斫津門出赴爽。

translations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: At first when Shuang went out, Sima Luzhi remained in the office; hearing there was an affair, he was about to lead camp cavalry to cut through Jinfang Gate and go out to join Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says when Shuang marched out, Sima Luzhi in the office heard trouble and prepared to cut through Jinfang Gate with cavalry to join him.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，擢爲御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed, he was promoted commandant of the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuang's execution Luzhi was promoted commandant of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 及爽解印綬，將出，主簿楊綜止之曰：「公挾主握權，捨此以至東巿乎？」

translations.literal: When Shuang removed seals and ribbon and was about to go out, chief clerk Yang Zong stopped him, saying: "Your lordship holds the ruler and wields power—abandon this to reach the eastern market?"
translations.idiomatic: As Shuang surrendered his seals, chief clerk Yang Zong stopped him: "You hold the emperor and power—will you abandon this for the execution ground?"

sentences.zh: 爽不從。

translations.literal: Shuang did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 有司奏綜導爽反，宣王曰：「各爲其主也。」

translations.literal: The responsible office memorialized that Zong guided Shuang in rebellion; the King of Xuan said: "Each served his lord."
translations.idiomatic: Authorities accused Zong of abetting rebellion; Sima Yi said, "Each served his lord."

sentences.zh: 宥之，以爲尚書郎。

translations.literal: He pardoned him and made him gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned and made a Masters of Writing gentleman.

sentences.zh: 芝字世英，扶風人也。

translations.literal: Zhi's courtesy name was Shiying; he was a man of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhi, styled Shiying, was from Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 以後仕進至特進光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later in official advancement he reached special advancement and household counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to special advancement and household counsellor.

sentences.zh: 綜字初伯，後爲安東將軍司馬文王長史。

translations.literal: Zong's courtesy name was Chubo; later he was chief clerk to General Who Guards the East Sima Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, styled Chubo, later became chief clerk to Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：夏侯湛爲芝銘及干寶晉紀並云爽旣誅，宣王即擢芝爲并州刺史，以綜爲安東參軍。

translations.literal: Commentator Pei Songzhi notes: Xiahou Zhan composed Zhi's epitaph and Gan Bao's Jin Annals both say that when Shuang was already executed, the King of Xuan immediately promoted Zhi inspector of Bing and made Zong an army staff officer to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Xiahou Zhan's epitaph and Gan Bao's Jin ji make Luzhi inspector of Bing and Zong an eastern staff officer immediately after Shuang's fall.

sentences.zh: 與《世語》不同。

translations.literal: It differs from the Worldly Talk.
translations.idiomatic: This differs from the Shiyu.

sentences.zh: 嘉平中，紹功臣世，封真族孫熙爲新昌亭侯，邑三百戶，以奉真後。

translations.literal: In the Jiaping era the meritorious ministers' lines were continued; Zhen's collateral descendant Xi was enfeoffed village marquis of Xinchang, fief three hundred households, to continue Zhen's line.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiaping era Cao Zhen's collateral descendant Xi was enfeoffed village marquis of Xinchang with three hundred households to continue Zhen's sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 干寶《晉紀》曰：蔣濟以曹真之勳力，不宜絕祀，故以熙爲後。

translations.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Annals states: Jiang Ji because Cao Zhen's meritorious strength ought not to have sacrifices cut off, therefore made Xi his successor.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's Jin ji says Jiang Ji secured the enfeoffment lest Cao Zhen's line die out.

sentences.zh: 濟又病其言之失信於爽，發病卒。

translations.literal: Ji again was ill that his words had broken faith with Shuang and died of the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji, ashamed that his counsel had misled Shuang, sickened and died.

sentences.zh: 晏，何進孫也。

translations.literal: Yan was He Jin’s grandson.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan was the grandson of He Jin.

sentences.zh: 母尹氏，爲太祖夫人。

translations.literal: His mother was the Lady Yin, who became the Grand Progenitor’s consort.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Yin, entered Cao Cao’s harem as a consort.

sentences.zh: 晏長於宮省，又尚公主，少以才秀知名，好老莊言，作《道德論》及諸文賦著述凡數十篇。

translations.literal: Yan grew up in the palace precincts, again married a princess, in youth was known for talent and distinction, loved Laozi and Zhuangzi’s words, and wrote the Discourse on the Way and Virtue and various literary rhapsodies and compositions totaling several tens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up inside the palace, married an imperial princess, won early fame as a prodigy, doted on Laozi and Zhuangzi, and produced the Dao de lun plus dozens of essays and fu.

sentences.zh: 〈晏字平叔。

translations.literal: 〈Yan’s courtesy name was Pingshu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈His courtesy name was Pingshu.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：「太祖爲司空時，納晏母并收養晏，其時秦宜祿兒阿蘇亦隨母在公家，並見寵如公子。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: “When the Grand Progenitor was minister of works, he took Yan’s mother in marriage and also adopted and raised Yan; at that time Qin Yilu’s son A Su also followed his mother in the lord’s household, and together they were favored like noble sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary states: “When the Grand Progenitor was minister of works, he took Yan’s mother in marriage and also adopted and raised Yan; at that time Qin Yilu’s son A Su also followed his mother in the lord’s household, and together they were favored like noble sons.

sentences.zh: 蘇即朗也。

translations.literal: Su is namely Lang.
translations.idiomatic: That A Su is Qin Lang.

sentences.zh: 蘇性謹慎，而晏無所顧憚，服飾擬於太子，故文帝特憎之，每不呼其姓字，常謂之爲「假子」。

translations.literal: Su’s nature was cautious, but Yan had no scruples whatever; his clothing and adornments were modeled on the heir apparent’s, therefore Emperor Wen especially hated him, never called his surname and personal name, and always called him ‘false son’.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Lang was careful by temperament, but He Yan dressed and swaggered like the crown prince; Emperor Pi loathed him, never used his name, and called him the “sham son.”

sentences.zh: 晏尚主，又好色，故黃初時無所事任。

translations.literal: Yan had married a princess and again loved beauty; therefore in the Huangchu era he had no office or duty.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had married a princess and chased every pretty face, he held no post during the Huangchu years.

sentences.zh: 及明帝立，頗爲冗官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, he was largely a supernumerary official.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he idled in sinecures.

sentences.zh: 至正始初，曲合於曹爽，亦以才能，故爽用爲散騎侍郎，遷侍中尚書。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Zhengshi he bent to fit with Cao Shuang; also because of talent and ability, therefore Shuang employed him as supernumerary cavalry gentleman, promoted him to palace attendant and secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhengshi he curried favor with Cao Shuang; Shuang, valuing his brilliance, named him supernumerary cavalry gentleman, then palace attendant and secretary.

sentences.zh: 晏前以尚主，得賜爵爲列侯，又其母在內，晏性自喜，動靜粉白不去手，行步顧影。

translations.literal: Yan earlier because of marrying a princess had been granted a fief as full marquis, and moreover his mother was inside; Yan’s nature was self-pleased, in movement and repose powder white did not leave his hand, and walking he gazed at his shadow.
translations.idiomatic: His princess marriage had already won him a full marquisate, and with his mother still in the inner palace he grew vain, never without a cosmetic box, and minced along studying his reflection.

sentences.zh: 晏爲尚書，主選舉，其宿與之有舊者，多被拔擢。」

translations.literal: Yan as secretary directed selection and appointment; those with whom he had long-standing old ties were for the most part promoted and pulled up."
translations.idiomatic: As secretary he ran appointments and promoted every old crony in sight."

sentences.zh: 《魏末傳》曰：晏婦金鄉公主，即晏同母妹。

translations.literal: The Wei End Transmission states: Yan’s wife was the princess of Jinyang, who was Yan’s uterine younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei mo zhuan names his wife as the Princess of Jinyang—He Yan’s own younger sister by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 公主賢，謂其母沛王太妃曰：「晏爲惡日甚，將何保身？」

translations.literal: The princess was worthy; she said to her mother the grand consort of the Prince of Pei: “Yan’s evil grows daily severe; how will he preserve his body?”
translations.idiomatic: The princess was a woman of sense. She told her mother, the Princess Dowager of Pei, “He Yan’s crimes mount by the day—how will he save himself?”

sentences.zh: 母笑曰：「汝得無妬晏邪！」

translations.literal: The mother laughed saying: “Could it be you are jealous of Yan!”
translations.idiomatic: Her mother laughed, “You are simply jealous of your brother!”

sentences.zh: 俄而晏死。

translations.literal: Shortly Yan died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, He Yan was executed.

sentences.zh: 有一男，年五六歲，宣王遣人錄之。

translations.literal: He had one boy, age five or six sui; the King of Xuan sent men to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son of five or six; Sima Yi sent officers to take the child.

sentences.zh: 晏母歸藏其子王宮中，向使者搏頰，乞白活之，使者具以白宣王。

translations.literal: Yan’s mother returned and hid her grandson in the prince’s palace, toward the envoy beat her cheeks, begging to let him live white; the envoy fully reported it to the King of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan’s mother smuggled the boy into the Prince of Pei’s palace, then threw herself before the escort, slapping her own face and begging for the child’s life; the officer reported everything to Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 宣王亦聞晏婦有先見之言，心常嘉之；

translations.literal: The King of Xuan also heard Yan’s wife had had prescient words, and his heart always praised her;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi had also heard the princess’s warning and admired her judgment;

sentences.zh: 且爲沛王故，特原不殺。

translations.literal: moreover for the Prince of Pei’s sake, especially pardoned and did not kill.
translations.idiomatic: and for the prince’s sake he spared the boy.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：初，夏侯玄、何晏等名盛於時，司馬景王亦預焉。

translations.literal: The Wei Family Spring and Autumn states: at first Xiahou Xuan, He Yan, and others’ names flourished in the age; Sima Jingwang also joined them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu records that Xiahou Xuan, He Yan, and their circle once dominated polite society, and Sima Shi moved among them.

sentences.zh: 晏嘗曰：「唯深也，故能通天下之志，夏侯泰初是也；

translations.literal: Yan once said: “Only depth therefore can penetrate the wills of all under Heaven; Xiahou Taichu is such;
translations.idiomatic: He Yan once said, “Only depth can fathom the mind of the world—there stands Xiahou Xuan;

sentences.zh: 唯幾也，故能成天下之務，司馬子元是也；

translations.literal: only subtlety therefore can accomplish the tasks of all under Heaven; Sima Ziyuan is such;
translations.idiomatic: only subtlety can finish the world’s business—there stands Sima Shi;

sentences.zh: 惟神也，不疾而速，不行而至，吾聞其語，未見其人。」

translations.literal: only spirit, without haste yet swift, without moving yet arriving—I have heard the saying, but have not seen the person.”
translations.idiomatic: only the sage moves without haste yet arrives without walking—I have heard the phrase, but never met the man.”

sentences.zh: 蓋欲以神況諸己也。

translations.literal: He probably wished to compare spirit to himself.
translations.idiomatic: He meant the third name to be his own.

sentences.zh: 初，宣王使晏與治爽等獄。

translations.literal: At first the King of Xuan had Yan together try the case of Shuang and others’ prison.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi first set He Yan to interrogate Cao Shuang’s associates.

sentences.zh: 晏窮治黨與，冀以獲宥。

translations.literal: Yan exhaustively prosecuted the clique, hoping thereby to obtain pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan hounded every accomplice, hoping to buy mercy with zeal.

sentences.zh: 宣王曰：「凡有八族。」

translations.literal: The King of Xuan said: “In all there are eight clans.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi said, “Eight great houses are implicated.”

sentences.zh: 晏疏丁、鄧等七姓。

translations.literal: Yan listed seven surnames Ding, Deng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan named seven houses—the Ding, Deng, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 宣王曰：「未也。」

translations.literal: The King of Xuan said: “Not yet.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi said, “You are short one.”

sentences.zh: 晏窮急，乃曰：「豈謂晏乎！」

translations.literal: Yan pressed in extremity, then said: “Could it mean Yan!”
translations.idiomatic: He Yan, cornered, cried, “Surely you cannot mean me!”

sentences.zh: 宣王曰：「是也。」

translations.literal: The King of Xuan said: “It is so.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi answered, “Precisely you.”

sentences.zh: 乃收晏。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan was seized.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan was arrested.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：《魏末傳》云晏取其同母妹爲妻，此搢紳所不忍言，雖楚王之妻媦，不是甚也已。

translations.literal: Your servant Song Zhi investigates: the Wei End Transmission says Yan took his uterine younger sister as wife, which gentry cannot bear to speak; though the Chu king’s marriage to aunt and wife’s sister was not as extreme as this.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: the Wei mo zhuan claims He Yan married his own uterine younger sister—a deed polite society shrinks from naming; even the Chu king’s incestuous unions seem mild beside it.

sentences.zh: 設令此言出於舊史，猶將莫之或信，況厎下之書乎！

translations.literal: Supposing this saying came from an old history, still none would quite believe it, how much less a book from the bottom of the stack!
translations.idiomatic: If such a tale surfaced in a canonical history we would doubt it—how much more a gossip sheet from the gutter!

sentences.zh: 案

translations.literal: Investigate
translations.idiomatic: Note:

sentences.zh: 〈諸王公傳〉，

translations.literal: 〈Biographies of the various princes and kings〉,
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biographies of the imperial princes〉

sentences.zh: 沛王出自杜夫人所生。

translations.literal: the Prince of Pei was born of what Lady Du bore.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pei was Lady Du’s son by Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 晏母姓尹，公主若與沛王同生，焉得言與晏同母？

translations.literal: Yan’s mother’s surname was Yin; if the princess were born together with the Prince of Pei, how could it be said she shared a mother with Yan?
translations.idiomatic: He Yan’s mother was surnamed Yin; if the princess were Lady Du’s daughter like the Prince of Pei, she could not be He Yan’s uterine sister.

sentences.zh: 皇甫謐《烈女傳》曰：爽從弟文叔，妻譙郡夏侯文寧之女，名令女。

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi’s Biographies of Exemplary Women states: Shuang’s cousin Wen Shu’s wife was the daughter of Xiahou Wenning of Qiao commandery, named Lady Lingnu.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi’s Lienu zhuan tells of Lady Lingnu, daughter of Xiahou Wenning of Qiao, wife of Cao Wen Shu, a cousin of Cao Shuang.

sentences.zh: 文叔早死，服闋，自以年少無子，恐家必嫁己，乃斷髮以爲信。

translations.literal: Wen Shu died early; when mourning was ended, she because she was young and without sons feared the family would surely marry her off, then cut her hair to make a pledge.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Shu died young she finished mourning, knew she was childless and still in her prime, and feared her in-laws would remarry her; she sheared her hair as a vow of widowhood.

sentences.zh: 其後，家果欲嫁之，令女聞，即復以刀截兩耳，居止常依爽。

translations.literal: Afterward the family indeed wished to marry her off; when Lady Lingnu heard, then again with a knife cut off both ears, and in dwelling always relied on Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: When the clan pressed a new marriage she sliced off both ears with a knife and clung to Cao Shuang’s protection.

sentences.zh: 及爽被誅，曹氏盡死。

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed, the house of Cao all died.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuang fell, every Cao kinsman linked to him was put to death.

sentences.zh: 令女叔父上書與曹氏絕婚，彊迎令女歸。

translations.literal: Lady Lingnu’s paternal uncle memorialized to break marriage with the Caos and forcibly welcomed Lady Lingnu home.
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle petitioned to annul the marriage to the Caos and had her dragged home by force.

sentences.zh: 時文寧爲梁相，憐其少，執義，又曹氏無遺類，冀其意沮，迺微使人諷之。

translations.literal: At that time Wenning was minister of Liang, pitied her youth, held to righteousness, and moreover the Caos had no survivors left; he hoped her intent would flag, then secretly sent someone to sound her out.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xiahou Wenning, then minister of Liang, pitied her youth and upright heart, knew the Cao line was extinct, and hoped her resolve would weaken; he sent a private messenger to probe her mood.

sentences.zh: 令女歎且泣曰：「吾亦惟之，許之是也。」

translations.literal: Lady Lingnu sighed and wept saying: “I have also thought of it; consenting is right.”
translations.idiomatic: She sighed through tears, “I have weighed it—perhaps I should yield.”

sentences.zh: 家以爲信，防之少懈。

translations.literal: The family deemed it sincere and guarded her a little slackly.
translations.idiomatic: The household took her at her word and relaxed the watch.

sentences.zh: 令女於是竊入寢室，以刀斷鼻，蒙被而臥。

translations.literal: Lady Lingnu thereupon secretly entered the bedchamber, with a knife cut off her nose, covered herself with a quilt and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: She stole to her chamber, cut off her nose with a knife, and lay swathed in quilts.

sentences.zh: 其母呼與語，不應，發被視之，血流滿牀席。

translations.literal: Her mother called and spoke to her; she did not answer; lifting the quilt and looking, blood flowed full over the mat and seat.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother called; she did not answer. Throwing back the coverlet they found the bed awash with blood.

sentences.zh: 舉家驚惶，奔往視之，莫不酸鼻。

translations.literal: The whole household was alarmed and rushed to look on her; none did not ache in the nose.
translations.idiomatic: The kinfolk ran in panic; every onlooker felt a stab in the nose.

sentences.zh: 或謂之曰：「人生世間，如輕塵棲弱草耳，何至辛苦迺爾！

translations.literal: Someone said to her: “Human life in the world is like light dust resting on weak grass—how reach such bitter hardship!
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged her, “Life is dust on dew—why torture yourself so?

sentences.zh: 且夫家夷滅已盡，守此欲誰爲哉？」

translations.literal: Moreover your husband’s house is exterminated to the end; guarding this—for whom is it?”
translations.idiomatic: Your husband’s clan is extinct—who benefits from this mutilation?”

sentences.zh: 令女曰：「聞仁者不以盛衰改節，義者不以存亡易心，曹氏前盛之時，尚欲保終，況今衰亡，何忍棄之！

translations.literal: Lady Lingnu said: “I have heard the benevolent do not change integrity with flourishing or decline, the principled do not change heart with survival or destruction; when the house of Cao was flourishing before, I still wished to preserve myself to the end; how much more now in decline and destruction—how could I bear to abandon them!
translations.idiomatic: She answered, “They say the humane do not bend principle to fortune, the righteous do not swap loyalty for life. While the Caos flourished I meant to see my vow through; now that they are gone, how could I betray them?

sentences.zh: 禽獸不行，吾豈爲乎？」

translations.literal: Beasts and birds will not do it—how could I do it?”
translations.idiomatic: Birds and beasts would not stoop so low—shall I?”

sentences.zh: 司馬宣王聞而嘉之，聽使乞子字養，爲曹氏後，名顯於世。〉

translations.literal: Sima Yi, King of Xuan, heard and commended her, allowed her to beg a son to adopt and raise as heir for the Caos, and her name was illustrious in the world.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi praised her, let her adopt an heir for the extinguished Cao house, and her fame spread through the realm.〉

sentences.zh: 夏侯尚

translations.literal: Xiahou Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Shang.

sentences.zh: 夏侯尚字伯仁，淵從子也。

translations.literal: Xiahou Shang, courtesy name Boren, was a nephew of Xiahou Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Shang, styled Boren, was a nephew of Xiahou Yuan.

sentences.zh: 文帝與之親友。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was intimate friends with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen counted him among his closest friends.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：尚有籌畫智略，文帝器之，與爲布衣之交。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Wei states: Shang had planning and stratagem; Emperor Wen valued him and was with him in friendship of common cloth.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu says Shang was a strategist whom Emperor Wen prized as a friend from commoner days.〉

sentences.zh: 太祖定冀州，尚爲軍司馬，將騎從征伐，後爲五官將文學。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor settled Ji province, Shang was army marshal, led cavalry and followed on campaigns, afterward was literary attendant to the heir apparent of the five offices.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao conquered Ji, Shang served as army marshal, led cavalry on campaign, then became literary aide to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the state of Wei was first established, he was promoted to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the kingdom of Wei was founded he rose to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 代郡胡叛，遣鄢陵侯彰征討之，以尚參彰軍事，定代地，還。

translations.literal: The Hu of Dai commandery rebelled; the Marquis of Yanling, Cao Zhang, was sent to punish them; Shang joined Zhang’s army staff, settled Dai territory, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hu of Dai rebelled, Cao Zhang, Marquis of Yanling, was sent against them with Shang on his staff; they pacified Dai and marched home.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩於洛陽，尚持節，奉梓宮還鄴。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor died at Luoyang, Shang held the credentials of office and escorted the catafalque back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao died at Luoyang, Shang carried the imperial baton and convoyed the bier to Ye.

sentences.zh: 并錄前功，封平陵亭侯，拜散騎常侍，遷中領軍。

translations.literal: Together his previous achievements were recorded; he was enfeoffed village marquis of Pingling, appointed supernumerary cavalry attendant, and promoted chief of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: His past service was entered in the rolls; he received the village marquisate of Pingling, was named supernumerary cavalry attendant, then chief of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，更封平陵鄉侯，遷征南將軍，領荊州刺史，假節都督南方諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, his fief was changed to village marquis of Pingling, he was promoted general who campaigns south, concurrently inspector of Jing province, was given the credentials of office and supervised the various southern military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the throne Shang’s fief shifted to Pingling village, he became general of the southern expedition with concurrent duty as Jing provincial inspector, baton in hand over all southern armies.

sentences.zh: 尚奏：「劉備別軍在上庸，山道險難，彼不我虞，若以奇兵潛行，出其不意，則獨克之勢也。」

translations.literal: Shang memorialized: “Liu Bei’s detached army is at Shangyong; mountain roads are perilous and hard; they will not guard against us; if with a surprise host we go secretly and catch them unawares, then it is the posture of being able to conquer alone.”
translations.idiomatic: Shang memorialized: “Liu Bei’s detached force holds Shangyong over treacherous mountain tracks; they will not expect us. A silent column that strikes from nowhere can take them alone.”

sentences.zh: 遂勒諸軍擊破上庸，平三郡九縣，遷征南大將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he commanded the various armies, smashed Shangyong, pacified three commanderies and nine counties, and was promoted grand general who campaigns south.
translations.idiomatic: He led the combined hosts, stormed Shangyong, reduced three commanderies and nine counties, and was raised to grand general of the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 孫權雖稱藩，尚益脩攻討之備，權後果有貳心。

translations.literal: Although Sun Quan styled himself vassal, Shang all the more perfected preparations for attack and punishment; Quan afterward indeed had a heart of two minds.
translations.idiomatic: Though Sun Quan paid tribute as a vassal, Shang kept tightening the screws for war; Quan soon showed his duplicity.

sentences.zh: 黃初三年，車駕幸宛，使尚率諸軍與曹真共圍江陵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu the imperial carriage visited Wan; he had Shang lead the various armies with Cao Zhen jointly to besiege Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 the emperor traveled to Wan and ordered Shang with Cao Zhen to invest Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 權將諸葛瑾與尚軍對江，瑾渡入江中渚，而分水軍於江中。

translations.literal: Quan’s general Zhuge Jin faced Shang’s army across the river; Jin crossed onto a mid-river islet and divided the water army in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan’s Zhuge Jin drew up opposite Shang across the Yangzi, crossed to a midstream sandbar, and split his fleet in the channel.

sentences.zh: 尚夜多持油舩，將步騎萬餘人，於下流潛渡，攻瑾諸軍，夾江燒其舟舩，水陸並攻，破之。

translations.literal: Shang by night took many oil boats, led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry, secretly crossed downstream, attacked Jin’s various armies, burned their boats on both banks of the river, attacked by water and land together, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shang sent fire ships by night, slipped more than ten thousand men across the river below the enemy, fell on Jin’s camps, torched his fleet from both banks, and overran him by land and water.

sentences.zh: 城未拔，會大疫，詔勑尚引諸軍還。

translations.literal: The city was not yet taken when it happened there was great pestilence; an edict ordered Shang to lead the various armies back.
translations.idiomatic: Before the walls fell a plague broke out; an edict recalled Shang’s army.

sentences.zh: 益封六百戶，并前千九百戶，假鉞，進爲牧。

translations.literal: His fief was increased six hundred households, together with the previous making one thousand nine hundred households; he was given the battle-axe and advanced to shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred new households were added to his fief, bringing the total to nineteen hundred; he received the ceremonial axe and promotion to provincial shepherd.

sentences.zh: 荊州殘荒，外接蠻夷，而與吳阻漢水爲境，舊民多居江南。

translations.literal: Jing province was ruined and waste, outwardly bordered the barbarians, and with Wu was blocked by the Han River as a boundary; the old population for the most part lived south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was a shattered frontier touching barbarian country, fronting Wu across the Han, while most of the old Han population had fled south of the stream.

sentences.zh: 尚自上庸通道，西行七百餘里，山民蠻夷多服從者，五六年間，降附數千家。

translations.literal: Shang opened a road from Shangyong westward more than seven hundred li; mountain people and barbarians for the most part had those who submitted; within five or six years those who surrendered and attached numbered several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He cut a supply road west from Shangyong for over seven hundred li; hill tribes and barbarians submitted by the thousand household, until within five or six years several thousand families had come over.

sentences.zh: 五年，徙封昌陵鄉侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his fief was moved to village marquis of Changling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his title was moved to the village marquisate of Changling.

sentences.zh: 尚有愛妾嬖幸，寵奪適室；

translations.literal: Shang still had a favored concubine whom he doted on, and her favor usurped that of the principal wife;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shang still kept a favored concubine whose attentions displaced those of his principal wife;

sentences.zh: 適室，曹氏女也，故文帝遣人絞殺之。

translations.literal: the principal wife was a daughter of the Cao clan, so Emperor Wen sent men to strangle her.
translations.idiomatic: The principal wife was a Cao clanswoman, so Emperor Wen had her strangled.

sentences.zh: 尚悲感，發病怳惚，旣葬埋妾，不勝思見，復出視之。

translations.literal: Shang was grieved and moved, fell ill in confusion and delirium; after burying the concubine, unable to bear longing to see her, he went out again to look at her.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and shock left Shang delirious; after the concubine was buried he could not bear the longing, went out, and looked upon her grave again.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞而恚之曰：「杜襲之輕薄尚，良有以也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard of it and grew angry, saying: "Du Xi's slighting of Shang was well founded indeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen heard of it he fumed: "Du Xi was right to look down on Shang."

sentences.zh: 然以舊臣，恩寵不衰。

translations.literal: Yet because he was an old minister, favor and grace did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: As an old servant of the house, however, Shang's favor never waned.

sentences.zh: 六年，尚疾篤，還京都，帝數臨幸，執手涕泣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shang fell gravely ill, returned to the capital, and the emperor repeatedly visited him in person, taking his hand and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, mortally ill, Shang returned to the capital; the emperor visited him again and again, clasped his hand, and wept.

sentences.zh: 尚薨，謚曰悼侯。

translations.literal: Shang died; his posthumous title was Marquis Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Shang died and was posthumously titled Marquis Dao.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》載詔曰：「尚自少侍從，盡誠竭節，雖云異姓，其猶骨肉，是以入爲腹心，出當爪牙。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei records an edict saying: "From youth Shang attended and followed, exhausting loyalty and exhausting integrity; though called of another surname, he was like flesh and bone; therefore within he was made heart and belly, without he served as fang and claw.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei preserves an edict: "From boyhood Shang served at my side with utter loyalty. Though not of our surname, he was as close as kin—my confidant within, my talon without.

sentences.zh: 智略深敏，謀謨過人，不幸早殞，命也柰何！

translations.literal: His wisdom and stratagem were deep and keen, his counsel surpassed other men; unhappily he perished early—fate, what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: His mind was keen and his counsel surpassed other men's; that he died young was fate—what can be done?

sentences.zh: 贈征南大將軍、昌陵侯印綬。」

translations.literal: He was granted the seals and ribbon of General Who Conquers the South and Marquis of Changling."
translations.idiomatic: He is granted the seals of General Who Conquers the South and Marquis of Changling."

sentences.zh: 子玄嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 又分尚戶三百，賜尚弟子奉爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Again three hundred households of Shang's fief were divided off and given to Shang's younger cousin Feng, enfeoffed as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred households from Shang's fief were also set aside for his younger cousin Feng, who was enfeoffed as a marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 玄字太初。

translations.literal: Xuan’s courtesy name was Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xuan bore the courtesy name Taichu.

sentences.zh: 少知名，弱冠爲散騎黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In youth he was known; at the capping age he was supernumerary cavalry gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He won fame while young and at twenty became supernumerary cavalry gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 嘗進見，與皇后弟毛曾並坐，玄恥之，不恱形之於色。

translations.literal: Once on advancing to audience he sat together with the empress’s younger brother Mao Zeng; Xuan was ashamed of it and displeasure showed in his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Once at court he was seated beside the empress’s brother Mao Zeng; the pairing disgusted him and his face showed it.

sentences.zh: 明帝恨之，左遷爲羽林監。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming resented him and demoted him to colonel of the feathered forest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming took offense and busted him down to colonel of the feathered forest guard.

sentences.zh: 正始初，曹爽輔政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi, Cao Shuang assisted the government.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengshi era opened, Cao Shuang directed the regency.

sentences.zh: 玄，爽之姑子也。

translations.literal: Xuan was Shuang’s nephew by a paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was Shuang’s cousin—son of Shuang’s aunt.

sentences.zh: 累遷散騎常侍、中護軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted supernumerary cavalry attendant and protector of the army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to supernumerary cavalry attendant and protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：玄世名知人，爲中護軍，拔用武官，參戟牙門，無非俊傑，多牧州典郡。

translations.literal: 〈The Worldly Talk states: Xuan through generations was famed for knowing men; as protector of the army in promoting and employing military officers, from halberd-bearing gate guards on, none were not outstanding men, many shepherding provinces and administering commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Shiyu says the Xiahous were famed as judges of character; as protector of the army Xuan picked every martial post from gate guard upward for talent, and many of his men became governors and shepherds.

sentences.zh: 立法垂教，於今皆爲後式。〉

translations.literal: He established laws and handed down teaching; to this day all are models for later generations.〉
translations.idiomatic: The regulations he framed are still cited as models.〉

sentences.zh: 太傅司馬宣王問以時事，玄議以爲：「夫官才用人，國之柄也，故銓衡專於臺閣，上之分也，孝行存乎閭巷，優劣任之鄉人，下之叙也。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Yi, King of Xuan, asked him on current affairs; Xuan’s deliberation held: “Now employing officials according to talent is the state’s handle; therefore the balance beam is specialized in the terrace and cabinet—this is the superior’s division of rank; filial conduct resides in lanes and alleys, excellence and inferiority are entrusted to village elders—this is the inferior’s ordering.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yi asked his view of the times. Xuan answered: “Matching office to talent is how the state steers itself—so high policy belongs to the central ministries, while village reputation for filial piety belongs to local appraisal.

sentences.zh: 夫欲清教審選，在明其分叙，不使相涉而已。

translations.literal: Now wishing to clear teaching and examine selection lies in clarifying their division of ordering and not letting them overlap each other, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: If you want clean government and fair promotion, keep those two spheres apart and let neither swallow the other.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 上過其分，則恐所由之不本，而干勢馳騖之路開；

translations.literal: If the superior exceeds his division, then one fears the source of what is followed is not rooted, and the road of relying on power and racing for favor opens;
translations.idiomatic: Let the center reach down too far and patronage replaces principle;

sentences.zh: 下踰其叙，則恐天爵之外通，而機權之門多矣。

translations.literal: if the inferior oversteps his ordering, then one fears communication beyond Heaven’s conferral of rank opens, and the gate of opportunism and maneuver becomes many.
translations.idiomatic: let local appraisal climb the ladder and backstairs influence multiplies.

sentences.zh: 夫天爵下通，是庶人議柄也；

translations.literal: Heaven’s conferral communicating below is the commoners’ grasp of the handle;
translations.idiomatic: When common gossip sets rank, the people hold the lever of power;

sentences.zh: 機權多門，是紛亂之原也。

translations.literal: many gates of opportunism and maneuver are the source of confusion.
translations.idiomatic: when many doors open for intrigue, chaos follows.

sentences.zh: 自州郡中正品度官才之來，有年載矣，緬緬紛紛，未聞整齊，豈非分叙參錯各失其要之所由哉！

translations.literal: From the time when province and commandery middle-rankers graded official talent, years have piled up; endlessly tangled, one has not heard of order—could it not be from the division of ordering being crossed and each missing its essential point?
translations.idiomatic: Since the nine-rank system began, years of crossed wires have produced no order—because the two functions were never kept distinct.

sentences.zh: 若令中正但考行倫輩，倫輩當行均，斯可官矣。

translations.literal: If one orders the middle-ranker only to examine conduct and peer group, and peer-group conduct is even, then they may be appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: Let the local grader rank only moral conduct among peers; when those grades are fair, appointments can follow.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夫孝行著於家門，豈不忠恪於在官乎？

translations.literal: When filial conduct is manifest in the family gate, will one not be loyal and scrupulous in holding office?
translations.idiomatic: Filial sons at home make loyal officials at court.

sentences.zh: 仁恕稱於九族，豈不達於爲政乎？

translations.literal: When benevolence and forbearance are praised in the nine agnates, will one not be penetrating in governing?
translations.idiomatic: Men praised for kindness within the clan govern with the same breadth.

sentences.zh: 義斷行於鄉黨，豈不堪於事任乎？

translations.literal: When principled judgment is practiced in village and community, will one not be adequate to duties?
translations.idiomatic: Fair dealing with neighbors shows capacity for responsibility.

sentences.zh: 三者之類，取於中正，雖不處其官名，斯任官可知矣。

translations.literal: In cases of these three sorts, taken from the middle-ranker, though one does not yet place him in an office title, then fitness for office can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Where the local grader vouches for such qualities, you know the man can serve even before he holds a title.

sentences.zh: 行有大小，比有高下，則所任之流，亦渙然明別矣。

translations.literal: Conduct has large and small, peers have high and low; then the stream of those appointed is also clearly distinguished in radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Character has degrees, peers have ranks—so the pool of appointees sorts itself clearly.

sentences.zh: 奚必使中正干銓衡之機於下，而執機柄者有所委仗於上，上下交侵，以生紛錯哉？

translations.literal: Why must one make the middle-ranker meddle with the balance beam’s mechanism below while those who hold the machinery’s handle have something to lean on above—superior and inferior encroaching on each other to breed tangled error?
translations.idiomatic: Why force local graders to duplicate the ministry’s scales while ministers lean on village gossip—top and bottom gnawing at each other until nothing is clear?

sentences.zh: 且臺閣臨下，考功校否，衆職之屬，各有官長，旦夕相考，莫究於此；

translations.literal: Moreover the terrace and cabinet oversee below, examine achievement and check failure; the host of offices each has a chief; morning and evening they examine each other—none investigates more thoroughly than this;
translations.idiomatic: The ministries already watch every bureau, morning and night, with a chain of responsibility—nothing is more thorough.

sentences.zh: 閭閻之議，以意裁處，而使匠宰失位，衆人驅駭，欲風俗清靜，其可得乎？

translations.literal: lane-and-alley discussion, disposed by whim, and thereby making craftsmen and stewards lose their place, the host of people driven in alarm—wishing customs to be pure and quiet, can one obtain it?
translations.idiomatic: Let alley gossip overrule appointed heads and the whole machine panics—you will never see honest customs that way.

sentences.zh: 天臺縣遠，衆所絕意。

translations.literal: Heaven’s terrace and the county are distant; the multitude breaks off thought.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is far from the district; ordinary folk give up hope of justice.

sentences.zh: 所得至者，更在側近，孰不脩飾以要所求？

translations.literal: What can be reached lies rather close at hand—who will not cultivate appearance to seek what is sought?
translations.idiomatic: What they can touch is the local boss—who will not polish a façade to win him?

sentences.zh: 所求有路，則脩己家門者，已不如自達於鄉黨矣。

translations.literal: When what is sought has a road, then those who cultivate their family gates already are not as good as those who reach through village and community.
translations.idiomatic: Once favor runs through private channels, staying home to build virtue loses to courting the neighborhood elite.

sentences.zh: 自達鄉黨者，已不如自求之於州邦矣。

translations.literal: Those who reach through village and community already are not as good as those who seek for themselves in province and state.
translations.idiomatic: Courting the neighborhood elite loses to pulling strings at the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 苟開之有路，而患其飾真離本，雖復嚴責中正，督以刑罰，猶無益也。

translations.literal: If once opening it has a road, and one worries they adorn the genuine and depart from the root, though again strictly charging the middle-ranker and supervising with punishments, still there is no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Open that path and even harsh laws against the graders cannot stop men from faking virtue and forgetting substance.

sentences.zh: 豈若使各帥其分，官長則各以其屬能否獻之臺閣，臺閣則據官長能否之第，參以鄉閭德行之次，擬其倫比，勿使偏頗。

translations.literal: How is it compared to having each keep his division: office chiefs then each according to their subordinates’ ability or inability present them to the terrace and cabinet; the terrace and cabinet then according to office chiefs’ gradings of ability or inability, join with the ordering of village conduct and virtue, match their peer groups, and do not allow partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Better each keep his lane: let every chief send up a candid rating of his staff; let the ministries weigh those ratings against village reputation, match peers fairly, and forbid favoritism.

sentences.zh: 中正則唯考其行迹，別其高下，審定輩類，勿使升降。

translations.literal: The middle-ranker then only examines their traces of conduct, distinguishes their high and low, examines and fixes peer class, and does not allow promotion or demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The local grader then records conduct, sorts grades, fixes peer rank, and does not shuffle appointments on his own.

sentences.zh: 臺閣總之，如其所簡，或有參錯，則其責負自在有司。

translations.literal: The terrace and cabinet totals them; according to what they have selected, if there is crossing error, then the responsibility and burden naturally lie with the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries synthesize the lists; if anything is wrong, blame rests with the bureaus.

sentences.zh: 官長所第，中正輩擬，比隨次率而用之，如其不稱，責負在外。

translations.literal: What office chiefs grade, the middle-ranker matches in peer groups; according to following order and rate they employ them; if they do not fit the name, responsibility and burden lie without.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs rank ability, graders assign peer bands, and men are used in order; if a man fails in office, blame lies outside the grading chain.

sentences.zh: 然則內外相參，得失有所，互相形檢，孰能相飾？

translations.literal: Then inner and outer reference each other, gain and loss have their places, mutually form and inspect—who can adorn each other?
translations.idiomatic: Court and country then check each other; credit and blame have addresses—who can paper over the truth?

sentences.zh: 斯則人心定而事理得，庶可以靜風俗而審官才矣。」

translations.literal: Then the people’s hearts are settled and affairs and principle are obtained; perhaps thereby one can quiet customs and examine official talent.”
translations.idiomatic: Hearts steady, right men in right posts—you may yet purify manners and pick true talent.”

sentences.zh: 又以爲：「古之建官，所以濟育羣生，統理民物也，故爲之君長以司牧之。

translations.literal: Again he held: “In antiquity establishing offices was to succor and nurture the host of lives and to order and govern the people and things; therefore for them one set lords and elders to shepherd them.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: “Ancient offices existed to nurture the people and order the world—hence rulers set magistrates to shepherd them.

sentences.zh: 司牧之主，欲一而專，一則官任定而上下安，專則職業脩而事不煩。

translations.literal: The lords who shepherd desire unity and specialization; unity then office assignment is fixed and superior and inferior are at peace; specialization then duties are cultivated and affairs are not troublesome.
translations.idiomatic: Shepherds need a single chain of command: unity fixes each man’s job and calms the ranks; specialization keeps duties sharp and business light.

sentences.zh: 夫事簡業脩，上下相安而不治者，未之有也。

translations.literal: Now affairs simple and duties cultivated, superior and inferior mutually at peace yet not well ordered—there has never been such.
translations.idiomatic: Light business, clear duties, a quiet chain of command—under that order nothing stays broken.

sentences.zh: 先王建萬國，雖其詳未可得而究，然分彊畫界，各守土境，則非重累羈絆之體也。

translations.literal: The former kings established ten thousand states; though their detail cannot be obtained and investigated, yet dividing strongholds and drawing boundaries, each guarding its soil and territory, was not the form of heavy piled layers of restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings split the realm into myriad polities—details are lost, but each lord held his own ground without a pile of overlapping overseers.

sentences.zh: 下考殷、周五等之叙，徒有小大貴賤之差，亦無君官臣民而有二統互相牽制者也。

translations.literal: Examining below the Yin and Zhou five-ranks ordering, they had only differences of great and small, noble and base, and also did not have lord officials and commoners with two lines mutually checking each other.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yin and Zhou the feudal ladder differed only in size and rank; lord, minister, and commoner did not answer to two rival chains of command.

sentences.zh: 夫官統不一，則職業不脩；

translations.literal: Now if official lines are not unified, then duties are not cultivated;
translations.idiomatic: Split command and duties decay;

sentences.zh: 職業不脩，則事何得而簡？

translations.literal: if duties are not cultivated, then how can affairs obtain simplicity?
translations.idiomatic: decayed duties never simplify government;

sentences.zh: 事之不簡，則民何得而靜？

translations.literal: if affairs are not simple, then how can the people obtain quiet?
translations.idiomatic: tangled government never calms the people;

sentences.zh: 民之不靜，則邪惡並興，而姦偽滋長矣。

translations.literal: if the people are not quiet, then evil and vicious arise together, and treachery and deceit multiply and grow.
translations.idiomatic: restless people breed crime and fraud.

sentences.zh: 先王達其如此，故專其職司而一其統業。

translations.literal: The former kings understood it was thus; therefore they specialized their duty offices and unified their governing lines.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings saw this and gave each office a single line of authority.

sentences.zh: 始自秦世，不師聖道，私以御職，姦以待下；

translations.literal: Beginning from the Qin age, not taking the sage’s way, they used private means to control offices and treachery to await those below;
translations.idiomatic: The Qin turned from the Way, ran offices by private whim, and set subordinates up for betrayal;

sentences.zh: 懼宰官之不脩，立監牧以董之，畏督監之容曲，設司察以糾之；

translations.literal: fearing stewards would not cultivate duties, they set overseers and herdsmen to supervise them; fearing overseers’ and supervisors’ tolerance of crookedness, they set investigators to correct them;
translations.idiomatic: fearing magistrates would slack, they piled on inspectors; fearing inspectors would bend, they added auditors;

sentences.zh: 宰牧相累，監察相司，人懷異心，上下殊務。

translations.literal: stewards and herdsmen piled on each other, overseers and investigators watched each other; men harbored different hearts, superior and inferior had divergent tasks.
translations.idiomatic: magistrate sat on magistrate, spy on spy, until every rank pursued a different purpose.

sentences.zh: 漢承其緒，莫能匡改。

translations.literal: Han inherited its thread and could not rectify and change it.
translations.idiomatic: Han inherited the tangle and never straightened it.

sentences.zh: 魏室之隆，日不暇及，五等之典，雖難卒復，可粗立儀準以一治制。

translations.literal: At the Wei house’s rise, days did not suffice to attend to it; the code of the five ranks, though hard to restore at a stroke, could roughly set a standard to unify the governing system.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s founders had no leisure to fix everything; the Zhou feudal model could not return overnight, yet a rough standard could still unify command.

sentences.zh: 今之長吏，皆君吏民，橫重以郡守，累以刺史。

translations.literal: Now the senior clerks all are the lord’s officers over the people, horizontally weighted again with the commandery governor, piled on with the provincial inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Today a county magistrate answers to the people, then to a governor, then to an inspector—triple harness on one horse.

sentences.zh: 若郡所攝，唯在大較，則與州同，無爲再重。

translations.literal: If what the commandery supervises is only the great outline, then it is the same as the province; there is no need for a doubled weight.
translations.idiomatic: If the governor only repeats the inspector’s summary, the middle layer is dead weight.

sentences.zh: 宜省郡守，但任刺史；

translations.literal: It is fitting to abolish the commandery governor and only employ the provincial inspector;
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the commandery governor and leave the inspector alone;

sentences.zh: 刺史職存，則監察不廢，郡吏萬數還親農業，以省煩費，豐財殖穀，一也。

translations.literal: with the inspector’s office existing, then oversight is not abandoned; the commandery’s clerks by the tens of thousands return to personal agriculture, thereby saving troublesome expense and enriching wealth and multiplying grain—first.
translations.idiomatic: first, oversight survives while tens of thousands of redundant clerks go back to the plow, cutting cost and filling granaries.

sentences.zh: 大縣之才，皆堪郡守，是非之訟，每生意異，順從則安，直己則爭。

translations.literal: The talent of great counties all can serve as commandery governor; lawsuits of right and wrong often produce divergent intentions; following along then peace, holding straight to oneself then quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: Second, able heads of large counties could be governors themselves; yet right and wrong suits breed feuds—yield and you are safe, stand on principle and you quarrel.

sentences.zh: 夫和羹之美，在於合異，上下之益，在能相濟，順從乃安，此琴瑟一聲也，蕩而除之，則官省事簡，二也。

translations.literal: Now the beauty of harmonized stew lies in combining the different; the benefit of superior and inferior lies in being able to aid each other; following along then peace—this is one note on zither and se; if you sweep and remove it, then offices are few and affairs simple—second.
translations.idiomatic: Good stew needs mixed flavors; ruler and ruled should help each other—forced harmony is one note on two strings. Remove the middle layer and offices shrink while work clears—second gain.

sentences.zh: 又幹郡之吏，職監諸縣，營護黨親，鄉邑舊故，如有不副，而因公掣頓，民之困弊，咎生於此，若皆并合，則亂原自塞，三也。

translations.literal: Again the meddling commandery clerks, duty supervising the various counties, camp to protect faction and kin, hometown and old ties; if there is non-conformity, then by public affairs they drag and halt—the people’s distress and exhaustion, blame arises from this; if all are merged and combined, then the source of disorder is blocked of itself—third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, commandery parasites who “supervise” counties really shield cronies; they trip any magistrate who resists. Merge the layers and you plug that spring of abuse.

sentences.zh: 今承衰弊，民人彫落，賢才鮮少，任事者寡，郡縣良吏往往非一，郡受縣成，其劇在下，而吏之上選，郡當先足，此爲親民之吏，專得厎下，吏者民命，而常頑鄙，今如并之，吏多選清良者造職，大化宣流，民物獲寧，四也。

translations.literal: Now inheriting decline and exhaustion, the people are carved down, worthy talent is scarce, those holding affairs are few, commandery and county good clerks often are not one; the commandery receives the county’s completion, its severity lies below, yet in clerks’ upper selection the commandery ought first to be filled—this makes the clerks who are close to the people obtain only the bottom; clerks are the people’s life, yet are constantly stubborn and base; now if one merges them, in clerks many clear and good men can be chosen for duty, great transformation spreads and flows, the people and things obtain peace—fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, in these ruined times talent is thin yet posts multiply; the commandery takes credit for county work while the real pain is downstream. Clerks are the people’s lifeline yet are often coarse men. Merge the ranks, pick honest clerks, and peace flows to the villages.

sentences.zh: 制使萬戶之縣名之郡守，五千以上名之都尉，千戶以下令長如故，自長以上考課遷用，轉以能升，所牧亦增，此進才効功之叙也，若經制一定，則官才有次，治功齊明，五也。

translations.literal: Institute that counties of ten thousand households be named commandery governor, those of five thousand upward be named commandant, those of a thousand households and below magistrates and chiefs as before; from chief upward examine and promote for use, turn according to ability to ascend, what they shepherd also increases—this is the ordering of advancing talent and displaying merit; if the basic system is fixed once, then official talent has order and governing merit is equally clear—fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, name ten-thousand-household counties “governor,” five-thousand-household seats “commandant,” smaller units “magistrate” as now, promote by merit up a ladder of wider responsibility—once the ladder is fixed, talent and achievement both stand clear.

sentences.zh: 若省郡守，縣皆徑達，事不擁隔，官無留滯，三代之風雖未可必，簡一之化庶幾可致，便民省費在於此矣。」

translations.literal: If one abolishes the commandery governor, the counties all reach directly, affairs are not blocked in layers, offices have no stagnation—though the wind of the Three Dynasties cannot be guaranteed, the transformation of simplicity and unity perhaps can be brought near; convenience to the people and saving expense lie in this.”
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the governor and counties report straight up—no logjam, no dead files. We may not recover the Three Dynasties, but we can approach their lean government; the savings and relief to the people are here.”

sentences.zh: 又以爲：「文質之更用，猶四時之迭興也，王者體天理物，必因弊而濟通之，時彌質則文之以禮，時泰侈則救之以質。

translations.literal: Again he held: “The mutual use of pattern and substance is like the four seasons’ succeeding rise; the king embodies Heaven’s pattern in ordering things, must because of exhaustion aid and penetrate it; when the age is more substance then ornament it with ritual, when the age is too grand and extravagant then rescue it with substance.
translations.idiomatic: He added: “Civil polish and plain substance alternate like the seasons; the king must read the times—when the age is crude, teach ritual; when it grows decadent, return to simplicity.

sentences.zh: 今承百王之末，秦漢餘流，世俗彌文，宜大改之以易民望。

translations.literal: Now inheriting the ends of a hundred kings, the dregs of Qin and Han, the vulgar age is ever more patterned; it is fitting greatly to change it to alter the people’s expectation.
translations.idiomatic: We stand at the tail of a hundred reigns, heir to Qin and Han excess; the age grows ever flashier—sweep it clean to shift popular ambition.

sentences.zh: 今科制自公、列侯以下，位從大將軍以上，皆得服綾錦、羅綺、紈素、金銀飾鏤之物，自是以下，雜綵之服通於賤人，雖上下等級，各示有差，然朝臣之制已得侔至尊矣，玄黃之采已得通於下矣。

translations.literal: Now the statute system from dukes and full marquises downward, ranks from grand general of the army upward, all may wear damask silk, gauze damask, fine silk, gold and silver carved and inlaid objects; from this downward, variegated-color clothing extends to mean people; although superior and inferior grades each show having differences, yet court ministers’ regulation already obtains matching the supreme; xuan and yellow hues already obtain extending to those below.
translations.idiomatic: The sumptuary code lets every noble from full marquis up and every general from grand general down wear brocade, gauze, gold, and silver, while colored silks reach commoners—grades exist on paper, yet ministers already ape the throne and forbidden colors seep to the street.

sentences.zh: 欲使市不鬻華麗之色，商不通難得之貨，工不作雕刻之物，不可得也。

translations.literal: Wishing to make the market not sell gorgeous colors, merchants not traffic in hard-to-obtain goods, craftsmen not make carved and engraved objects—cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: You cannot ban gaudy goods in the market, rare luxuries in the shop, or filigree in the workshop while the law itself dresses everyone like an emperor.

sentences.zh: 是故宜大理其本，準度古法，文質之宜，取其中則，以爲禮度。

translations.literal: Therefore it is fitting greatly to order the root, take measure by ancient methods, the fitness of pattern and substance, take their middle rule, and make ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: Strike at the root, measure dress against ancient mean between ornament and plain, and encode it in ritual.

sentences.zh: 車輿服章，皆從質樸，禁除末俗華麗之事，使幹朝之家，有位之室，不復有錦綺之飾，無兼采之服、纖巧之物，自上以下至於樸素之差，示有等級而已，勿使過一二之覺。

translations.literal: Carriages, robes, and insignia all follow plain substance; forbid and remove end-vulgar gorgeous matters; make households that attend court, chambers that hold rank, no longer have damask embroidery adornment, no clothing of doubled colors or dainty clever objects; from superior downward to plain substance’s differences, show there are grades only, do not let them exceed awareness of one or two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Simplify carriages, robes, and badges; outlaw vulgar finery so no court family flaunts brocade, two-tone silks, or gewgaws—let rank show only in modest steps of plain dress.

sentences.zh: 若夫功德之賜，上恩所特加，皆表之有司，然後服用之。

translations.literal: As for gifts of merit and virtue, what superior grace specially adds, all display it to the responsible offices, afterward then wear and use them.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards of merit from the throne should be registered with the ministry before they may be worn or used.

sentences.zh: 夫上之化下，猶風之靡草。

translations.literal: The superior’s transforming those below is like wind’s laying the grass low.
translations.idiomatic: What the ruler does, the people follow like grass bending in the wind.

sentences.zh: 樸素之教興於本朝，則彌侈之心自消於下矣。」

translations.literal: If the teaching of plain substance rises in this court, then the heart of ever greater extravagance will of itself vanish below.”
translations.idiomatic: Let this court practice austerity and the lust for display dies in the lanes below.”

sentences.zh: 宣王報書曰：「審官擇人，除重官，改服制，皆大善。

translations.literal: The King of Xuan answered in a letter saying: “Examining offices and selecting men, abolishing doubled offices, changing the clothing system—all are great good.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi wrote back: “Tighter appointments, fewer layers of office, simpler dress—excellent proposals.

sentences.zh: 禮鄉閭本行，朝廷考事，大指如所示。

translations.literal: Ritual: village community roots conduct, the court examines affairs—the great gist is as you showed.
translations.idiomatic: Village conduct as root, court examination as branch—your outline is sound.

sentences.zh: 而中間一相承習，卒不能改。

translations.literal: Yet in the middle one generation inherits practice and in the end cannot change.
translations.idiomatic: Yet habit piles up through reigns and cannot be overturned at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 秦時無刺史，但有郡守長吏。

translations.literal: In Qin times there were no provincial inspectors, only commandery governors and senior clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Qin knew no inspectors—only governors and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 漢家雖有刺史，奉六條而已，故刺史稱傳車，其吏言從事，居無常治，吏不成臣，其後轉更爲官司耳。

translations.literal: The Han house although had provincial inspectors, they observed only the six articles; therefore inspectors were called relay-carriage men, their clerks called attendants, dwelt without constant administration, clerks did not complete the minister relation; afterward they turned more into offices and bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Han’s inspectors rode circuit on the six articles—mobile auditors, not resident lords—until the post hardened into another bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 昔賈誼亦患服制，漢文雖身服弋綈，猶不能使上下如意。

translations.literal: In the past Jia Yi also worried about the clothing system; though Emperor Wen of Han personally wore coarse silk, still he could not make superior and inferior as wished.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi once pleaded for sumptuary reform; even Emperor Wen in homespun could not force the realm to follow suit.

sentences.zh: 恐此三事，當待賢能然後了耳。」

translations.literal: I fear these three matters must await worthies and ability afterward to be finished."
translations.idiomatic: I fear these three reforms will need worthier times before they can succeed."

sentences.zh: 玄又書曰：「漢文雖身衣弋綈，而不革正法度，內外有僭擬之服，寵臣受無限之賜，由是觀之，似指立在身之名，非篤齊治制之意也。

translations.literal: Xuan again wrote saying: “Though Emperor Wen of Han personally wore coarse silk, he did not reform the correct law system; inside and outside there was usurping clothing, favored ministers received unlimited gifts—from this viewing it, it seems the finger stood on establishing name in the person, not the intent earnestly to align and order the system.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan answered again: “Emperor Wen’s homespun was personal theater—he never rewrote the code; court and harem still flouted dress laws while favorites took limitless gifts. He cared for reputation, not systemic reform.

sentences.zh: 今公侯命世作宰，追蹤上古，將隆至治，抑末正本，若制定於上，則化行於衆矣。

translations.literal: Now dukes and marquises who command the age act as chief ministers, trace and follow high antiquity, will raise the utmost good order, suppress the branch and correct the root; if the system is fixed above, then transformation proceeds among the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Today you lords steer the age toward the ancient ideal—cut excess and mend the root. Set the pattern at the top and the whole realm will follow.

sentences.zh: 夫當宜改之時，留殷勤之心，令發之日，下之應也猶響尋聲耳，猶垂謙謙，曰『待賢能』，此伊周不正殷姬之典也。

translations.literal: Now at the time when it is fitting to change, retaining a heart of earnest deference, on the day the order issues the lower’s response to it is like echo seeking sound; yet still hanging modestly and saying ‘await worthies and ability’—this is not the model by which Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou set right the houses of Yin and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When the moment calls for reform, the realm will answer an edict like an echo—yet you still hide behind false modesty and say ‘wait for worthier men.’ That is not how Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou once straightened the fallen houses of Shang and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 竊未喻焉。」

translations.literal: Your servant privately has not understood this.”
translations.idiomatic: Frankly, I cannot accept that.”

sentences.zh: 頃之，爲征西將軍，假節都督雍、涼州諸軍事。

translations.literal: 」Before long he became General Who Conquers the West, bearing credentials as commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shortly afterward he was made General Who Conquers the West, with credentials to command all forces in Yong and Liang.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：玄旣遷，司馬景王代爲護軍。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: After Xuan was transferred, Sima Shi, King of Jing, replaced him as protector of the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe says that after Xuan was moved, Sima Shi replaced him as protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 護軍總統諸將，任主武官選舉，前後當此官者，不能止貨賂。

translations.literal: The protector of the army commands all generals and is charged with military appointments; those who held this office before and after could not stop bribery.
translations.idiomatic: The protector commanded all generals and controlled military appointments; none of his predecessors had been able to stop bribery.

sentences.zh: 故蔣濟爲護軍時，有謠言「欲求牙門，當得千匹；

translations.literal: Therefore when Jiang Ji was protector of the army there was a saying: "To seek a halberd-bearing gate post, one must have a thousand bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Ji held the post, people said, "A halberd gate command costs a thousand bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 百人督，五百匹」。

translations.literal: a commander of a hundred men, five hundred bolts."
translations.idiomatic: a company captain, five hundred."

sentences.zh: 宣王與濟善，聞以問濟，濟無以解之，因戲曰：「洛中市買，一錢不足則不行。」

translations.literal: The King of Xuan was on good terms with Ji; hearing of it he asked Ji, and Ji had no way to explain it away, so in jest he said: "In Luoyang market trade, if one cash is short nothing moves."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, on good terms with Jiang Ji, asked him about it; Ji could not explain it away and joked, "In Luoyang markets, trade stalls if a single cash is missing."

sentences.zh: 遂相對歡笑。

translations.literal: Thereupon they laughed together.
translations.idiomatic: The two men laughed together.

sentences.zh: 玄代濟，故不能止絕人事。

translations.literal: When Xuan replaced Ji, therefore he could not stop social obligations entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan replaced Ji he still could not shut the door on such obligations.

sentences.zh: 及景王之代玄，整頓法令，人莫犯者。

translations.literal: When the King of Jing replaced Xuan, he put the laws in order and no one dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Shi replaced Xuan he tightened the laws until no one dared transgress.

sentences.zh: 與曹爽共興駱穀之役，時人譏之。

translations.literal: Together with Cao Shuang he launched the Luogu Valley campaign, and men of the time mocked them for it.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Cao Shuang in the Luogu Valley expedition, which contemporaries ridiculed.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，徵玄爲大鴻臚，數年徙太常。

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed, Xuan was summoned as grand minister of splendid happiness; after several years he was moved to grand minister of worship.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuang's execution Xuan was recalled as grand minister of splendid happiness, then after several years made grand minister of worship.

sentences.zh: 玄以爽抑絀，內不得意。

translations.literal: Xuan, because Shuang had suppressed and demoted him, inwardly was discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated by Shuang's fall, Xuan brooded in discontent.

sentences.zh: 中書令李豐雖宿爲大將軍司馬景王所親待，然私心在玄，遂結皇後父光祿大夫張緝，謀欲以玄輔政。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Li Feng, though long favored by the grand general Sima Shi, King of Jing, in his private heart favored Xuan; he therefore joined the empress's father, Household Counsellor Zhang Ji, plotting to have Xuan assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Li Feng had long been favored by Sima Shi, yet privately backed Xuan; he joined the empress's father, Household Counsellor Zhang Ji, in a plot to install Xuan as regent.

sentences.zh: 豐旣內握權柄，子尚公主，又與緝俱馮翊人，故緝信之。

translations.literal: Feng already held power within; his son had married an imperial princess, and he was a fellow townsman of Ji—therefore Ji trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng already wielded inner power; his son had married a princess, and he shared Zhang Ji's home commandery—so Ji trusted him.

sentences.zh: 豐陰令弟兖州刺史翼求入朝，欲使將兵入，并力起。

translations.literal: Feng secretly ordered his younger brother Yi, inspector of Yan province, to request audience, wishing to have him lead troops in and join forces to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Feng secretly ordered his brother Yi, inspector of Yan, to request audience so he could march troops in and join the rising.

sentences.zh: 會翼求朝，不聽。

translations.literal: It happened that Yi requested audience and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's request for audience was denied.

sentences.zh: 嘉平六年254年二月，當拜貴人，豐等欲因御臨軒，諸門有陛兵，誅大將軍，以玄代之，以緝爲驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Jiaping (254), when a noble consort was to be invested, Feng and the others wished to take advantage of the emperor's facing the hall, with gate guards stationed at every door, to execute the grand general, replace him with Xuan, and make Ji general of agile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jiaping 6 (254), when a noble consort was to be invested, Feng planned to strike during the imperial audience, with gate guards at every portal: kill the grand general, put Xuan in his place, and make Zhang Ji general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 豐密語黃門監蘇鑠、永寧署令樂敦、宂從僕射劉賢等曰：「卿諸人居內多有不法，大將軍嚴毅，累以爲言，張當可以爲誡。」

translations.literal: Feng secretly told Yellow Gate Supervisor Su Shuo, Director of the Eternal Tranquility Office Yue Dun, deputy director of attendants Liu Xian, and others, saying: "You all within often have unlawful conduct; the grand general is stern and severe and has repeatedly spoken of it—Zhang Dang can serve as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Feng secretly told Yellow Gate Supervisor Su Shuo, Director of the Office of Eternal Tranquility Yue Dun, deputy director of attendants Liu Xian, and others: "You inside the palace have many offenses; the grand general is stern and has warned you repeatedly—remember Zhang Dang."

sentences.zh: 鑠等皆許以從命。

translations.literal: Shuo and the others all promised to follow his command.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shuo and the rest all pledged obedience.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：玄素貴，以爽故廢黜，居常怏怏不得意。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Xuan had always been honored; because of Shuang he was dismissed and demoted, and in daily life was discontent and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Xuan had always been eminent; Shuang's fall left him demoted and perpetually sour.

sentences.zh: 中書令李豐與玄及後父光祿大夫張緝陰謀爲亂，緝與豐同郡，傾巧人也，以東莞太守召，爲後家，亦不得意，故皆同謀。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Li Feng, Xuan, and the empress's father Household Counsellor Zhang Ji secretly plotted rebellion; Ji and Feng were of the same commandery, a man crafty and clever; summoned from grand administrator of Dongguan to serve the empress's family, he too was discontent—therefore all plotted together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng, Xuan, and the empress's father Zhang Ji plotted together; Ji, a clever schemer from Feng's home commandery, had been recalled from Dongguan to serve the empress's kin and was equally resentful.

sentences.zh: 初，豐自以身處機密，息韜又以列侯給事中，尚齊長公主，有內外之重，心不自安。

translations.literal: At first Feng, because he himself stood in confidential affairs, and his son Tao moreover held the rank of full marquis as director of attendants and had married the Princess of Qi the Long, bearing weight within and without, was inwardly ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Feng himself held confidential office, and his son Tao, a full marquis and director of attendants married to the Princess of Qi the Long, gave the family weight at court—yet Feng felt uneasy.

sentences.zh: 密謂韜曰：「玄旣爲海內重人，加以當大任，年時方壯而永見廢，又親曹爽外弟，於大將軍有嫌。

translations.literal: He secretly told Tao: "Xuan is already a man of weight within the seas, and moreover bears great responsibility; in the prime of life he is forever dismissed; he is also Cao Shuang's cousin by marriage and bears resentment toward the grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly told Tao: "Xuan is a man of national stature still in his prime, yet permanently shelved; he is also Cao Shuang's cousin by marriage and bears a grudge against the grand general.

sentences.zh: 吾得玄書，深以爲憂。

translations.literal: I received a letter from Xuan and deeply took it as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: A letter from Xuan has me deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 緝有才用，棄兵馬大郡，還坐家巷。

translations.literal: Ji has talent and use; he was cast aside from a great commandery of troops and horses and sent back to sit in a home lane.
translations.idiomatic: Ji has ability, yet was pulled from a major command and left idle at home.

sentences.zh: 各不得志，欲使汝以密計告之。」

translations.literal: Each is frustrated in ambition; I wish you to tell him the secret plan."
translations.idiomatic: Each of us is thwarted—I want you to confide the plan to him."

sentences.zh: 緝嘗病創臥，豐遣韜省病，韜屏人語緝曰：「韜尚公主，父子在機近，大將軍秉事，常恐不見明信，太常亦懷深憂。

translations.literal: Ji once lay ill with a wound; Feng sent Tao to visit him in his illness; Tao dismissed the attendants and spoke to Ji, saying: "Tao has married a princess; father and son stand near the inner secrets; the grand general holds affairs and constantly fears he will not be trusted—Grand Minister of Worship also bears deep worry.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji lay wounded, Feng sent Tao to visit him; Tao sent servants away and said: "I have married a princess; my father and I stand near the inner secrets. The grand general holds power and we fear we are not trusted; the grand minister of worship is deeply anxious too.

sentences.zh: 君侯雖有後父之尊，安危未可知，皆與韜家同慮者也，韜父欲與君侯謀之。」

translations.literal: Your lordship, though you have the honor of the empress's father, safety and peril are not yet known; all share the Tao family's concern; Tao's father wishes to plot with your lordship."
translations.idiomatic: Though you are the empress's father, your safety is uncertain—we share the same fears, and my father wishes to plot with you."

sentences.zh: 緝默然良久曰：「同舟之難，吾焉所逃？

translations.literal: Ji was silent a long while and said: "In the same boat in hardship—where can I flee?
translations.idiomatic: Ji was silent a long while, then said: "We are in the same boat—where could I flee?

sentences.zh: 此大事，不捷即禍及宗族。」

translations.literal: This is a great affair; if it does not succeed, disaster will reach the clan."
translations.idiomatic: This is a grave matter; failure means the destruction of our clans."

sentences.zh: 韜於是往報豐。

translations.literal: Tao thereupon went to report to Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Tao then reported back to Feng.

sentences.zh: 密語黃門監蘇鑠等，蘇鑠等荅豐：「惟君侯計。」

translations.literal: He secretly told Yellow Gate Supervisor Su Shuo and others; Su Shuo and the others answered Feng: "Only your lordship's plan."
translations.idiomatic: Feng again secretly told Su Shuo and the others; they answered, "We follow your plan alone."

sentences.zh: 豐言曰：「今拜貴人，諸營兵皆屯門。

translations.literal: Feng spoke, saying: "Today when the noble consort is invested, all camp soldiers will be stationed at the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Feng said: "When the noble consort is invested today, camp soldiers will mass at the gates.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨軒，因此便共迫脅，將羣寮人兵，就誅大將軍。

translations.literal: When His Majesty faces the hall, on this occasion together coerce and threaten, take the crowd of ministers and soldiers, and go execute the grand general.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor faces the hall we will seize the moment, force the ministers and soldiers with us, and kill the grand general.

sentences.zh: 卿等當共密白此意。」

translations.literal: You all ought together secretly report this intent."
translations.idiomatic: You must all secretly report this plan."

sentences.zh: 鑠等曰：「陛下儻不從人，柰何？」

translations.literal: Shuo and the others said: "If His Majesty perchance does not follow men, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Su Shuo asked, "What if the emperor refuses?"

sentences.zh: 豐等曰：「事有權宜，臨時若不信聽，便當劫將去耳。

translations.literal: Feng and the others said: "In affairs there is expedient measure; at the moment if he does not believe and listen, then one must seize the general and go.
translations.idiomatic: Feng replied, "There are expedients: if he will not listen, seize the general and go.

sentences.zh: 郍得不從？」

translations.literal: How could he fail to follow?"
translations.idiomatic: Would he not have to obey?"

sentences.zh: 鑠等許諾。

translations.literal: Shuo and the others promised.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed.

sentences.zh: 豐曰：「此族滅事，卿等密之。

translations.literal: Feng said: "This is a clan-destroying affair; you all must keep it secret.
translations.idiomatic: Feng warned, "This is a matter of extermination—keep it secret.

sentences.zh: 事成，卿等皆當封侯常侍也。」

translations.literal: If the affair succeeds, you all will be enfeoffed as marquises and made regular palace attendants."
translations.idiomatic: Succeed, and you will all be enfeoffed marquises and made regular palace attendants."

sentences.zh: 豐復密以告玄、緝。

translations.literal: Feng again secretly told Xuan and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Feng secretly informed Xuan and Ji as well.

sentences.zh: 緝遣子邈與豐相結，同謀起事。

translations.literal: Ji sent his son Miao to join with Feng and together plot the rising.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent his son Miao to join Feng in the plot.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：豐遣子韜以謀報玄，玄曰「宜詳之耳」，而不以告也。

translations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: Feng sent his son Tao to report the plot to Xuan; Xuan said "It ought to be examined carefully," and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Feng sent Tao to tell Xuan; Xuan replied only, "This needs careful thought," and reported nothing.

sentences.zh: 大將軍微聞其謀，請豐相見，豐不知而往，即殺之。

translations.literal: The grand general faintly heard of the plot, invited Feng to an audience; Feng did not know and went, and was immediately killed.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general caught wind of the plot, summoned Feng, and killed him when he came unaware.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：大將軍聞豐謀，舍人王羕請以命請豐：「豐若無備，情屈勢迫，必來，若不來，羕一人足以制之；

translations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: The grand general heard of Feng's plot; attendant Wang Yang requested by order to summon Feng: "If Feng is unprepared, his feelings bent and his situation pressed, he is sure to come; if he does not come, Yang alone is enough to control him;
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu adds that attendant Wang Yang proposed summoning Feng: "If he is unprepared, bent by pressure, he will come; if not, I alone can handle him;

sentences.zh: 若知謀泄，以衆挾輪，長戟自衞，徑入雲龍門，挾天子登陵雲臺，臺上有三千人仗，鳴鼓會衆，如此，羕所不及也」。

translations.literal: if he knows the plot is leaked, with a crowd bearing carriage wheels and long halberds guarding himself, going straight through the Cloud Dragon Gate, seizing the Son of Heaven and ascending the Lingyun Terrace—on the terrace are three thousand men with weapons, beating drums to assemble the crowd—thus Yang could not reach him."
translations.idiomatic: but if he knows the plot is out, he may force his way through Cloud Dragon Gate with an armed escort, seize the emperor, and rally three thousand men on Lingyun Terrace—then I could not stop him."

sentences.zh: 大將軍乃遣羕以車迎之。

translations.literal: The grand general thereupon sent Yang with a carriage to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi sent Wang Yang with a carriage to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 豐見劫迫，隨羕而至。
