translations.literal: Feng, seeing coercion, followed Yang and arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Feng went with Yang.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：大將軍責豐，豐知禍及，遂正色曰：「卿父子懷姦，將傾社稷，惜吾力劣，不能相禽滅耳！」

translations.literal: The Wei Clan Annals states: The grand general reproached Feng; Feng knew disaster had reached him and thereupon with stern countenance said: "Your lordship and son harbor treachery and will overturn the altars of soil and grain; I regret my strength is weak and cannot seize and destroy you!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu says the grand general rebuked Feng, who answered coldly: "You and your father plot treason against the state; I regret I am too weak to destroy you!"

sentences.zh: 大將軍怒，使勇士以刀環築豐腰，殺之。

translations.literal: The grand general was angry and had warriors strike Feng's waist with knife rings and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the grand general had warriors beat Feng to death with knife rings.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：豐字安國，故衞尉李義子也。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: Feng's courtesy name was Anguo; he was the son of the former Commandant of the Guard Li Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe gives Feng the courtesy name Anguo; he was son of the former commandant of the guard Li Yi.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，以父任召隨軍。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era, through his father's appointment he was summoned to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangchu era he entered service through his father's appointment.

sentences.zh: 始爲白衣時，年十七八，在鄴下名爲清白，識別人物，海內翕然，莫不注意。

translations.literal: When he first was in plain clothes, at seventeen or eighteen, in Ye he was famed as pure and clean, discerning and distinguishing men; within the seas all at once attended to it, none not paying attention.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man of seventeen or eighteen in Ye he was famed for integrity and for judging character; the empire took notice.

sentences.zh: 後隨軍在許昌，聲稱日隆。

translations.literal: Later following the army at Xuchang, his reputation daily grew.
translations.idiomatic: Later, serving at Xuchang, his fame grew daily.

sentences.zh: 其父不願其然，遂令閉門，勑使斷客。

translations.literal: His father did not wish it so and thereupon ordered the gates closed and commanded that visitors be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: His father disapproved and shut the gates to visitors.

sentences.zh: 初，明帝在東宮，豐在文學中。

translations.literal: At first when Emperor Ming was in the Eastern Palace, Feng was in the literary academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was crown prince, Feng served in the literary academy.

sentences.zh: 及即尊位，得吳降人，問「江東聞中國名士爲誰」？

translations.literal: When he assumed the honored throne, Wu surrenderers were obtained; he asked, "In Jiangdong whom do they hear are famous gentlemen of China?"
translations.idiomatic: After his accession he questioned Wu captives: "Whom do they call China's leading gentlemen?"

sentences.zh: 降人云：「聞有李安國者是。」

translations.literal: The surrenderer said: "I hear there is one called Li Anguo."
translations.idiomatic: One answered, "I hear of a Li Anguo."

sentences.zh: 時豐爲黃門郎，明帝問左右安國所在，左右以豐對。

translations.literal: At that time Feng was a gentleman of the Yellow Gates; Emperor Ming asked his attendants where Anguo was; the attendants answered with Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was then a gentleman of the Yellow Gates; the emperor asked where Anguo was, and attendants named Feng.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豐名乃被於吳越邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Feng's name is spread even to Wu and Yue?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So Feng's name reaches even Wu and Yue?"

sentences.zh: 後轉騎都尉、給事中。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred cavalry commandant and director of attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made cavalry commandant and director of attendants.

sentences.zh: 帝崩後，爲永寧太僕，以名過其實，能用少也。

translations.literal: After the emperor's death he became grand steward of Eternal Tranquility; because the name exceeded the reality, he was little employed.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming's death he became grand steward of Eternal Tranquility but was little used—his reputation outran his role.

sentences.zh: 正始中，遷侍中尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was promoted palace attendant and vice director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era he rose to palace attendant and vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 豐在臺省，常多託疾，時臺制，疾滿百日當解祿，豐疾未滿數十日，輒暫起，已復臥，如是數歲。

translations.literal: Feng in the terrace offices often pleaded illness on many occasions; at that time the terrace regulation was that illness reaching a hundred days should result in dismissal from salary; Feng's illness had not reached several tens of days when he would briefly rise, then lie down again—thus for several years.
translations.idiomatic: In the central offices Feng often feigned illness; regulations allowed dismissal after a hundred sick days, yet he would rise briefly every few dozen days and then return to bed—for years.

sentences.zh: 初，豐子韜以選尚公主，豐雖外辭之，內不甚憚也。

translations.literal: At first Feng's son Tao was selected to marry a princess; Feng outwardly declined but inwardly was not very fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao was chosen to marry a princess, Feng outwardly declined but inwardly was not much alarmed.

sentences.zh: 豐弟翼及偉，仕數歲閒，並歷郡守。

translations.literal: Feng's younger brothers Yi and Wei, within several years of service, both successively served as grand administrators.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Yi and Wei both became commandery governors within a few years.

sentences.zh: 豐嘗於人中顯誡二弟，言當用榮位爲□。

translations.literal: Feng once openly admonished the two younger brothers before people, saying glory and rank ought to be used as □.
translations.idiomatic: Feng once publicly admonished his brothers before others that rank ought to be used with restraint.

sentences.zh: 及司馬宣王久病，偉爲二千石，荒於酒，亂新平、扶風二郡，而豐不召，衆人以爲恃寵。

translations.literal: When Sima Yi, King of Xuan, was long ill, Wei held a two-thousand-bushel post, was dissolute in wine, and threw into disorder Xinping and Fufeng commanderies, yet Feng did not summon him; the multitude thought he relied on favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi lay long ill, his brother Wei, a two-thousand-bushel official, drank himself into misrule in Xinping and Fufeng, yet Feng did not recall him—people thought he traded on favor.

sentences.zh: 曹爽專政，豐依違二公間，無有適莫，故於時有謗書曰：「曹爽之勢熱如湯，太傅父子冷如漿，李豐兄弟如游光。」

translations.literal: When Cao Shuang monopolized government, Feng wavered between the two lords without fixed preference; therefore at the time there was a lampoon saying: "Cao Shuang's power hot as boiling water, the Grand Tutor and son cold as gruel, the Li Feng brothers like wandering light."
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang monopolized power, Feng trimmed between him and the Simas; a lampoon ran: "Shuang's heat boils like soup, the Grand Tutor and son are cold as gruel, the Li Feng brothers drift like will-o'-the-wisp light."

sentences.zh: 其意以爲豐雖外示清淨，而內圖事，有似於游光也。

translations.literal: Its meaning held that though Feng outwardly showed purity, inwardly he plotted affairs, somewhat like wandering light.
translations.idiomatic: The point was that Feng looked pure outwardly while plotting within—like drifting light.

sentences.zh: 及宣王奏誅爽，住車闕下，與豐相聞，豐怖，遽氣索，足委地不能起。

translations.literal: When the King of Xuan memorialized to execute Shuang, stopping the carriage below the palace gate, he and Feng were within hearing; Feng was afraid, suddenly his breath failed, his feet gave way to the ground and he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi memorialized against Shuang and halted below the palace gate, Feng within hearing was terrified—his breath failed and his legs gave way.

sentences.zh: 至嘉平四年252年宣王終後，中書令缺，大將軍諮問朝臣：「誰可補者？」

translations.literal: By the fourth year of Jiaping (252), after the King of Xuan died, the director of the secretariat was vacant; the grand general consulted the court ministers: "Who can fill it?"
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yi died in Jiaping 4 (252), the directorship fell vacant; the grand general asked the court, "Who can fill it?"

sentences.zh: 或指向豐。

translations.literal: Some pointed to Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Some named Feng.

sentences.zh: 豐雖知此非顯選，而自以連婚國家，思附至尊，因伏不辭，遂奏用之。

translations.literal: Feng though knew this was not a conspicuous selection, yet because he himself was connected by marriage to the imperial house, wished to attach to the supreme lord, and therefore bowed without declining, and memorial was submitted to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng knew it was no glittering appointment, yet through imperial marriage ties he wished to cling to the throne and accepted without demur.

sentences.zh: 豐爲中書二歲，帝比每獨召與語，不知所說。

translations.literal: Feng was director of the secretariat two years; the emperor repeatedly summoned him alone to speak; what was said is not known.
translations.idiomatic: For two years as director the emperor repeatedly summoned Feng alone—what passed between them is unknown.

sentences.zh: 景王知其議己，請豐，豐不以實告，乃殺之。

translations.literal: The King of Jing knew he discussed himself, invited Feng; Feng did not tell the truth, and thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi learned Feng had plotted against him, summoned him, and killed him when he would not confess.

sentences.zh: 其事祕。

translations.literal: The affair was secret.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 豐前後仕歷二朝，不以家計爲意，仰俸廩而已。

translations.literal: Feng through his career served two reigns and did not take household accounts to heart; he relied on salary grain alone.
translations.idiomatic: Through two reigns Feng cared nothing for household wealth and lived on salary alone.

sentences.zh: 韜雖尚公主，豐常約勑不得有所侵取，時得賜錢帛，輒以外施親族；

translations.literal: Though Tao had married a princess, Feng constantly restrained and commanded that he must not seize or take anything; when he occasionally received bestowed money and silk, he would outwardly give it to kinsmen;
translations.idiomatic: Though Tao had married a princess, Feng forbade him to seize anything; gifts of money or silk went to kin;

sentences.zh: 及得賜宮人，多與子弟，而豐皆以與諸外甥。

translations.literal: and when he received bestowed palace women, he mostly gave them to sons and younger brothers, while Feng all gave them to various nephews.
translations.idiomatic: palace women given him he passed to nephews and younger kin.

sentences.zh: 及死後，有司籍其家，家無餘積。

translations.literal: After his death the responsible office inventoried his household; the household had no surplus accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: After his death officials inventoried his home and found no surplus.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：夜送豐尸付廷尉，廷尉鍾毓不受，曰：「非法官所治也。」

translations.literal: The Wei Clan Annals states: At night Feng's corpse was sent to the commandant of justice; Commandant of Justice Zhong Yu refused it, saying: "It is not what the law office governs."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu says Feng's corpse was sent at night to the commandant of justice; Zhong Yu refused, saying, "This is outside the law office's jurisdiction."

sentences.zh: 以其狀告，且勑之，乃受。

translations.literal: Reporting the circumstances and moreover commanding him, then he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Only after orders were reported and repeated did he accept.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，將問豐死意，太後懼，呼帝入，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and was about to question Feng's dying intent; the empress dowager feared it, called the emperor in, and then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to interrogate Feng's dying intent; the empress dowager, fearing scandal, called him in and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 遣使收翼。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to seize Yi.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to arrest Yi.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：翼後妻，散騎常侍荀廙姊，謂翼曰：「中書事發，可及書未至赴吳，何爲坐取死亡！

translations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: Yi's later wife, elder sister of Regular Palace Attendant Xun Yi, said to Yi: "The director of the secretariat affair has broken out; while the letter has not yet arrived you can hurry to Wu—why sit and court death!
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Yi's second wife, sister of Xun Yi, told him: "The secretariat plot is exposed—you can still reach Wu before the warrant arrives. Why sit here and die?

sentences.zh: 左右可共同赴水火者誰？」

translations.literal: Among those at hand who can together go through fire and water, who is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Who among your household would follow you through fire?"

sentences.zh: 翼思未荅，妻曰：「君在大州，不知可與同死生者，去亦不免。」

translations.literal: Yi thought and had not answered; his wife said: "Your lordship is in a great province and does not know who can live or die with you; go and you still will not escape."
translations.idiomatic: Yi hesitated; his wife said, "You command a great province yet do not know who would die with you—even flight will not save you."

sentences.zh: 翼曰：「二兒小，吾不去。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The two sons are small; I will not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "My two sons are small; I will not flee.

sentences.zh: 今但從坐，身死，二兒必免。」

translations.literal: Now if I merely suffer joint punishment, though my person dies, the two sons are sure to be spared."
translations.idiomatic: If I accept joint punishment, my sons will be spared."

sentences.zh: 果如翼言。

translations.literal: It turned out as Yi had said.
translations.idiomatic: It happened as Yi predicted.

sentences.zh: 翼子斌，楊駿外甥也。

translations.literal: Yi's son Bin was nephew by marriage to Yang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Bin was Yang Jun's nephew by marriage.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝初，爲河南尹，與駿俱死，見晉書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Hui of Jin he was governor of Henan and died together with Jun—see the Book of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui of Jin he was governor of Henan and died with Yang Jun—see the Jin shu.

sentences.zh: 事下有司，收玄、緝、鑠、敦、賢等送廷尉。

translations.literal: The affair was handed to the responsible office; Xuan, Ji, Shuo, Dun, Xian, and others were seized and sent to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the courts; Xuan, Ji, Shuo, Dun, Xian, and others were sent to the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：玄至廷尉，不肯下辭。

translations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: When Xuan reached the commandant of justice, he refused to submit a confession.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Xuan at the commandant of justice refused to confess.

sentences.zh: 廷尉鍾毓自臨治玄。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Zhong Yu himself came to try Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu personally tried him.

sentences.zh: 玄正色責毓曰：「吾當何辭？

translations.literal: Xuan with stern countenance reproached Yu, saying: "What confession ought I to make?
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rebuked him: "What confession should I make?

sentences.zh: 卿爲令史責人也，卿便爲吾作。」

translations.literal: You are a clerk rebuking a man; you just write it for me."
translations.idiomatic: You are a clerk judging a man—write it yourself."

sentences.zh: 毓以其名士，節高不可屈，而獄當竟，夜爲作辭，令與事相附，流涕以示玄。

translations.literal: Yu, because he was a famous gentleman whose integrity was high and could not be bent, yet the case was near its end, at night composed the confession, making it attach to the affair, and with tears showed it to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, knowing Xuan's unbending dignity yet needing to close the case, composed the confession by night, weeping as he showed it to him.

sentences.zh: 玄視，頷之而已。

translations.literal: Xuan looked, and merely nodded—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan looked and merely nodded.

sentences.zh: 毓弟會，年少於玄，玄不與交，是日於毓坐狎玄，玄不受。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Hui was younger than Xuan; Xuan did not associate with him; that day at Yu's seat he familiarly pressed Xuan; Xuan did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Hui, younger than Xuan and not his friend, tried that day at Yu's seat to be familiar; Xuan refused.

sentences.zh: 孫盛雜語曰：玄在囹圄，會因欲狎而友玄，玄正色曰：「鍾君何相偪如此也！」

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's Miscellaneous Sayings states: Xuan in prison; Hui thereupon wished to be familiar and befriend Xuan; Xuan with stern countenance said: "Lord Zhong, why press me so!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's zayu says Hui in prison tried to befriend Xuan, who answered coldly, "Lord Zhong, why press me so?"

sentences.zh: 廷尉鍾毓奏：「豐等謀迫脅至尊，擅誅冢宰，大逆無道，請論如法。」

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Zhong Yu memorialized: "Feng and others plotted to coerce and threaten the supreme lord, executed the chief minister on their own authority, great rebellion without the Way—request judgment according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu memorialized: "Feng and the rest plotted to coerce the emperor and murder the chief minister without authority—great treason warranting legal judgment."

sentences.zh: 於是會公卿朝臣廷尉議，咸以爲「豐等各受殊寵，典綜機密，緝承外戚椒房之尊，玄備世臣，並居列位，而苞藏禍心，構圖凶逆，交關閹豎，授以姦計，畏憚天威，不敢顯謀，乃欲要君脅上，肆其詐虐，謀誅良輔，擅相建立，將以傾覆京室，顛危社稷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the assembled dukes, ministers, court officials, and commandant of justice deliberated; all held that "Feng and the others each received special favor, controlled confidential affairs comprehensively; Ji inherited the empress's father's pepper-room honor; Xuan was equipped as a minister of generations, all occupying ranks and posts, yet harbored treacherous hearts, plotted wicked rebellion, associated with eunuch attendants, entrusted with wicked plans, feared Heaven's majesty, dared not plot openly, and therefore wished to coerce the ruler and threaten the sovereign, unleash their fraud and cruelty, plot to execute good assistants, establish others on their own authority, and thereby overturn the capital house and endanger the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers agreed: "Feng and the rest, favored confidants and imperial in-laws, had harbored treason, used eunuchs, and sought to coerce the throne and overturn the state.

sentences.zh: 毓所正皆如科律，報毓施行」。

translations.literal: What Yu corrected all accorded with statute law; report Yu to carry out."
translations.idiomatic: Yu's findings matched the statutes; let them be executed."

sentences.zh: 詔書：「齊長公主，先帝遺愛，匄其三子死命。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Princess of Qi the Long, the late emperor's beloved—beg three sons' lives."
translations.idiomatic: An edict pleaded: "The Princess of Qi the Long was the late emperor's beloved—spare her three sons."

sentences.zh: 於是豐、玄、緝、敦、賢等皆夷三族，《魏書》曰：豐子韜，以尚主，賜死獄中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Feng, Xuan, Ji, Dun, Xian, and others were all exterminated to the third degree; the Book of Wei states: Feng's son Tao, because he had married a princess, was granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, Xuan, Ji, Dun, and Xian were exterminated to the third degree; the Book of Wei adds that Tao, as imperial son-in-law, was granted death in prison.

sentences.zh: 其餘親屬徙樂浪郡。

translations.literal: The rest of the kin were moved to Lelang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Other kin were exiled to Lelang.

sentences.zh: 玄格量弘濟，臨斬東巿，顏色不變，舉動自若，時年四十六。

translations.literal: Xuan's measure was broad and sustaining; facing execution at the eastern market, his color did not change and his bearing was as usual; at the time he was forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan met execution at the eastern market with unchanged color and composed bearing; he was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：玄自從西還，不交人事，不蓄華妍。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary states: From the time Xuan returned from the west he did not engage in human affairs and did not store splendor or beauty.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe says that after returning from the west Xuan withdrew from public life and kept no luxuries.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：初，夏侯霸將奔蜀，呼玄欲與之俱。

translations.literal: The Wei Clan Annals states: At first when Xiahou Ba was about to flee to Shu, he called Xuan wishing to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu says when Xiahou Ba prepared to flee to Shu he called Xuan to come along.

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「吾豈苟存自客於寇虜乎？」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "How could I basely preserve myself and be a guest among bandit enemies?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "How could I basely save myself by lodging with bandits?"

sentences.zh: 遂還京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital instead.

sentences.zh: 太傅薨，許允謂玄曰：「無復憂矣。」

translations.literal: When the Grand Tutor died, Xu Yun said to Xuan: "No more worries."
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Tutor died, Xu Yun told Xuan, "You need worry no more."

sentences.zh: 玄歎曰：「士宗，卿何不見事乎？

translations.literal: Xuan sighed and said: "Shizong, why do you not see how things stand?
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sighed: "Shizong, can you not read the times?

sentences.zh: 此人猶能以通家年少遇我，子元、子上不吾容也。」

translations.literal: This man could still treat me as a young man of a connected house; Ziyuan and Zishang will not spare me."
translations.idiomatic: He still treated me as a family friend's son; Ziyuan and Zishang will not spare me."

sentences.zh: 玄嘗著樂毅、張良及本無肉刑論，辭旨通遠，咸傳於世。

translations.literal: Xuan once composed treatises on Yue Yi, Zhang Liang, and on abolishing corporal punishment; their wording and intent were penetrating and far-reaching, all transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wrote treatises on Yue Yi, Zhang Liang, and abolishing corporal punishment that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 玄之執也，衞將軍司馬文王流涕請之，大將軍曰：「卿忘會趙司空葬乎？」

translations.literal: When Xuan was seized, General of the Guard Sima Zhao wept and begged for him; the grand general said: "Have you forgotten meeting at Minister of Works Zhao Yan's funeral?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan was arrested, Sima Zhao wept and begged for him; the grand general said, "Have you forgotten Minister of Works Zhao Yan's funeral?"

sentences.zh: 先是，司空趙儼薨，大將軍兄弟會葬，賔客以百數，玄時後至，衆賔客咸越席而迎，大將軍由是惡之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Minister of Works Zhao Yan died; the grand general brothers met at the funeral; guests numbered in the hundreds; Xuan at that time arrived later; all the guests alike rose from their mats to welcome him—the grand general on this account hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier at Zhao Yan's funeral the Sima brothers saw every guest rise to welcome the late-arriving Xuan—hence their hatred.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：曹爽以正始五年244年伐蜀，時玄已爲關中都督，至十年，爽誅滅後，方還洛耳。

translations.literal: Commentator Pei Songzhi notes: Cao Shuang in the fifth year of Zhengshi (244) campaigned against Shu; at that time Xuan was already metropolitan protector of Guanzhong; only in the tenth year, after Shuang was destroyed and executed, did he return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: Cao Shuang invaded Shu in Zhengshi 5 (244), when Xuan was already metropolitan protector of Guanzhong; he returned to Luoyang only after Shuang's fall in the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 案少帝紀，司空趙儼以六年亡，玄則無由得會儼葬，若云玄入朝，紀、傳又無其事。

translations.literal: According to the Annals of the Lesser Emperor, Minister of Works Zhao Yan died in the sixth year; Xuan then had no way to meet Yan's funeral; if one says Xuan entered court, the annals and biography again have no such affair.
translations.idiomatic: The annals place Zhao Yan's death in the sixth year, so Xuan could not have attended his funeral; nor do annals or biography record such a court appearance.

sentences.zh: 斯近妄不實。

translations.literal: This is near to reckless untruth.
translations.idiomatic: The story is nearly certainly false.

sentences.zh: 正元中，紹功臣世，封尚從孫本爲昌陵亭侯，邑三百戶，以奉尚後。

translations.literal: In the Zhengyuan era the meritorious ministers' lines were continued; Shang's collateral descendant Ben was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changling, fief three hundred households, to continue Shang's line.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengyuan era Shang's collateral descendant Ben was enfeoffed village marquis of Changling with three hundred households to continue Shang's sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 初，中領軍高陽許允與豐、玄親善。

translations.literal: At first, chief of the palace guard Xu Yun of Gaoyang was intimate and friendly with Feng and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu Yun of Gaoyang, chief of the palace guard, had been close to Li Feng and Xiahou Xuan.

sentences.zh: 先是有詐作尺一詔書，以玄爲大將軍，允爲太尉，共錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Before this there was someone who forged a foot-one edict, making Xuan grand general and Yun grand commandant, together recording the affairs of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Someone had forged an edict on the one-foot board naming Xuan Grand General and Xu Yun Grand Commandant, jointly to oversee the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有何人天未明乘馬以詔版付允門吏，曰「有詔」，因便馳走。

translations.literal: There was a man before dawn riding a horse who gave the edict board to Yun’s gate clerk, saying “There is an edict,” then galloped off.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn a horseman thrust the wooden edict into Xu Yun’s gatehouse, cried “Imperial order!” and vanished at a gallop.

sentences.zh: 允即投書燒之，不以開呈司馬景王。

translations.literal: Yun immediately threw the document into the fire and burned it, not thereby opening and presenting it to Sima Jingwang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun threw the paper straight into the fire and never showed it to Sima Shi.

sentences.zh: 後豐等事覺，徙允爲鎮北將軍，假節督河北諸軍事。

translations.literal: Afterward when Feng and others’ affair was discovered, Yun was shifted to general who guards the north, was given the credentials of office and supervised the various Hebei military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Feng’s plot surfaced, Xu Yun was transferred to general of the northern march, with baton over Hebei armies.

sentences.zh: 未發，以放散官物，收付廷尉，徙樂浪，道死。

translations.literal: Before he set out, because he wantonly distributed official goods, he was seized and delivered to the commandant of justice, banished to Lelang, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he was charged with embezzling state property, handed to the commandant of justice, sentenced to exile in Lelang, and died en route.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：允字士宗，世冠族。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary states: Yun’s courtesy name was Shizong; for generations a leading clan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei lüe names him Xu Yun, styled Shizong, from a great lineage.

sentences.zh: 父據，仕歷典農校尉、郡守。

translations.literal: His father Ju served successively as colonel of the agricultural colonies and grand administrator of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu Ju had been an agricultural colonel and a commandery governor.

sentences.zh: 允少與同郡崔贊俱發名於冀州，召入軍。

translations.literal: Yun in youth together with Cui Zan of his same commandery both rose to fame in Ji province and were summoned into the army.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and his townsman Cui Zan won fame in Ji and were drafted into the army.

sentences.zh: 明帝時爲尚書選曹郎，與陳國袁侃對，同坐職事，皆收送獄，詔旨嚴切，當有死者，正直者爲重。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming’s time he was secretary in the personnel bureau of the secretariat, paired with Yuan Kan of Chen; sitting together on office business, both were seized and sent to prison; the edict’s intent was stern and cutting—there ought to be one who died; the upright one bore the heavier guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he served in the Secretariat’s appointments bureau opposite Yuan Kan of Chen; both were jailed over a paperwork dispute; the emperor’s edict demanded a death—and hinted the more upright man should hang.

sentences.zh: 允謂侃曰：「卿，功臣之子，法應八議，不憂死也。」

translations.literal: Yun said to Kan: “You, a meritorious minister’s son, by law ought to receive the eight deliberations; you need not worry about death.”
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun told Yuan Kan, “You are a hero’s son—the eight grounds for clemency cover you; you will not hang.”

sentences.zh: 侃知其指，乃爲受重。

translations.literal: Kan knew his intent, then for him bore the heavy guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Kan read between the lines and took the heavier sentence himself.

sentences.zh: 允刑竟復吏，出爲郡守，稍遷爲侍中尚書中領軍。

translations.literal: When Yun’s punishment was finished he again became a clerk, went out as grand administrator, was gradually promoted to palace attendant, secretary, and chief of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: After his term Xu Yun returned to office, became a governor, then rose to palace attendant, secretary, and chief of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 允聞李豐等被收，欲往見大將軍，已出門，回遑不定，中道還取袴，豐等已收訖。

translations.literal: Yun heard Li Feng and others had been seized, wished to go see the grand general, had already gone out the gate, wavered undecided, halfway returned to fetch trousers, and Feng and others had already been seized and finished.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Feng was arrested Xu Yun started for Sima Shi’s mansion, hesitated at the gate, doubled back for a pair of trousers, and by the time he returned the roundup was over.

sentences.zh: 大將軍聞允前遽，恠之曰：「我自收豐等，不知士大夫何爲忩忩乎？」

translations.literal: The grand general heard Yun had been in haste before and wondered at it, saying: “I myself seized Feng and others; I do not know why the gentlemen were in such a flurry?”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi heard of Xu Yun’s panic and said, “I arrested Li Feng myself—why were the ministers scurrying about?”

sentences.zh: 是時朝臣遽者多耳，而衆人咸以爲意在允也。

translations.literal: At that time many court ministers had been in haste, yet the multitude all thought the intent pointed at Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials had been rushing that day, but rumor said Sima Shi’s eye was really on Xu Yun.

sentences.zh: 會鎮北將軍劉靜卒，朝廷以允代靜。

translations.literal: It happened that general who guards the north Liu Jing died; the court used Yun to replace Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jing, general of the northern march, died, the court named Xu Yun his successor.

sentences.zh: 已受節傳，出止外舍。

translations.literal: Having received the baton and tallies, he went out and stopped at an outer lodging.
translations.idiomatic: He took the baton and tallies and moved to an outer residence to prepare his column.

sentences.zh: 大將軍與允書曰：「鎮北雖少事，而都典一方，念足下震華鼓，建朱節，歷本州，此所謂著繡晝行也。」

translations.literal: The grand general wrote Yun a letter saying: “Though guarding the north has few affairs, yet it all governs a region; I think of you shaking the flower drum, raising the vermilion baton, passing through your home province—this is what is called wearing brocade and walking by day.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi wrote, “The northern command is quiet, yet it rules a whole quadrant—imagine yourself with war drums and crimson baton riding through your native commandery: the proverbial homecoming in silks.”

sentences.zh: 允心甚恱，與臺中相聞，欲易其鼓吹旌旗。

translations.literal: Yun’s heart was very pleased; he communicated with the terrace and wished to exchange his musicians’ banners and standards.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun was delighted and asked the ministry to upgrade his band and banners for the parade.

sentences.zh: 其兄子素頗聞衆人說允前見嫌意，戒允「但當趣耳，用是爲邪」！

translations.literal: His elder brother’s son Su had somewhat heard the multitude say Yun before had been viewed with suspicion; he warned Yun “you need only hurry—what use is this?”
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Xu Su had heard whispers that Xu Yun was under suspicion and urged him, "Just ride—why fuss over finery?"

sentences.zh: 允曰：「卿俗士不解，我以榮國耳，故求之。」

translations.literal: Yun said: “You vulgar scholar do not understand; I do this to bring glory to the state; therefore I seek it.”
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun snapped, “A pedant like you would not understand—I mean to honor the state, which is why I want the full panoply.”

sentences.zh: 帝以允當出，乃詔會羣臣，羣臣皆集，帝特引允以自近；

translations.literal: The emperor because Yun was about to go out, then ordered to assemble the group ministers; the group ministers all gathered; the emperor especially led Yun near himself;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, thinking Xu Yun was leaving, called a full court and drew him to his side;

sentences.zh: 允前爲侍中，顧當與帝別，涕泣歔欷。

translations.literal: Yun before had been palace attendant and looked as though he ought to take leave of the emperor, weeping and sobbing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun, once a palace attendant, behaved as if bidding the emperor a last farewell, weeping openly.

sentences.zh: 會訖，罷出，詔促允令去。

translations.literal: When the meeting finished, dismissed and going out, an edict urged Yun ordering him to depart.
translations.idiomatic: When the audience ended an edict hurried him out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 會有司奏允前擅以厨錢穀乞諸俳及其官屬，故遂收送廷尉，考問竟，減死徙邊。

translations.literal: It happened that the responsible offices memorialized that Yun earlier on his own authority had used kitchen money and grain to beg the jesters and their office subordinates; therefore he was seized and sent to the commandant of justice; examination and questioning finished, death was commuted and he was banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate then charged him with diverting kitchen funds to entertain actors and staff; he was jailed, interrogated, spared execution, and banished to the border.

sentences.zh: 允以嘉平六年秋徙，妻子不得自隨，行道未到，以其年冬死。

translations.literal: Yun was shifted in the autumn of the sixth year of Jiaping; wife and children could not follow of themselves; on the road before he arrived, in that year’s winter he died.
translations.idiomatic: He left in the autumn of Jiaping 6 without his family, and died that winter before reaching his place of exile.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：允爲吏部郎，選郡守。

translations.literal: The Wei Family Spring and Autumn states: Yun as bureau secretary in the personnel ministry selected a commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu notes that as appointments secretary he picked a governor.

sentences.zh: 明帝疑其所用非次，召入，將加罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming suspected those he employed were not in proper order, summoned him in, and was about to add punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming thought his choices out of sequence and summoned him for punishment.

sentences.zh: 允妻阮氏跣出，謂曰：「明主可以理奪，難以情求。」

translations.literal: Yun’s wife the Lady Ruan barefoot came out and said to him: “An enlightened lord can be swayed by reason, hard to seek by emotion.”
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Ruan ran out barefoot and told him, “A wise emperor yields to argument, not tears.”

sentences.zh: 允頷之而入。

translations.literal: Yun nodded and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun nodded and went in.

sentences.zh: 帝怒詰之，允對曰：「某郡太守雖限滿文書先至，年限在後，某守雖後，日限在前。」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily questioned him; Yun answered saying: “A certain commandery governor though his term-limit document arrived first, his year-term came after; a certain governor though later, his day-limit came before.”
translations.idiomatic: He explained, “One candidate’s paperwork arrived first though his seniority date was later; another’s file came later though his eligibility date was earlier.”

sentences.zh: 帝前取事視之，乃釋遣出。

translations.literal: The emperor before him took the dossiers and looked; then released and sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor checked the files himself and let him go.

sentences.zh: 望其衣敗，曰：「清吏也。」

translations.literal: Looking at his clothing worn out, he said: “A pure clerk.”
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Xu Yun’s threadbare coat he said, “There goes an honest official.”

sentences.zh: 賜之。

translations.literal: He gifted him.
translations.idiomatic: and rewarded him with cloth.

sentences.zh: 允之出爲鎮北也，喜謂其妻曰：「吾知免矣！」

translations.literal: When Yun went out as guard of the north, joyfully he said to his wife: “I know I am spared!”
translations.idiomatic: When named general of the north he told his wife, “Now I am safe!”

sentences.zh: 妻曰：「禍見於此，何免之有？」

translations.literal: The wife said: “Disaster shows itself here; what sparing is there?”
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "Disaster shows its face here—where is safety?"

sentences.zh: 允善相印，將拜，以印不善，使更刻之，如此者三。

translations.literal: Yun was good at reading seals; about to be invested, because the seal was not good, he had it recarved; thus three times.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun read omens in official seals; before his investiture he had a flawed seal recut three times.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「印雖始成而已被辱。」

translations.literal: Yun said: “Though the seal has just been completed, already it has suffered dishonor.”
translations.idiomatic: He said, “The new seal is already dishonored before it reaches my hand.”

sentences.zh: 問送印者，果懷之而墜於厠。

translations.literal: Questioning the seal deliverer, it turned out he had carried it in his bosom and dropped it in the privy.
translations.idiomatic: The courier admitted he had tucked it in his robe and dropped it into a latrine.

sentences.zh: 相印書曰：「相印法本出陳長文，長文以語韋仲將，印工楊利從仲將受法，以語許士宗。

translations.literal: The book Reading Seals says: “The seal-reading method fundamentally came out from Chen Changwen; Changwen told it to Wei Zhongjiang; seal-craftsman Yang Li received the method from Zhongjiang and told it to Xu Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: The book Reading Seals says: “The seal-reading method fundamentally came out from Chen Changwen; Changwen told it to Wei Zhongjiang; seal-craftsman Yang Li received the method from Zhongjiang and told it to Xu Shizong.

sentences.zh: 利以法術占吉凶，十可中八九。

translations.literal: Li by occult method divined auspicious and inauspicious; in ten cases he hit eight or nine.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Li’s mantic reading was right eight or nine times in ten.

sentences.zh: 仲將問長文『從誰得法』？

translations.literal: Zhongjiang asked Changwen ‘from whom did you obtain the method’?
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan asked Chen Qun where the art came from.

sentences.zh: 長文曰：『本出漢世，有相印、相笏經，又有鷹經、牛經、馬經。

translations.literal: Changwen said: ‘Fundamentally it came out in Han times; there were classics on reading seals and reading hu tablets, moreover classics on hawks, cattle, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Qun said it began in Han: treatises on seal and tablet omens, plus tracts on hawks, oxen, and horses.

sentences.zh: 印工宗養以法語程申伯，是故有一十三家相法傳於世。』」

translations.literal: Seal-craftsman Zong Yang by the method told Cheng Shenbo; therefore there are thirteen houses’ seal methods handed down in the world."
translations.idiomatic: The craftsman Zong Yang passed it to Cheng Shenbo—hence the thirteen schools of seal lore."

sentences.zh: 允妻阮氏賢明而醜，允始見愕然，交禮畢，無復入意。

translations.literal: ’” Yun’s wife the Lady Ruan was worthy and intelligent but ugly; when Yun first saw her he was startled; when exchange of bows was finished, he had no further intention to enter.
translations.idiomatic: ’” Xu Yun’s wife Lady Ruan was wise but plain; after the wedding bows he refused to join her in the bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 妻遣婢覘之，云「有客姓桓」，妻曰：「是必桓範，將勸使入也。」

translations.literal: His wife sent a maid to spy; she reported “There is a guest surnamed Huan”; the wife said: “That must be Huan Fan; he will urge him to enter.”
translations.idiomatic: She sent a maid to watch; learning a visitor named Huan had come, she said, “That is Huan Fan—he will talk my husband inside.”

sentences.zh: 旣而範果勸之。

translations.literal: Presently Fan indeed urged him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Fan did just that.

sentences.zh: 允入，須臾便起，妻捉裾留之。

translations.literal: Yun entered; in a moment he rose; his wife seized his skirt hem and detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun went in, rose almost at once, and his wife grabbed his robe to stop him.

sentences.zh: 允顧謂婦曰：「婦有四德，卿有其幾？」

translations.literal: Yun looked back and said to the woman: “A wife has four virtues; how many do you possess?”
translations.idiomatic: He turned on her: “A wife should have the four virtues—which do you have?”

sentences.zh: 婦曰：「新婦所乏唯容。

translations.literal: The wife said: “What your new wife lacks is only countenance.
translations.idiomatic: She answered, “Among the four I lack only beauty.

sentences.zh: 士有百行，君有其幾？」

translations.literal: A gentleman has a hundred conducts; how many does the lord possess?”
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman needs a hundred virtues—which do you possess?”

sentences.zh: 許曰：「皆備。」

translations.literal: Yun said: “All are complete.”
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun said, “Every one of them.”

sentences.zh: 婦曰：「士有百行，以德爲首，君好色不好德，何謂皆備？」

translations.literal: The wife said: “Among a gentleman’s hundred conducts, virtue is the head; the lord loves beauty and does not love virtue—what is called all complete?”
translations.idiomatic: She retorted, “Virtue heads the list—yet you love looks, not virtue. How is that ‘complete’?”

sentences.zh: 允有慙色，知其非凡，遂雅相親重。

translations.literal: Yun had a ashamed expression, knew she was not ordinary, then treated her with refined intimacy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun flushed, saw she was extraordinary, and thereafter honored her as a partner.

sentences.zh: 生二子，奇、猛，少有令問。

translations.literal: He begot two sons, Qi and Meng; in youth they had fair repute.
translations.idiomatic: They had two sons, Xu Qi and Xu Meng, both promising boys.

sentences.zh: 允後爲景王所誅，門生走入告其婦，婦正在機，神色不變，曰：「早知爾耳。」

translations.literal: Afterward Yun was executed by Jingwang; a disciple ran in to tell his wife; the wife was just at the loom, her expression unchanged, saying: “I knew it long ago.”
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Shi executed Xu Yun, a student rushed to tell Lady Ruan; she sat at her loom unmoved and said, “I expected this.”

sentences.zh: 門生欲藏其子，婦曰：「無預諸兒事。」

translations.literal: The disciple wished to hide his sons; the wife said: “It does not concern the various sons’ affair.”
translations.idiomatic: The student wanted to hide the boys; she said, “Leave my sons out of it.”

sentences.zh: 後移居墓所，景王遣鍾會看之，若才藝德能及父，當收。

translations.literal: Afterward they moved residence to the tomb site; Jingwang sent Zhong Hui to look at them; if in talent, arts, virtue, and ability they matched their father, then seize them.
translations.idiomatic: After they moved near the grave, Sima Shi sent Zhong Hui to interview the sons—if they rivaled their father in talent, arrest them.

sentences.zh: 兒以語母，母荅：「汝等雖佳，才具不多，率胷懷與會語，便自無憂，不須極哀，會止便止。

translations.literal: The sons told their mother; the mother answered: “You although are fine, talent and capacity are not much; lead with your bosom in speaking with Hui and of yourselves there will be no worry; you need not extreme grief; when Hui stops then stop.
translations.idiomatic: She told them, “You are clever but not brilliant—speak from the heart with Zhong Hui, show neither genius nor deep grief, and stop when he stops.

sentences.zh: 又可多少問朝事。」

translations.literal: Again you may somewhat ask about court affairs.”
translations.idiomatic: Ask a few harmless questions about court business.”

sentences.zh: 兒從之。

translations.literal: The sons followed her.
translations.idiomatic: They obeyed.

sentences.zh: 會反命，具以狀對，卒免其禍，皆母之教也。

translations.literal: When Hui returned mission, fully according to the situation answered, in the end they were spared that disaster—all the mother’s teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui reported that they were harmless mediocrities, and the danger passed—entirely their mother’s lesson.

sentences.zh: 雖會之識鑒，而輸賢婦之智也。

translations.literal: Although Hui’s insight and discernment, yet he lost to a worthy wife’s wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: For all Zhong Hui’s sharp eye, he was outplayed by a wise wife.

sentences.zh: 果慶及後嗣，追封子孫而已。

translations.literal: Indeed blessing reached later descendants; posthumously enfeoffing sons and grandsons only.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune later smiled on the line—only posthumous titles for the descendants.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：允二子：奇字子泰，猛字子豹，並有治理才學。

translations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: Yun’s two sons: Qi’s courtesy name was Zitai, Meng’s courtesy name was Zibao; both had governing order talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu names the sons Xu Qi (Zitai) and Xu Meng (Zibao), both able administrators.

sentences.zh: 晉元康中，奇爲司隷校尉，猛幽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yuan Kang era of Jin, Qi was colonel of the metropolitan province, Meng inspector of You province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Western Jin’s Yuankang, Qi became metropolitan colonel and Meng governor of You.

sentences.zh: 傅暢《晉諸公贊》曰：猛禮樂儒雅，當時最優。

translations.literal: Fu Chang’s Appraisal of Jin Worthies states: Meng in ritual and music was refined and Ru; of the age the most excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang’s Jin zhugong zan calls Xu Meng the age’s finest Confucian stylist in ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 奇子遐，字思祖，以清尚稱，位至侍中。

translations.literal: Qi’s son Xia, courtesy name Sizu, by pure high conduct was praised; rank reached palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Qi’s son Xu Xia (Sizu) was famed for integrity and rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 猛子式，字儀祖，有才幹，至濮陽內史、平原太守。〉

translations.literal: Meng’s son Shi, courtesy name Yizu, had talent and capacity; reached interior secretary of Puyang and grand administrator of Pingyuan.〉
translations.idiomatic: Meng’s son Xu Shi (Yizu) was capable, ending as Puyang interior secretary and governor of Pingyuan.〉

sentences.zh: 清河王經亦與允俱稱冀州名士。

translations.literal: Wang Jing of Qinghe was also with Yun together called famous gentlemen of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing of Qinghe was ranked with Xu Yun among Ji province's celebrated gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 甘露中爲尚書，坐高貴鄉公事誅。

translations.literal: In the Ganlu era he was secretary; he sat with the affair of the noble township and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ganlu era he served as secretary and was executed in the noble township affair.

sentences.zh: 始經爲郡守，經母謂經曰：「汝田家子，今仕至二千石，物太過不祥，可以止矣。」

translations.literal: At first when Jing was grand administrator, Jing's mother said to Jing: "You are a farmer's son; now in office reaching two thousand bushels—things too much exceeding is inauspicious; you can stop."
translations.idiomatic: When Jing first became a commandery governor, his mother warned him: "You are a farmer's son risen to two thousand bushels—excess invites misfortune; stop while you can."

sentences.zh: 經不能從，歷二州刺史，司隷校尉，終以致敗。

translations.literal: Jing could not follow; he successively served as inspector of two provinces and metropolitan commandant, and in the end thereby met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Jing would not listen; he served two terms as provincial inspector and as metropolitan commandant, and was ruined.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：經字彥偉，初爲江夏太守。

translations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: Jing's courtesy name was Yanwei; at first he was grand administrator of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu names him Wang Jing, styled Yanwei; he first governed Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 大將軍曹爽附絹二十匹令交市於吳，經不發書，棄官歸。

translations.literal: The grand general Cao Shuang attached twenty bolts of silk ordering trade in Wu; Jing did not issue the letter, abandoned office, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Cao Shuang sent twenty bolts of silk ordering trade with Wu; Jing refused the order, resigned, and went home.

sentences.zh: 母問歸狀，經以實對。

translations.literal: His mother asked the circumstances of return; Jing answered with the facts.
translations.idiomatic: His mother asked why he returned; he told the truth.

sentences.zh: 母以經典兵馬而擅去，對送吏杖經五十，爽聞，不復罪。

translations.literal: His mother, because Jing commanded troops and horses yet left on his own authority, had the escort clerk beat Jing fifty blows; Shuang heard of it and did not again punish.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, angry that he had abandoned command without leave, had the escort clerk beat him fifty strokes; Shuang heard and did not punish further.

sentences.zh: 經爲司隷校尉，辟河內向雄爲都官從事，王業之出，不申經，竟以及難。

translations.literal: When Jing was metropolitan commandant, he recruited Xiang Xiong of Henei as director of capital cases; when Wang Ye went out, he did not report to Jing, and in the end thereby met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: As metropolitan commandant he recruited Xiang Xiong of Henei; when Wang Ye went out without reporting to Jing, disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 經刑於東市，雄哭之，感動一市。

translations.literal: Jing was executed at the eastern market; Xiong wept for him and moved the whole market.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was executed at the eastern market; Xiong wept until the whole market was moved.

sentences.zh: 刑及經母，雍州故吏皇甫晏以家財收葬焉。

translations.literal: When the punishment reached Jing's mother, Huangfu Yan, a former clerk of Yong province, buried her at his household's expense.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing's mother was executed, former Yong clerk Huangfu Yan buried her at his own expense.

sentences.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：經被收，辭母。

translations.literal: The Han–Jin Annals states: When Jing was seized, he bade farewell to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The Han–Jin chunqiu says Jing took leave of his mother when arrested.

sentences.zh: 母顏色不變，笑而應曰：「人誰不死？

translations.literal: His mother's color did not change; smiling she answered: "Who among men does not die?
translations.idiomatic: Her color never changed; smiling she answered, "Who does not die?

sentences.zh: 往所以不止汝者，恐不得其所也。

translations.literal: The reason I before did not stop you was fear you would not obtain your place.
translations.idiomatic: I did not stop you before lest you fail to meet your proper end.

sentences.zh: 以此并命，何恨之有哉？」

translations.literal: To die together on this account—what regret is there?"
translations.idiomatic: To die together now—what regret could there be?"

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太始元年詔曰：「故尚書王經，雖身陷法辟，然守志可嘉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin's inaugural edict of the first year of Taishi said: "Former Secretary Wang Jing, though his person fell into law's punishment, yet his holding to purpose is praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin's Taishi inaugural edict said: "Former Secretary Wang Jing, though punished by law, held firm purpose worth praise.

sentences.zh: 門戶堙沒，意常愍之，其賜經孫郎中。」

translations.literal: His household gates were buried and extinguished; I constantly pitied it—grant Jing's grandson the post of gentleman of the palace gate."
translations.idiomatic: His house was destroyed; I have long pitied it—grant his grandson the post of gentleman of the palace gate."

sentences.zh: 允友人同郡崔贊，亦嘗以處世太盛戒允云。

translations.literal: Yun's friend Cui Zan of the same commandery also once warned Yun that worldly standing was too full.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun's friend Cui Zan of the same commandery had also warned that worldly eminence was perilous.

sentences.zh: 荀綽《冀州記》曰：贊子洪，字良伯，清恪有匪躬之志，爲晉吏部尚書、大司農。

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Record of Ji Province states: Zan's son Hong, courtesy name Liangbo, was pure and scrupulous with a will not to turn his person; he became director of the ministry of personnel and grand minister of agriculture of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo's Record of Ji Province says Zan's son Hong, styled Liangbo, was pure and scrupulous with unbending integrity, and became Jin's director of the ministry of personnel and grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 評曰：夏侯、曹氏，世爲婚姻，故惇、淵、仁、洪、休、尚、真等並以親舊肺腑，貴重於時，左右勳業，咸有効勞。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: The Xiahous and the house of Cao for generations have been marriage kin; therefore Dun, Yuan, Ren, Hong, Xiu, Shang, Zhen, and others all by intimate old ties of flesh and blood were honored weightily in the age, attended on the left and right in merit and enterprise, and all had effect in service.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The Xiahous and Caos had intermarried for generations, so Dun, Yuan, Ren, Hong, Xiu, Shang, Zhen, and the rest rose as kinsmen at court, basked in unique favor, and gave solid service on campaign and in council.

sentences.zh: 爽德薄位尊，沈溺盈溢，此固大易所著，道家所忌也。

translations.literal: Shuang’s virtue was thin yet his position honored, sinking and drowning in overflow—this is indeed what the great Changes writes of, what the Daoist school taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang’s virtue was slight while his power was vast; he drowned in excess—the very fault the Yijing warns against and Daoist teachers curse.

sentences.zh: 「玄以規格局度，世稱其名，然與曹爽中外繾綣；

translations.literal: "Xuan by regulation pattern and capacity measure was praised in the age by his name, yet with Cao Shuang inner and outer were intertwined;
translations.idiomatic: "Xiahou Xuan won fame for scope and style, yet he was bound tight to Cao Shuang inside and out;

sentences.zh: 榮位如斯，曾未聞匡弼其非，援致良才。

translations.literal: with glory and position like this, never once did one hear of him correcting Shuang's errors or drawing in good talent.
translations.idiomatic: with rank and glory such as his, he never once rebuked Shuang's misrule or brought worthy men to his aid.

sentences.zh: 舉茲以論，焉能免之乎！」

translations.literal: Raising this to discuss, how can one be spared!"
translations.idiomatic: Judged by that, how could he hope to escape ruin?"
